This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Explosions heard near Qeshm: Two explosions were on Qeshm Island on Thursday, Iran's Tasnim News Agency reported, and were reportedly caused by Iranian forces engaging with "hostile enemy targets" near the entry to the Strait of Hormuz. Iran deal on Hormuz with Oman nears: Hassan Ghashghavi, a spokesperson for the National Security Commission and an MP, said on Friday that a "framework of understanding" with Oman regarding the Strait had been agreed upon. "The general framework of the understanding with Oman has been determined, and the final text and details will be announced soon," Ghashghavi told the official IRNA news agency, noting that the "final decision" would be made at "higher levels." A senior Iranian official told Drop Site's Jeremy Scahill that Iran and Oman have finalized technical talks and agreed on temporary rules for the "security, supervisory, and economic management" of the Strait of Hormuz, following several rounds of negotiations. The official said Iran's implementation of the agreement remains conditional on the "full and tangible return" of the United States to the temporary ceasefire understanding, stressing that merely suspending the naval blockade would not be sufficient. Iran parliament speaker slams Trump 's "theater diplomacy": Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad and lead negotiator Mohamed Bagher Ghalibaf criticized President Donald Trump's repeated shifts between threatening a major attack on Iran and announcing negotiations, calling it "theater diplomacy on loop." Ghalibaf said, in a on X, that using "bullying + broken promises + fake news as leverage" was a failed strategy and urged Washington to "acknowledge the facts and fulfill your commitments," adding: "We don't need more theater." Tehran sent Gulf countries list of power plants that it could strike if U.S. attacked its infrastructure, report says: Iran Gulf mediators a detailed list of power plants and desalination facilities it could strike if the U.S. attacked Iranian energy infrastructure earlier this week, the AFP reported on Thursday, threatening to "black out the Gulf, country by country" in response to Washington's potential attacks. Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the UAE subsequently urged Trump not to launch the planned strikes, according to the agency. Trump says Iran war "going very well," to end "pretty soon": In a post on Truth Social on Thursday, Trump claimed that the war on Iran was going "very well," adding that the country was "decimated." He also said he was "extremely happy" with War Secretary Pete Hegseth, who he reportedly confronted during a Cabinet meeting last week about low munitions supplies. "Everything has been extraordinary." While taking questions in the Oval Office from reporters, U.S. President Donald Trump said that the war on Iran would end "pretty soon," speculating that the Iranian government could not "go much longer." Trump also that the Strait of Hormuz remained "sort of open" right now, despite acknowledging the previous day that Iran maintained its ability to threaten shipping through the waterway with its naval power. Pezeshkian discusses effects of war, leadership of country: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said in an interview with Iran's IRNA news service that attacks on the country's power infrastructure caused "a daily shortage of approximately 230 million cubic metres of gas," and that the U.S. exerted "maximum pressure" on Iran, "expecting the country to collapse." He also his relationship with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, saying that communication with Khamenei, who has not appeared publicly since his appointment in March, is currently "very difficult," but calling him a "major asset" in allowing Iran to continue its successful defense of the country. Mossad fires two senior officials over Iran war failure: Israel's Mossad chief, Roman Gofman, fired two of the spy agency's top officials over a failed plan to topple Iran's government, Israel's Channel 12 and Haaretz reported on Thursday. One of the officials had served as the head of Mossad's intelligence directorate since September, and the other was the head of the agency's Iran division. The two drafted the written plan to remove Iran's leadership by mobilizing the country's minority groups to rebel and whip up mass protests to oust the government. White House tells Emiratis to silence Iran war critic: The White House has reportedly the government of the United Arab Emirates to "shut down" Amjad Taha, a political strategist and journalist with ties to the government and a staunch advocate of Israel and the Abraham Accords, whose criticism of the U.S.'s war in Iran has "irked" Trump and his allies, according to a report from the Washington Times on Thursday. Traffic through Hormuz drops sharply: Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz dropped to 33 vessels between Monday and Thursday, down from 50 the previous week, according to data published by the maritime tracking firm Kpler on Friday. Citing data from ship-tracking company Kpler, Reuters said that only four vessels transited the strait on Thursday, including the very large crude carrier Nissos Kea, which was carrying about two million barrels of crude oil from Iraq. Several Chinese and Indian refiners have unsuccessfully sought vessels this week to enter the Strait and load crude at Iraq's Basrah Oil Terminal, following steep discounts offered by Iraq's state oil marketer. Yemen Ansarallah clashes with Saudi-backed government in Marib and Hadramout: Saudi-backed Yemeni forces reported that Ansarallah missile and drone attacks on the Yemeni provinces of Marib and Hadramout on Thursday killed at least 18 of its soldiers, with other reports putting the death toll as high as 58. The health minister of the Saudi-backed government later announced that a second round of attacks on Friday had killed two civilians and wounded 14 others. An Ansarallah political bureau member described Thursday's operations as a "preemptive" response to alleged plans by Saudi forces to attack Sana'a. Ansarallah's Supreme Political Council claimed Saudi Arabia had been preparing a ground invasion to create internal chaos and prevent an end to the country's "12-year siege," according to Tasnim. The Saudi-backed government said that its army had shot down multiple Ansarallah drones launched towards Marib on Friday, with several explosions reported. In the southwestern Saudi city of Najran, the Saudi-led coalition said projectiles launched by Ansarallah wounded 11 civilians, seven of whom were Saudi nationals and one of whom was a 4-year-old child. Traffic increases through Bab Al-Mandab: 26 vessels transited the Bab Al-Mandab Strait on Thursday, up from 19 the previous day, according to Kpler data. Palestine UNICEF reports one Palestinian child killed every day in Gaza since "ceasefire": "At least 300 children have been killed in Gaza in the 300 days since a 'ceasefire' went into effect on October 10, 2025, UNICEF said in a on Thursday. "A ceasefire that leaves an average of one child dead each and every day is failing children," UNICEF's Regional Director for the Middle East and North Africa, Edouard Beigbeder, said. "With hundreds more children injured, many severely, children in Gaza are still waiting for the end to the violence they were promised." Israeli forces withdraw from Qalandia as attacks continue across occupied West Bank: Qalandia: Israeli forces from Qalandia refugee camp and Kafr Aqab in Jerusalem late Thursday after a two-day military raid that left 51 Palestinians injured and more than 60 detained or subjected to field interrogation, including women and children, according to the Jerusalem Governorate. Israeli troops also demolished seven shops and a car wash, damaged dozens of homes and businesses, and converted homes into military posts. Families also reported money and gold jewelry stolen during raids. Jenin: Israeli forces two Palestinians in Jenin on Thursday, including a 14-year-old, who soldiers shot in the lower back, according to WAFA. The Israeli military off a roundabout, detained a group of young Palestinian men, and raided multiple shops. The military also a series of new orders targeting land in several towns in Jenin on Thursday, including orders to uproot trees and seize more land in the town of Marka. Ramallah: Israeli settlers a Bedouin community near the town of Taybeh on Thursday, injuring three people from a single family, one international activist, and arresting a Palestinian, WAFA reported. In another attack on Thursday evening, Israeli forces and fired stun grenades at an 80-year-old Palestinian-American man near Turmus Ayya. He sustained cuts and bruises from the attack. Sen. Chris Van Hollen on Thursday that U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee resign, pointing to the attack, following reporting from Zeteo that the man who was attacked is an American citizen. Tubas: Israeli forces the city of Tamman, near Tubas, early Friday morning, raiding the town and ransacking a house, according to WAFA. On Thursday, Israeli forces the body of a 28-year-old Palestinian who had been shot in Tubas in April, and whose body had been withheld from his family since. Drop Site 's Mohamed Awad interviewed residents from Tuba in Masafer Yatta, who were attacked by Israeli settlers on Wednesday. "They smashed and burned everything," one resident said, describing the attack that wounded five Palestinians, including a child whose nose was broken, and burned at least four homes.. "They left nothing untouched." Watch Mohamed 's video dispatches and . Hamas urges mediators to prevent Israel from derailing Gaza agreement: Hamas called on mediators and the U.S. administration on Thursday, asking them to intervene to prevent Israel from derailing the Gaza agreement, saying continued Israeli violations threaten implementation of its second phase. The movement said Palestinian factions have engaged "positively and responsibly" with efforts to complete the agreement and presented their position on the roadmap "in a national spirit" that clears the way for implementing Phase 2. Number of Palestinian children held in Israeli prisons without charge sharply rises: At least 191 Palestinian children are being in "administrative detention" in Israeli prisons in March 2026, according to data from the organization Parents Against Child Detention, up from 103 in January of 2025, the Times of Israel reported on Friday.. Palestinians in administrative detention can be held indefinitely and without trial, are not informed of the allegations against them, and evidence presented against them in court is routinely classified and withheld from the accused and their attorneys. Lebanon Lebanese soldier wounded, water station set ablaze in Israeli attacks on southern Lebanon: Israeli forces carried out a series of attacks across southern Lebanon on Friday, continuing near-daily violations despite the U.S.-backed ceasefire. An Israeli drone an airstrike on Al-Mansouri, south of Tyre (Sour) district, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. A Lebanese soldier was when an Israeli attack targeted an army bulldozer in Al-Mansouri while it was clearing roads and removing rubble, according to the Lebanese Army. Israeli artillery Meiss Al-Jabal, in Marjayoun district, while Israeli forces simultaneously fired machine guns toward the town, NNA reported. Israeli forces Friday to the Shaqra water station in the Bint Jbeil district. U.S. says Hezbollah did not violate ceasefire in Majdal Zoun: Washington Israel that Hezbollah did not violate the ceasefire in Thursday's incident in Majdal Zoun, in which an IED explosion killed two Israeli soldiers and wounded several others, an Israeli security source told Israel's public broadcaster, as reported by Al Jazeera. Israeli assessments also that the explosive device in Majdal Zoun was planted before the ceasefire took effect, according to the broadcaster. The comments come as U.S. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott Sky News Arabia the Rome talks between Lebanon and Israel were "effective and positive," saying progress was made on several technical issues. U.S. News Trump issues more executive orders attempting to rewrite birthright citizenship law : President Donald Trump two executive orders Thursday seeking to deny birthright citizenship to children born to certain foreign diplomatic staff, alleged "alien enemies" including those tied to designated terrorist groups, mothers who deceptively enter the U.S. for commercial "birth tourism," and, contingent on future congressional action, people born in U.S. territories such as Puerto Rico, according to Axios. A second order directs the secretaries of state and homeland security to issue rules targeting the "birth tourism" industry both domestically and abroad. The move marks Trump's second attempt to curb birthright citizenship after the Supreme Court struck down his broader executive order on June 30. Legal experts expect the new orders to face 14th Amendment challenges. U.S. economy shed 23,000 jobs in July: The U.S. economy a seasonally adjusted 23,000 jobs in July, according to a Bureau of Labor Statistics report released Friday. The figure is well below the Dow Jones consensus forecast, which had anticipated a gain of 83,000. The unemployment rate slipped to 4.1%, while the labor force participation fell to 61.4%, its lowest level in more than five years. Trump says he 'll keep Blanche as acting AG if confirmation fails: President Donald Trump he would keep Todd Blanche as acting attorney general if his Senate confirmation fails, telling Punchbowl News, "We'll try it again," as Blanche's path narrowed following Alaska Sen. Lisa Murkowski 's decision to join Maine Sen. Susan Collins in opposing him. Murkowski cited the Justice Department's handling of Jeffrey Epstein -related files, sweeping immunity promised to Trump and his family, and statements to anti-abortion groups as reasons for her opposition, saying, "I simply do not have confidence" Blanche would check "the worst impulses of this administration." ICE will only release body camera footage when in "agency's best interests": Immigration and Customs Enforcement, which plans to equip all field officers with body cameras by the end of September, has a policy that allows release of footage from shootings or serious confrontations only when the agency's director determines it is "in the best interests of the agency," according to an Associated Press investigation. ICE officers shot two men in Houston and Maine last month, and neither incident was recorded, despite the $20 million Congress previously allocated to ICE for body camera equipment in an April spending bill. ICE spent $30.9 million in July purchasing camera equipment from Axon, one day after the killing in Maine. DNC autopsy author says Gaza war hurt Harris: Paul Rivera , author of the Democratic National Committee's 2024 election autopsy, to Axios that he concluded the Gaza war hurt Kamala Harris politically, particularly costing her votes in Michigan communities with large Arab American populations such as Dearborn. Rivera said he privately shared the assessment with a pro-Palestinian group, the IMEU project, but did not include it in the autopsy's final draft. University of Minnesota to pay pro-Palestine professor after nixing job offer: The University of Minnesota will Israeli-American Holocaust scholar Raz Segal $250,000 after withdrawing an offer to lead its Center for Holocaust and Genocide Studies following backlash over his description of Israel's assault on Gaza as "a textbook case of genocide," the Guardian reported on Thursday. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan sign defense deal: Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan a trilateral defense agreement in Saudi Arabia on Friday, aiming to "promote peace, security, and stability in the region and beyond," according to a statement announcing the deal from Pakistan's Foreign Ministry. The agreement "stipulates that any armed attack against any one of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all," according to the FM statement. A Turkish official told the NYT that the deal only covered mutual defense, and is "not directed against any other country." U.S. intelligence claims Russia could test NATO with limited attack: New U.S. intelligence assessments reportedly that Russian President Vladimir Putin could attempt to fracture NATO by launching a calibrated attack on an allied country between this fall and 2029. Possible scenarios in the assessments range from a cyberattack or deployment of unmarked armed groups to a limited incursion along NATO's eastern flank, with a full land assault the least likely scenario. The assessment comes amid increasing incidents in which Russian missiles and drones have struck or flown over NATO countries in what U.S. and European officials have described as probes of NATO's willingness to respond. Bombing near Damascus wounds 14 : An explosive device planted on a minibus 14 people Thursday night in Jaramana, a predominantly Druze suburb of Damascus, according to Syrian officials. Authorities initially reported two fatalities after finding what appeared to be body parts at the scene, but the Health Ministry later said they belonged to people who had been severely wounded. Some of the victims remain in serious condition, including the minibus driver. Authorities have not attributed responsibility for the bombing. Jaramana has experienced clashes between Druze residents and Islamist militants aligned with Syria's new authorities since the 2024 overthrow of Bashar al-Assad. Former Guerrero governor arrested for evidence destruction in missing students case: Angel Aguirre, a former governor of Mexico's southern Guerrero state, was on charges of obstruction of justice and forced disappearance for allegedly ordering the destruction of evidence that could have shed light on the whereabouts of 43 students who disappeared in 2014, Mexican Attorney General Ernestina Godoy announced Thursday. Godoy said new testimony from two witnesses helped establish that Aguirre may have ordered the destruction of security camera footage during a meeting with senior officials the night of the students' disappearance. International probes have determined the students, who were on their way to a protest in Mexico City, were killed by organized crime members working with police. Pakistan expands press restrictions to cover Pakistani nationals working for foreign media: Pakistan new restrictions on journalists on Sunday, imposing routine movement controls on Pakistani nationals working for foreign media outlets for the first time. Journalists now require government permission to travel and report outside Islamabad, Lahore, and Karachi. The guidelines, whose motivation officials have not explained, come amid protests over recent multi-round elections in Pakistan-administered Kashmir and widening insurgencies in the country's western provinces. The country also ordered foreign outlets without reporting permits to immediately leave Pakistan-administered Kashmir. on Monday. Human Rights Watch called the curbs "an alarming step" in Pakistan's "narrowing space for press freedom." Uganda 's parliament approves potential military deployment to Gaza: Uganda's parliament Thursday to approve deploying its military to the Gaza Strip if needed as part of a proposed multinational security force under President Donald Trump's ceasefire plan, Reuters reported. Defense Minister Kiryowa Kiwanuka told lawmakers before the vote that Trump had contacted Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni through emissaries in July seeking Kampala's participation. The move marks the first public acknowledgment by Uganda, which has peacekeeping contingents in Somalia, South Sudan, and the Democratic Republic of Congo, that it might join the International Stabilization Force envisioned under Trump's plan. Attack on former Bangladesh cricketer Shakib Al Hasan 's home follows his appearance alongside Hasina: A group and set fire to former Bangladesh cricket captain Shakib Al Hasan's ancestral home in Magura town Wednesday, hours after he joined ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's first public media event since her 2024 removal, Al Jazeera reported. During the virtual event, held on the second anniversary of her ouster, Hasina, who has been sentenced to death in absentia by Bangladesh's war crimes tribunal, said she would return to the country in December despite the risk of imprisonment or death. Shakib, a former Awami League lawmaker who has remained abroad since the uprising that toppled Hasina's government, faces multiple investigations over allegations of murder and money laundering. Rubio announces new sanctions on Cuba: Secretary of State Marco Rubio new sanctions on Thursday against five Cuban companies and eight individuals, including Defense Minister Alvaro Lopez Miera and Chief of the General Staff Roberto Legra Sotolongo. The sanctions target firms including Tecnoimport, which the State Department says imports Russian and Chinese military equipment for Cuba's armed forces, and Union de Industria Militar, a weapons manufacturer. Iraqi resistance leader urges pause to operations against Saudi Arabia: Hadi al-Amiri, head of the Iraqi Badr Organization, part of the Popular Mobilisation Forces (PMF), urged Iraqi resistance groups on Friday to postpone retaliatory operations against Saudi Arabia in a video address carried by Iraqi media. He called groups to overlook "American-Saudi" aggression for the "sake of Iraq's highest interest." The U.S. and Saudi Arabia attacked the PMF headquarters in Iraq on July 29, killing more than 20 people and wounding at least 30 others. Pro-Palestine protester acquitted in UK court: Paula Akpan, one of the 10 British pro-Palestine protesters charged with criminal damage for spraying red paint across the entrances of Scotiabank in June 2024, was found not guilty in court on Thursday. It didn't go the way he planned.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136807762/638668092/1328794144?refcode=ea.43d066c0-7592-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ms=ea.43d066c0-7592-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjQzZDA2NmMwLTc1OTItZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMGQzYTExZmEzMCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=4nokHF6gmPlqrTH65o1J2Rgq38a4zBdSKwxi8_rlZeE=&emci=f6fba774-cc91-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=43d066c0-7592-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=4823105)
---
Friends, a free press only means something if it's free to make those in power uncomfortable. Trump proved once again that he doesn't believe in that kind of freedom, but this time, our courts reminded him there are still limits to his power. | **U.S. Withdraws Subpoenas Issued to New York Times Journalists** _\- The New York Times, July 23, 2026_
---
Federal agents showed up at the homes of New York Times reporters with subpoenas demanding their phone records and testimony. Their offense was reporting on the security risks of the Qatari jet Trump's been flying around as his new Air Force One.
Reporting the truth turned into a punishable offense, simply because the truth embarrassed Trump.
When the case landed in front of a judge who actually asked hard questions, the Trump administration’s justification fell apart fast, and they withdrew the subpoenas rather than defend them in court.
**But the Justice Department says this investigation isn't over, and I believe them. Losing this round won't stop Trump from testing the next limit, and the next, until something actually holds.**
When those in power come after journalists, books, and our cultural institutions, they're testing how far they can push before people notice, and the same playbook gets used next on scientists, on activists, on anyone else telling an inconvenient truth.
Well, we see what’s happening plain as day.
**I've protested outside the halls of power. I've marched alongside people who refused to stay quiet. I relaunched my father’s Committee for the First Amendment because I recognized exactly what this administration was doing.**
And through JanePAC, I'm doing what I know how to do best: _helping elect leaders with the backbone to defend our rights and freedoms._
But it takes all of us staying united, because that unity is the one thing Trump has never been able to break.
✊ In solidarity,
Jane

Offering up to $100 million for information that leads to their arrests, the DoJ said the following members are responsible for extreme violence in Mexico and tons of deadly drugs being sold within the U.S.:
* Juan Carlos Valencia Gonzalez also known as "Pelon"
* Audias Flores Silva also known as "Jardinero"
* Julio Cesar Montero Pinzon also known as "Tarjetas"
* Carlos Andres Rivera Varela also known as "La Firma"
* Hugo Gonzalo Mendoza Gaytan also known as "Sapo"
* Ricardo Ruiz Velasco also known as "RR" / "Tripa"
* Julio Alberto Castillo Rodriguez also known as "Chorro"
* Griselda Margarita Arredondo Pinzon

"The American people gave us a mandate to keep this country safe, and we will not rest until it is fulfilled," Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche explained. "Today's unsealing of criminal charges against five high-ranking CJNG leaders marks another decisive step in our campaign to dismantle the cartels that have plagued this country for far too long...this administration will use every tool at its disposal to bring these defendants to justice - no matter where they hide."
CJNG has been in a period of transition since the Mexican operation in February that resulted in the death of Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes, a.k.a El Mencho. It has since been reported, his stepson, Valencia Gonzalez, is now leading the cartel. What makes Valencia Gonzalez unique compared to other cartel leaders is that he has U.S. citizenship after being born in California.
Both of Valencia Gonzalez's parents were cartel operatives.

Before I ask you to [**split a contribution between our grassroots General Election Fund and John Hickenlooper**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136808141/638669593/-12753500?refcode=email_080726_weiser&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkZTE3ZTVmZi03NjkyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=bgoYSHsXH38t5GZ87VfzyCfVDjDYRGKMuDxj88Qzs9g=), I want to reintroduce myself and explain why I hope to earn your support. I came to Colorado over 30 years ago for a job interview, and that decision changed my life forever. It was here that my wife, Heidi, and I raised our two wonderful kids — three, if you count our mostly-well-behaved dog, Zeke. I’ve dedicated my life to public service. And, as the son and grandson of Holocaust survivors, I’m committed to our shared American values of liberty, justice, and the idea that all people should live free from discrimination, hatred, and oppression. My first job after law school was here in Colorado, and it launched my career that included clerking for Supreme Court Justice Ruth Bader Ginsberg, working for President Obama, and serving as the Dean of the University of Colorado Law School. From that first job to now, I have always believed that Colorado is the best place to live and the ideal place to raise a family. I love this state. And when you love something, you fight for it. **My commitment to fight for Colorado is why I don’t get it when others try to appease and give in to bullies like the President and his cabinet. It does not work, and it’s not what leaders do. Not now, not ever. We must take a stand, not be afraid, and not back down.** I know fighting for what’s right isn’t easy. Fights worth having rarely are. As the People’s Lawyer, I’ve had a lot of practice in these fights. It’s been my job to enforce the rule of law, and no one is above it: not deceitful corporations, not abusive employers, and definitely not the federal government. In fact, as part of upholding the rule of law, I’ve taken the Trump administration to court 75 times (and counting) — and we’re winning again and again. **I’m proud of the reputation I’ve built here in Colorado********.** I’m not here to do “politics as usual”. I’m here to fight for you, not the powerful or wealthy few. And I am always going to show up, listen, and deliver for all of Colorado. [**I refuse to let billionaire money cloud our agenda of freedom, affordability, and opportunity. clean_body: = Hi there, Phil here — Colorado’s Attorney General, and your official Democratic nominee for Colorado’s next governor. Before I ask you to =, I want to reintroduce myself and explain why I hope to earn your support. I came to Colorado over 30 years ago for a job interview, and that decision changed my life forever. It was here that my wife, Heidi, and I raised our two wonderful kids — three, if you count our mostly-well-behaved dog, Zeke. I’ve dedicated my life to public service. And, as the son and grandson of Holocaust survivors, I’m committed to our shared American values of liberty, justice, and the idea that all people should live free from discrimination, hatred, and oppression. My first job after law school was here in Colorado, and it launched my career that included clerking for Supreme Court Justice Ruth Bader Ginsberg, working for President Obama, and serving as the Dean of the University of Colorado Law School. From that first job to now, I have always believed that Colorado is the best place to live and the ideal place to raise a family. I love this state. And when you love something, you fight for it. My commitment to fight for Colorado is why I don’t get it when others try to appease and give in to bullies like the President and his cabinet. It does not work, and it’s not what leaders do. Not now, not ever. We must take a stand, not be afraid, and not back down. I know fighting for what’s right isn’t easy. Fights worth having rarely are. As the People’s Lawyer, I’ve had a lot of practice in these fights. It’s been my job to enforce the rule of law, and no one is above it: not deceitful corporations, not abusive employers, and definitely not the federal government. In fact, as part of upholding the rule of law, I’ve taken the Trump administration to court 75 times (and counting) — and we’re winning again and again. I’m proud of the reputation I’ve built here in Colorado****. I’m not here to do “politics as usual”. I’m here to fight for you, not the powerful or wealthy few. subject: This pin reminds me why I’m in this fight

body:
I’m giving this Senate race everything I’ve got – but the only way I can win is with your grassroots support.
Peter, at the end of this message, I’m going to ask you to split $10 between my Senate campaign in Ohio and Heartland Patriots. But before I do, let me tell you why I’m running and why I need your support to win.**
When I first came to the Senate, they gave me an official Senate pin – the kind that says, “Look at me; look how important I am.” I wore it for a couple of days, but it just didn’t feel right.
**So I replaced it with a pin depicting a canary in a birdcage, which a Lorain steelworker gave to me decades ago at a Workers' Memorial Day rally.**
[](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/107129?refcode=em20260807-10768&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=10768%2E614464%2EcIQlEq)
As the story goes, coal miners once brought canaries down into the mines with them as a warning system against poisonous gases. Back then, they didn’t have a union strong enough to fight for them or a government that cared enough to protect them. They were on their own.
But together, we changed that. We passed worker safety laws and overtime pay. We banned child labor. We passed clean air and safe drinking water laws. We enacted Social Security and Medicare, workers’ rights, women’s rights, and civil rights.
Because when you love this country, you fight for the people who make it work.
**But Republican Jon Husted has shown he isn’t willing to keep up this fight for Ohioans. He’s put his billionaires donors before working people, and enough is enough.**
I’ve never forgotten what my canary pin means, and I’m giving this Senate race everything I’ve got. But the only way I can win is with your support.
**[I’m personally asking you, Peter: Will you split $10 or more between me and Heartland Patriots today to help me flip Ohio’s must-win seat, retake the Senate, and continue making progress for workers?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/107129?refcode=em20260807-10768&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=10768%2E614464%2EcIQlEq)**
**[DONATE](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/107129?refcode=em20260807-10768&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=10768%2E614464%2EcIQlEq)**
In solidarity,
Sherrod

| | | Friend, Thank you for your strong support in July. We want to be honest with you about what July looked like from our perspective. Sabato's Crystal Ball moved 14 races toward Democrats in a single update, but Texas Senate stayed put. Polling continues to show this race is neck and neck. One Silicon Valley billionaire wrote a $10 million check to James Talarico's super PAC. Democrats raised over $1.1 billion nationally in the first six months of this year alone. Everything was moving in the wrong direction. _And then the conservative grassroots did what conservatives do._ **You showed up. **You gave. You proved that this race is not going to be decided by billionaire checkbooks and coastal money. July was the strongest grassroots fundraising month of this entire campaign, and it happened in the middle of the worst national environment Republicans have faced in years. That is not a small thing. That is the difference between a campaign that can compete on television through November and one that cannot. **If you were able to give,_THANK YOU_. If you weren't able, we hope you will [consider donating in the future.](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=dae8a349668e47859e6d2b06ed08e476&_e=eTkIGsT2hPXIR7oB7p8bGANsaLpzd-w_1hLkgR8gUUsXp8Xy0w9oBMfeDpsMpnclRUl4mXBREe_2zWkheWtc2iOQMNjDKfrELtp_tXnSCGWN1A7MBAjeFwmQBXEwTUxXa2AOqYYFx9AYhwgxUEj16PBP9N9Hh-3heqXmpirYywCVpSiPolX9zjkpatYmZ5Y9mEbWqDL0xEoScVvgprwApZQyIGcGZmyAUHTdUh96lajMT8BbDLnutUnAcyJCIY7pFS_HuE7cEnG8w1oydzD07nquuaisUaqIwagPCs3tyaNVli2ODZbLU0eSzBfHCPd3H1ctdhJsuMioU1g8uuaJRu0Nikq0RKHciQEIKMNHYHnpoqZslQbgygpN6zk6MQyuJ6NkdBoA9QOZJ-8uWGaayhM60Q_QMReKd6HVlJSylGt2Gcd443QR0Lk1qRxJsKc0kFQhX4L1o84tCY_cfmmrzcRGp5PZq9e70vSyzt5RgpoMFQegc5C9QtJQv0RZmahi5ljr8HRVJ3grs1DSwc7GGEFNBhA7ypqyyklq23gWTKNJm4rqGwk2XDtKeTT3k_BpTy47CPJv7FPk-aVyhZG2WO6lAdnf630oQ-qUGjf2K8nnMRaQ5EE6c9Hp2YQg93E8Y6JlayhOIVa66KwfyXjBzbahDqVnItPWVg7BEbsVqY7bZkD3lmoVDBKCTVPela7xeLMkcwhLwMwD9P6KEfXgCU2PvaJQ3yhPcUGIT8hVE2xO2zmOLCN9_yPwGFFrnXBYC9baIJ6kmYDN2-wdFZNEKiOb5i-aQ8bDXn6aDtVwRMthQFUcpbQa_08737d62asyi7WPo3o0gZmyz4KhlbM0TS-qmvGtYyHtolJuu455mREQWAbX6igy674EK8oYPRphO2Vm-ok89Cujc13dLC2Qfl4GQCKJA23M9ZM_41Y33mtGsvbgULcDRLpfVw3C7bbJ)** While July was great, we cannot stop here. You sent me there to fight for Southwest Washington—even when it's unpopular. To stand up for our timber communities. To protect the right to repair. To support local manufacturers and small businesses. To put this district ahead of any political party.
Now they're sending the Speaker of the House into our backyard because they think this seat belongs to them.
It doesn't.
It belongs to the people who live here.
Today, we have an opportunity to send Mike Johnson, John Braun, and every DC insider a message they won't forget:
Southwest Washington isn't for sale.
We won't be bullied.

This week, we officially launched our general election campaign to flip Virginia’s Fifth, and I wanted to make sure you saw one of the first videos we put out.
This video is about trust, but it’s also about our path to winning this race. [https://youtu.be/X7S4TZRtytw?si=7nlgE1Sl1UKlvhoU]
We know there are voters across this district who are frustrated with politics. Our job over the next three months is to show them that Tom is different, not just because of what he says, but because of what he’s already done.
When healthcare was on the line, Tom cast the deciding vote to protect it, knowing it would cost him his seat in Congress. He’s taken on powerful corporate interests, stood up to his own party when he thought they were wrong, and made the tough choice even when it wasn't a politically easy one.
That’s the story this video tells. And it’s the case we’re going to make across the fifth district: You may not agree with Tom on everything, but you can trust him to fight for you.
Watch the video here: https://youtu.be/X7S4TZRtytw?si=7nlgE1Sl1UKlvhoU [https://youtu.be/X7S4TZRtytw?si=7nlgE1Sl1UKlvhoU]
Now we need your help getting out there. This district is going to be won person by person. So head to your social media channels, share the video, post it, and send it directly to a friend or family member who needs to see it.
That’s how we are going to win this race: expanding the coalition, earning people’s trust, and giving voters a reason to choose Tom.
Thanks for being part of this,
Team Tom

Did you know we don’t have to wait until 2028 to stop Trump? That’s right. There are three big ways we can put a strong check on his administration. Here's my plan:
1. If Democrats win back our majorities in November, we will be able to stop these spineless Republicans from enabling the president to do whatever he wants.
2. Once we have that power, we can block any far-right, extremist judge that Trump nominates to the Supreme Court.
3. And we can use our power in Congress to make Trump and his cronies follow the law and pass our plans to make our government work for working people.

This is our chance to actually put a stop to Trump as soon as possible — and I’m not taking this chance for granted. **So I have an announcement to share: Our campaign has now contributed over $1 million to support state parties in 2026.** [**I have to ask: If you’re able, will you please pitch in $28 or anything you can to help support this project and guarantee Democrats beat MAGA Republicans in the midterms?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3737?amount=28&t=8&akid=2983%2E4032634%2EwqA9hX)

Renewed sense of possibilities

| | | [ ](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=MtBLw57MCBnd28lIl741uxhE24SlqUGA-DgV4-cYEvs&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=2026_august_newsletter&n=1)
---
---
## **A Movement, Not a Mob**
On July 18, Forward Party members and allies gathered in King of Prussia to spend their Saturday discussing local government, election reform, and a kind of politics not centered around conflict. As featured speaker Chris Gambino put it: _"We are creating a movement, not a mob. . . . Mobs lead with anger and violence. Movements lead with purpose and solutions."_ Many of the attendees spent months planning the event and years building relationships with others in room. We heard from speakers who have stepped into (often thankless) jobs to serve their communities. Our objective is huge, but on days like this one, it all seems possible. Thanks so much to those of you who made the convention a success!
---
| [](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=MtBLw57MCBnd28lIl741u2f82VcN49yJ3Wou-X6QZ0jZ5Ang5aVBoHWH8fyeg-pIBTEJ2gF5S1tOXNsoSLARMQ&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=2026_august_newsletter&n=2 "Read a Convention Recap \(One Attendee's Perspective\)") [Read a Convention Recap (One Attendee's Perspective)](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=MtBLw57MCBnd28lIl741u2f82VcN49yJ3Wou-X6QZ0jZ5Ang5aVBoHWH8fyeg-pIBTEJ2gF5S1tOXNsoSLARMQ&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=2026_august_newsletter&n=2)

Coming out of the convention, there is a renewed sense of the serious challenges facing us and the opportunity we have to get this right. Our party has been building a foundation for the last four years; now it's time to push to the next level. We want to hold more events and get our message out to a wider audience. We want to define our goals clearly to that audience. We want to find new ways to support the candidates who affiliate with us and recruit more great candidates in the future. If you want to help, this is the time to get involved.

name: Kirk Cameron
subject: The antidote to Drag Queen Story Hour
body:
| [View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6568691/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvR05wcFFQdVJ5Rg/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA4MDc/LbmNsZXpCUzh4Zw/qP2hpZHM9bmNNbHJTMEx2VWxLcGdscw/ganYH7w/s3v6ef002f5)
| | | If you haven’t heard about the “See You at the Library Day” on Fox News or Newsmax or your other favorite news sources, please let me tell you why it’s so critical.
---
| | Fellow Conservative, If you haven’t heard about “See You at the Library Day” on Fox News or Newsmax or your other favorite news sources, _**[please let me tell you why it’s so critical.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**_ Back when you were growing up, you may remember lazy Saturdays at the library with a kind but stern librarian. She would fill your mind with classics like _Pat the Bunny_ and _The Little Engine That Could_. And eventually you got old enough to roam by yourself and discover adventures like the _Three Musketeers_ , _Treasure Island_ and _Charlotte’s Web_. But today, all that has changed. Instead of filling children with wholesome stories, the president of the American Library Association (ALA) says libraries should be used to address ‘systemic racism’ and elevate ‘BIPOC and GLBTQR+ writers and voices.’ Radical librarians call _Adventures of Huckleberry Finn_ and _To Kill a Mockingbird_ “racist.” They’ve stripped Laura Ingalls Wilder’s name from a prestigious book award because of her “problematic’ _Little House_ series. And they bring in men wearing full makeup, dresses, and high heels for “Drag Queen Story Hours” where books like these are read to children of all ages... _A is for Activist._ An _ABC_ _board_ _book_ for “families who want their kids to grow up in a space that is unapologetic about activism, environmental justice, civil rights, LGBTQ rights, and everything else that activists believe in and fight for.” _Woke Baby_. “For all the littlest progressives, waking up to seize a new day of justice and activism. Woke babies raise their fists in the air. Woke babies cry out for justice. Woke babies grow up to change the world.” _Prince and Knight._ The “premier queer-friendly fairy tale” about a prince who marries a knight instead of a princess. And _The Hips on the Drag Queens Go Swish, Swish, Swish._ A “family-friendly celebration of drag” that encourages children to “work it.” I wish I could tell you this was only happening in places like New York City and San Francisco...
---
| | [ ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
| | ...but that’s just not true. <\- THIS IS A MAN leading “Drag Queen Story Hour.”
---
| | _**[That’s why parents and grandparents across the country are rising up through See You At The Library Day.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**_ For decades, the ultra-liberal Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation and George Soros’ Open Society have spent millions radicalizing the ALA. And as a result, a new generation of pink-haired, activist librarians have made it their mission to fill library shelves with anti-American, LGBTQ-friendly, and explicitly sexual content. Maybe you’ve noticed all the displays at your own library celebrating Pride Month or elevating ‘the environment’ to a type of religion. Or maybe you’ve noticed the “Teen Zone” which is really meant to be a “parent-free” zone. The “Teen Zone” is filled with books like: _Rick_ about a cross-dressing Grandpa, _Melissa_ filled with graphic nudity, and _Darkstalker_ featuring gory violence and domestic abuse. But here’s what’s really alarming. We can’t just sit back and say, “Well, I’ll just make sure my family doesn’t go to “Drag Queen Story Hour” and we won’t check out those inappropriate books.” That may be good for your family -- for now. But meanwhile, the ALA uses our taxpayer-funded libraries to lure in millions of _other_ children who grow up to be the very activists who are destroying our country and conservative values! _**[I hope you see why I need your help today.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.) **_ My name is Kirk Cameron. Maybe you recognize me from the 1980’s family sitcom “Growing Pains” or from my work in inspirational movies like “Fireproof” and “Left Behind.” I know firsthand how dangerous it is to be indoctrinated by leftist values. Pride almost took me down as a young actor in Hollywood. But the gospel saved me. I love being an actor, but what’s far more important is being a husband, dad, grandad, and a Christian. When I saw what book publishers and libraries were doing to indoctrinate children with anti-God, anti-family, anti-America messages, I knew I had a duty to take action. So, I wrote a little book called “As You Grow” to teach children how to grow in wisdom through the fruit of the spirit. Then I decided to go one step further and counter those awful “Drag Queen Story Hours” with _conservative Story Hours_ filled with the classic books you and I grew up with, plus new wholesome books like mine that captivate children with lessons in bravery, honesty, kindness, and patriotism. And boy, the ALA and radical librarians didn’t like that one bit. >> Over 50 libraries rejected my request to host our Story Hour. >> The ALA helped local libraries scheme ways to keep me out including booking all the event rooms for themselves. >> Social media blew up with attacks: I was compared to a Nazi (that’s original), my publisher was accused of trying to “confuse and demoralize children,” supporters were described as “bored moms/busybodies who need something to feel good about,” and on and on. I can’t even print most things these radicals said because it’s so vile. In the end I got two libraries to reverse course by reminding them that their censorship violated the Constitution of the United States. And thousands of parents and grandparents brought their little ones to those “Story Hours” where we pledged allegiance to the flag, sang “God Bless America”, and read wholesome and Godly books. It was incredible. But here’s the greatest part... From there, parents and grandparents started asking how they could host “Story Hours” of their own. And that’s how the nationwide “See You at the Library” movement was born. Last year, committed conservatives just like you booked event rooms at 201 libraries in 46 states. On the same day, across America hundreds of “Story Hours” filled children’s hearts with goodness, gratitude, and God. Conservative parents, grandparents, and patriots stood together for a very simple mission -- to reject the Left’s radical ideas and reclaim childhood innocence in America’s libraries. _**[And this year, honoring America’s 250th birthday, my ambitious goal is to expand “See You at the Library Day” to reach 250,000 children.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**_ The exact date will soon be announced. And before then, I need you! The response from parents, grandparents, and patriots who want to host “Story Hours” has been overwhelming. That’s a very good thing. But it’s going to be a big undertaking and expensive to give these volunteers the resources they need to hold “Story Hours” for 250,000 children. _**[That’s why I’ve teamed with a very special non-profit called BRAVE for Good to make this year’s “See You at the Library Day” a bigger success than ever.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**_ **BRAVE for Good** was started by BRAVE Books -- the small Christian publisher of my book “As You Grow” –- because so many patriots were asking how they could help “See You at the Library Day” with a tax-deductible gift. Your sponsorship gift helps send a ‘Story Hour Kit’ to every parent, grandparent, and patriot who’s organizing a “See You at the Library” event. The kit includes everything they need to bring your conservative values back into our public libraries: instructions for booking their library space and running their Story Hour, small American flags for little ones, fun stickers, wholesome books, Bible memory verse cards, and other specialty items. Your sponsorship gift is the only way we can fund our “Story Hours” for 250,000 children to counter the radical leftists who’ve taken control of our libraries. We don’t have the millions behind us like the giant taxpayer-funded ALA. _**[Knowing that, please consider a sponsorship gift of $125. That’s enough to sponsor one entire ‘Story Hour Kit’ yourself.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**_ Singlehandedly, you’ll be reaching 50 children with our wholesome, Godly, and patriotic message. Whatever you can give whether it’s $35, $125, or anything higher or lower please send in your sponsorship gift in the next 48 hours so we know how many libraries we have sponsored for this year’s “See You at the Library Day.”

---
Thank you! God Bless You and God Bless America,

Kirk Cameron

Instead of filling children with wholesome stories, the president of the American Library Association (ALA) says libraries should be used to address ‘systemic racism’ and elevate ‘BIPOC and GLBTQR+ writers and voices.’ Radical librarians call Adventures of Huckleberry Finn and To Kill a Mockingbird “racist.” They’ve stripped Laura Ingalls Wilder’s name from a prestigious book award because of her “problematic’ Little House series. And they bring in men wearing full makeup, dresses, and high heels for “Drag Queen Story Hours” where books like these are read to children of all ages... A is for Activist. An ABC board book for “families who want their kids to grow up in a space that is unapologetic about activism, environmental justice, civil rights, LGBTQ rights, and everything else that activists believe in and fight for.” Woke Baby. “For all the littlest progressives, waking up to seize a new day of justice and activism. Woke babies raise their fists in the air. Woke babies cry out for justice. Woke babies grow up to change the world.” Prince and Knight. The “premier queer-friendly fairy tale” about a prince who marries a knight instead of a princess. And The Hips on the Drag Queens Go Swish, Swish, Swish. A “family-friendly celebration of drag” that encourages children to “work it.” I wish I could tell you this was only happening in places like New York City and San Francisco... | | | | ...but that’s just not true. <\- THIS IS A MAN leading “Drag Queen Story Hour.” | | For decades, the ultra-liberal Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation and George Soros’ Open Society have spent millions radicalizing the ALA. And as a result, a new generation of pink-haired, activist librarians have made it their mission to fill library shelves with anti-American, LGBTQ-friendly, and explicitly sexual content. Maybe you’ve noticed all the displays at your own library celebrating Pride Month or elevating ‘the environment’ to a type of religion. Or maybe you’ve noticed the “Teen Zone” which is really meant to be a “parent-free” zone. The “Teen Zone” is filled with books like: Rick about a cross-dressing Grandpa, Melissa filled with graphic nudity, and Darkstalker featuring gory violence and domestic abuse. But here’s what’s really alarming. We can’t just sit back and say, “Well, I’ll just make sure my family doesn’t go to “Drag Queen Story Hour” and we won’t check out those inappropriate books.” That may be good for your family -- for now. But meanwhile, the ALA uses our taxpayer-funded libraries to lure in millions of other children who grow up to be the very activists who are destroying our country and conservative values! My name is Kirk Cameron. Maybe you recognize me from the 1980’s family sitcom “Growing Pains” or from my work in inspirational movies like “Fireproof” and “Left Behind.” I know firsthand how dangerous it is to be indoctrinated by leftist values. Pride almost took me down as a young actor in Hollywood. But the gospel saved me. I love being an actor, but what’s far more important is being a husband, dad, grandad, and a Christian. When I saw what book publishers and libraries were doing to indoctrinate children with anti-God, anti-family, anti-America messages, I knew I had a duty to take action. So, I wrote a little book called “As You Grow” to teach children how to grow in wisdom through the fruit of the spirit. Then I decided to go one step further and counter those awful “Drag Queen Story Hours” with conservative Story Hours filled with the classic books you and I grew up with, plus new wholesome books like mine that captivate children with lessons in bravery, honesty, kindness, and patriotism. And boy, the ALA and radical librarians didn’t like that one bit. >> Over 50 libraries rejected my request to host our Story Hour. >> The ALA helped local libraries scheme ways to keep me out including booking all the event rooms for themselves. >> Social media blew up with attacks: I was compared to a Nazi (that’s original), my publisher was accused of trying to “confuse and demoralize children,” supporters were described as “bored moms/busybodies who need something to feel good about,” and on and on. I can’t even print most things these radicals said because it’s so vile. In the end I got two libraries to reverse course by reminding them that their censorship violated the Constitution of the United States. And thousands of parents and grandparents brought their little ones to those “Story Hours” where we pledged allegiance to the flag, sang “God Bless America”, and read wholesome and Godly books. It was incredible. But here’s the greatest part... From there, parents and grandparents started asking how they could host “Story Hours” of their own. And that’s how the nationwide “See You at the Library” movement was born. Last year, committed conservatives just like you booked event rooms at 201 libraries in 46 states. On the same day, across America hundreds of “Story Hours” filled children’s hearts with goodness, gratitude, and God. Conservative parents, grandparents, and patriots stood together for a very simple mission -- to reject the Left’s radical ideas and reclaim childhood innocence in America’s libraries. The exact date will soon be announced. And before then, I need you! The response from parents, grandparents, and patriots who want to host “Story Hours” has been overwhelming. That’s a very good thing. But it’s going to be a big undertaking and expensive to give these volunteers the resources they need to hold “Story Hours” for 250,000 children. BRAVE for Good was started by BRAVE Books -- the small Christian publisher of my book “As You Grow” –- because so many patriots were asking how they could help “See You at the Library Day” with a tax-deductible gift. Your sponsorship gift helps send a ‘Story Hour Kit’ to every parent, grandparent, and patriot who’s organizing a “See You at the Library” event. The kit includes everything they need to bring your conservative values back into our public libraries: instructions for booking their library space and running their Story Hour, small American flags for little ones, fun stickers, wholesome books, Bible memory verse cards, and other specialty items. Your sponsorship gift is the only way we can fund our “Story Hours” for 250,000 children to counter the radical leftists who’ve taken control of our libraries. We don’t have the millions behind us like the giant taxpayer-funded ALA. Singlehandedly, you’ll be reaching 50 children with our wholesome, Godly, and patriotic message. Whatever you can give whether it’s $35, $125, or anything higher or lower please send in your sponsorship gift in the next 48 hours so we know how many libraries we have sponsored for this year’s “See You at the Library Day.” Thank you! God Bless You and God Bless America, Kirk Cameron | | | BRAVE For Good 100 I-45 N 260 Conroe, TX 77301

Plenty of people doubted I could win. They were wrong. That experience taught me something important: **when the pressure is highest, real leaders don’t back down.**_**_They fight harder, Peter_**_** _._** That’s exactly where Mike Rogers is right now.

My thoughts are with everyone who has been displaced, everyone facing uncertainty about what comes next, and the firefighters, first responders, volunteers, and neighbors working to keep people safe. Many Washingtonians are looking for ways to help. **The City of Spokane has activated its[H.O.M.E. All donations will remain local and go directly toward needs including short- and long-term rental assistance, transportation, replacement documents, medical equipment, diapers, formula, children’s clothing, school supplies, furniture, and basic household items.
**I also want to bring your attention to the importance of giving securely and making sure your donation reaches the people you intend to help.**
Unfortunately, scammers occasionally try to take advantage of people’s generosity after a disaster. Before donating elsewhere, take a moment to verify the organization and its website, and be cautious of high-pressure requests, unfamiliar fundraisers asking for personal information, and QR codes that don't come from a trusted source.

body:
Republicans would love nothing more than this:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1709%2E1086043%2EwX7UAw)
Peter, we're just 90 days out from the election -- **[and we need your help to power our re-election fight.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260807-1.0g85qX&refcode=em-20260807-1&t=2&akid=1709%2E1086043%2EwX7UAw)** Let us explain.
Most people assume Maryland is a safe blue state, _but two of our last four governors were Republicans._
Republicans would love nothing more than to make Wes a one-term governor and prove that they can take out a successful Democrat with a track record of delivering for the people. Now that we’re in the heat of the election, we need to fight back -- and that means running ads to get our message out there.
**But ads are expensive.** If you’ve been waiting to have an impact on this race, now is the time. We need YOUR help to get advertisements on the airwaves and counter any attacks from our opponent.
The only way we’ll be able to run this campaign is with your grassroots support.
**[So Peter, can you chip in any amount to help us run ads in these last 90 days? Your support now will keep us competitive when it matters most.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260807-1.0g85qX&refcode=em-20260807-1&t=3&akid=1709%2E1086043%2EwX7UAw)**

Marylander,

**Maryland cannot afford “business as usual.”**
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/17yRgHLm8oM?e=8837fbc313&c2id=828d56a1e08c8ea74084c0881271a4b3)

For too long, the Comptroller’s Office has been treated as a political stepping stone rather than the**independent fiscal watchdog** it was meant to be. The result is _**insufficient oversight**_ , a structural _**imbalance between spending and revenue**_ , and a government that too often _**fails to earn public trust.**_ Responsible stewardship means **treating every taxpayer dollar with care, discipline, and transparency.** It means **asking hard questions** , **exposing waste** , and putting the **long-term financial health** of Maryland first.I am running for Comptroller to end business as usual and deliver the responsible leadership our state needs. As your Independent Taxpayer Watchdog, I will:**✅ Fight fraud, waste, and abuse****✅ Strengthen oversight and accountability** ✅ Provide **honest,** **long-term financial forecasts** I’m a businesswoman and military spouse who understands that**real fiscal discipline starts with respect for the people who pay the bills.** The general election is November 3. Two different pollsters showing identical results in the same week is not a fluke. It’s a trend. **[Chip in right now to help us take the lead in this race.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260807_2_1ptpoll.N2eby7&refcode=em20260807-1766&amount=5&t=2&akid=1766%2E299639%2EaTd6wj)**

This is essential to our mission: to report on what matters most, beholden only to the truth. Palestinian journalists protest against the assassination of their colleague Hassan Eslaiah, outside Nasser Hospital, in Khan Yunis, Gaza on May 13, 2025. Eslaih was killed in an Israeli attack on Nasser Hospital. Photo by Alaa Y. M. Abumohsen/Anadolu via Getty Images.
Honest Reporting, a self-described media watchdog and nonprofit with offices in New York, Jerusalem, and Toronto, [claims](https://substack.com/redirect/22530894-421b-4d0e-8b95-279775a2ef68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that its mission is exposing "media bias, challenging false narratives, and ensuring that reporting on Israel is rooted in facts, context, and accountability." In practice, it operates as a pressure group, monitoring international media coverage of Israel, producing reports attacking coverage it deems unfavorable, running access operations that embed international journalists within curated pro-Israel perspectives, and organizing mass campaigns directing its subscribers to contact newsrooms directly until corrections, retractions, and rewordings are secured.
That work has led to the dismissal of journalists at publications around the world. But since October 7, 2023, Honest Reporting's operations have moved into considerably darker territory, and its activities have contributed to the assassination of at least one journalist, Hassan Eslaiah--a freelance photographer and director of the Gaza-based Alam24 news agency whose images had appeared in the Associated Press and CNN.
The campaign against Eslaiah was not isolated. Honest Reporting has systematically targeted journalists and news organizations--including Drop Site News--across multiple platforms and countries, employing consistent tactics: publishing posts raising questions about individual journalists' alleged connections to Hamas or other armed groups, characterizing their coverage as propaganda or as "antisemitic," and mobilizing its subscriber network to contact news organizations directly. The cumulative effect of this approach has been to characterize numerous Palestinian journalists as combatants.
Despite its record as a pressure group that targets and endangers reporters, in 2023 Honest Reporting's Israeli organization--registered under the name Divuach Ne'eman R''A--received an "emergency" grant of $100,000 from the Knight Foundation, a widely respected U.S.-based foundation that prominently touts a commitment to freedom of press and the safety of journalists. The grant, listed in Honest Reporting's Israeli nonprofit filings for 2024, is not reported in the Knight Foundation's 990 for 2024 or on its website.
The Knight Foundation [says](https://substack.com/redirect/d70bdf84-4de2-4644-b2d4-d218224d234c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that it primarily funds U.S.-based organizations and that international programs and organizations are among the categories it generally prefers not to fund, making grants outside the United States limited and exceptional by the foundation's own description. Knight's website [states](https://substack.com/redirect/d70bdf84-4de2-4644-b2d4-d218224d234c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that "most of our grantmaking is tied to strategies with defined goals and outcomes" and that funding "typically emerges through relationships, research and ongoing work," with most grants initiated by Knight itself rather than through open applications.
When approached for comment, Atena Sherry, Knight Foundation's director of communications, initially denied that Knight had provided funding to Honest Reporting: "Knight Foundation did not provide any grant to Honest Reporting, and the foundation has not directed any Knight funds to Honest Reporting" through any third party, Sherry told Drop Site. In a follow-up statement, Sherry said, "We reviewed all documentation. Knight Foundation has never provided any funding to Honest Reporting."
According to Honest Reporting, however, "the grantor, Jewish Federations of North America and United Israel Appeal, notified Divuach Ne'eman R"A and HonestReporting.com, Inc. that a donation of $100,000 was made 'on the recommendation of the donor, The Knight Foundation.' Honest Reporting added that "Staff for Divuach Ne'eman R"A and Honest Reporting.com, Inc. were in direct touch with staff at the Knight Foundation throughout the process on the grant and the programs that would benefit from the grant."
When Drop Site then asked the Knight Foundation about Honest Reporting's statement, which directly contradicted its own, the Knight Foundation acknowledged that it had provided funds for Media Central, an Honest Reporting program that arranges tours for international journalists. "Knight Foundation did make a one-time, emergency grant of $100,000 in November 2023 to Media Central to support a very specific project: helping international journalists to gain access they wouldn't otherwise have had to report on the facts from the ground in the West Bank," said Alejandro de Onis, vice president for communications, in a statement. "Neither the grant agreement nor the grant file contains any reference to Honest Reporting."
Unlike Gaza, the West Bank has remained accessible to international journalists, raising the question of what access Media Central was providing that journalists could not obtain independently, and whether the access in question was in fact embedded reporting alongside the Israeli military.
Knight declined to answer additional questions about the specific reporting funded by its grant or how it could have been unaware that Media Central was a program operated by Honest Reporting.

## "We don't claim to be a news organization."
On November 8, 2023, one month into the genocide in Gaza and the same month as the Knight Foundation grant, Honest Reporting published what it classified as an [expose](https://substack.com/redirect/627ff8c1-2b14-4c97-a9cd-d80adc7ccc40?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on its website. The article featured photographs of several Palestinian freelance journalists who had been covering the events near the Gaza border on the morning of October 7, among them Hassan Eslaiah. It asked, in language the organization has since described as just "raising questions," whether these journalists could have had advance knowledge of the Hamas attack. The article was then updated to feature a photograph from 2020 of Eslaiah next to Hamas leader Yayha Sinwar--clearly suggesting guilt by association through proximity in a photograph.
Within hours, Israel's official X account had [amplified](https://substack.com/redirect/190a64d3-bf40-499a-a0fe-8b1ea17630e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the post to its own audience of 1.8 million. The Associated Press reviewed its relationship with Eslaiah and later [severed](https://substack.com/redirect/c34e9974-51a2-4208-b7f4-94011339ed34?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it, while stating publicly it had found no evidence he had foreknowledge of the attack beyond what was known to journalists routinely working in the border area. When the AP asked Gil Hoffman, then Honest Reporting's executive director, to substantiate the allegations, his [response](https://substack.com/redirect/e7eae1f4-5668-48c2-b5aa-bb44d97f79b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) was notable. "They acted as if we were stating facts instead of asking questions," Hoffman said. "We don't claim to be a news organization."
Jonthan Dagher, head of the Middle East desk of Reporters Without Borders (RSF), described the November 2023 Honest Reporting article as being "full of conjecture" and "based on circumstantial evidence," noting that it "provoked a chain of reactions from Israeli authorities and politicians who started accusing Gazan journalists of belonging to Hamas."
RSF named Honest Reporting in its 2025 list of Press Freedom Predators that it says "smear media and promote mistrust of journalists."
Eighteen months later, in April 2025, an Israeli airstrike struck a media tent outside Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, [killing](https://substack.com/redirect/c5fd573b-9fd6-49d2-bd8c-3b5840802bdf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two journalists and wounding eight others, Eslaiah was among them. The Israeli military publicly [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/6422920d-dba0-46dc-9617-acb8d37a1fcd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it had deliberately targeted Eslaiah, claiming he was a member of the Khan Younis Brigade and had participated in the attacks of October 7th. Eslaiah survived the strike but his skull was fractured, his body was burned, and he lost two of his fingers. He was admitted to Nasser Hospital's burns unit to recover. On May 13, 2025, while he lay in the burn unit, an Israeli drone bombed the hospital and murdered him. Hours later, the Israeli military admitted to assassinating Eslaiah, calling him "Aslih" and [posting](https://substack.com/redirect/727283c5-fffd-4737-912e-010cba3daf85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a screenshot of Eslaiah on Oct. 7, 2023 from a video also posted by Honest Reporting in its "expose" and saying: "Don't let Aslih's press vest fool you...Journalist? More like terrorist."
## Targeting Palestinian Journalists
Since the start of the genocide in Gaza, one of Honest Reporting's central goals has been to challenge the records kept by press freedom organizations documenting Palestinian journalists killed in Gaza. The organization has led a sustained pressure campaign against the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ), which maintains the most widely cited casualty list of media workers killed in Gaza. It has also sought to attack and pressure other press freedom bodies such as [Reporters Without Borders](https://substack.com/redirect/5d4e9576-017c-4e4e-abf1-1b262cde7871?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and the [International Federation of Journalists](https://substack.com/redirect/89b3f6f2-25a1-411c-8774-76097c376b38?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
On June 25, CPJ [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/8f6c2238-bef1-4cef-b6e9-bc493f7eab1d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that it would be "conducting a full review of its database of journalists killed during the Israel-Gaza War." Honest Reporting was quick to [claim](https://substack.com/redirect/ecac01fb-6cd9-42e4-b2f5-b3dd05dc5f27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) victory, [stating](https://substack.com/redirect/5e11b622-92f7-47c5-b65a-36ee618a4a61?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the review had happened because Honest Reporting had "helped put them in an untenable position."
In a statement, CPJ denied that Honest Reporting's pressure campaign was responsible for its database review.
"The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) is an independent organization. We independently research, source and report information related to attacks on journalists and media workers. When new information becomes available, we update our reporting. Our review of the Israel-Gaza war casualties list was spurred by new information published by Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad that identified as combatants individuals previously listed by CPJ as journalists. Honest Reporting's campaign had absolutely no bearing on the review process or on the decision to remove names from the list."
CPJ, which receives major funding from the Knight Foundation, did not respond to questions about the foundation's grant to Honest Reporting.
"We condemn any misrepresentation of that process to serve political agendas or to try to obscure the fact Israel has killed more journalists than any other country in the world and been the leading killer of journalists for the past three years," CPJ said in its statement.
In response to questions about the direct conflict of interest entailed by funding both a press freedom organization that maintains a database of journalists killed by Israel and a pressure group that targets Palestinian journalists, the Knight Foundation said, "The funding directed to Media Central was specifically and only earmarked to facilitate journalists' access to report on the war in hard to reach areas and there is no ongoing relationship. Nothing in Knight Foundation's grant records reflects any reference to a campaign concerning CPJ, and Knight Foundation has never funded advocacy directed at CPJ."
On the same day that CPJ announced its Gaza database review, Jacob Weisberg, chair of CPJ's board of directors, [emailed fellow board members](https://substack.com/redirect/64c09ed1-2f4e-4aa6-a5c1-a23c0e41b6e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to say that he was establishing a "special task force to reexamine the question of 'Who is a journalist?'"
According to [reporting](https://substack.com/redirect/64c09ed1-2f4e-4aa6-a5c1-a23c0e41b6e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the Columbia Journal Review, Weisberg's initiative was separate from the database review and grew out of a board discussion of an article in the right-wing Washington Free Beacon that largely repackaged Honest Reporting's attacks on CPJ and news organizations that report critically on Israel, including Drop Site.
Nika Soon-Shiong, publisher of Drop Site News and a member of the CPJ board, was alarmed by Weisberg's email and requested a vote on the proposal by the full board, according to a letter she posted publicly. She was then informed by Weisberg that her term on the board had expired. On July 1, the board held an emergency meeting and voted to [affirm](https://substack.com/redirect/b7e5999c-364e-4168-bb0a-5d9339e558a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its "existing definition of who is a journalist."

Honest Reporting was launched in 2000 in association with the Jerusalem Fund of Aish HaTorah, an Orthodox Jewish outreach movement whose stated mission is encouraging secular Jews to embrace religious observance, but which also operates one of the most extensive pro-Israel advocacy networks in the world. The organization's first executive director was [Irwin Katsof](https://substack.com/redirect/17d2e586-ea61-4aab-8df1-4ab8524114a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), who simultaneously served as president of the Jerusalem Fund. In 2001, the Jerusalem Fund lent the newly established Middle East Media Watch (Honest Reporting's registered name at the time) $158,724. The following year, Aish HaTorah's Jerusalem operation provided a further $48,100 grant.
Honest Reporting's 2006 tax return lists [Ephraim Shore](https://substack.com/redirect/b2702add-5bb5-4028-b3cb-6c3319c4dc48?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), who heads Aish's operations in Israel, as president. His twin brother, Raphael Shore, produced "Obsession: Radical Islam's War Against the West," a controversial 2005 film that Honest Reporting initially promoted as its own project on its website and listed as an affiliate in 2006, before later [denying any involvement](https://substack.com/redirect/daf893cd-3c86-4958-97d9-44f108c7d958?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in its production.
