Multiple current Honest Reporting staff members worked as Hasbara Fellowship lecturers.
The financial relationship between Aish HaTorah and Honest Reporting has not been confined to the founding period. Canadian tax filings [show](https://substack.com/redirect/a54a738c-9823-4999-9a4d-74e0caa345d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Honest Reporting Canada made a donation of $15,000 to Aish HaTorah as recently as 2023, demonstrating that the institutional relationship between the two organizations remains active more than two decades after Honest Reporting's founding.
The network around Honest Reporting extends to some of the most controversial pro-Israel blacklisting operations on the internet, including Canary Mission, the pro-Israel doxxing site that publishes dossiers on students, academics, and activists it accused of anti-Semitism or support for Palestinian rights. At least one former employee of [Honest Reporting](https://substack.com/redirect/e10e2606-e7e4-44e7-aad0-461684e643a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg),[ Zahava Raymond](https://substack.com/redirect/b0a1599c-760c-48a1-a2e6-343a36acd898?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has worked at [Megamot Shalom](https://substack.com/redirect/917842c8-e3fc-417e-a2f6-02939e9988ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the Israeli nonprofit organization funding Canary Mission.
## **A Widening Operation**
According to Honest Reporting's filings with Israel's Corporations Authority, 96.6% of the total 2024 budget of 6,040,198 NIS [$1,632,044] comes from foreign donations. In addition to the $100,000 grant from the Knight Foundation, 4,903,640 NIS [$1,324,950] came directly from Honest Reporting's U.S. organization. The Israeli operation is almost entirely dependent on American dollars.
Honest Reporting's recent [communications](https://substack.com/redirect/cff7edf1-20dc-4fee-9561-d8c75b601100?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) demonstrate the group's growing ambitions. An update to supporters describes the launch of "Honest Reporting AI Labs," a proprietary system trained to identify "anti-Israel bias" and intercept narratives "before they reach mainstream credibility." The system monitors social media in real time, traces what the organization characterizes as "coordinated narrative pipelines," and feeds findings to what it calls "strategic communications partners," among them the Foundation for Defense of Democracies.
In May, for example, Rachel O'Donoghue, an employee of Honest Reporting, was [invited](https://substack.com/redirect/3940c70b-4db1-44e5-bb27-80ccc663eef0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to publish a column in the [Wall Street Journal](https://substack.com/redirect/6763a237-e9d6-4ac1-8079-9f3a9d36e1bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) challenging Nicolas Kristoff's article in the New York Times about Israel's use of sexual violence against Palestinian detainees. The organization's research has also been cited in articles published by the [Washington Free Beacon](https://substack.com/redirect/f0032f95-c41b-4ebc-bf38-b1fa853de7ea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [National Review](https://substack.com/redirect/f038bd5c-f262-4727-a709-d20871d046d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
The reach of Honest Reporting and its affiliates extends into the legislative institutions of its English-speaking donor base. In 2018, Honest Reporting submitted [evidence](https://substack.com/redirect/a79acb3a-8c73-470c-a05e-980a607105f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the UK Parliament's inquiry into fake news, falsely claiming that "Honest Reporting is not aligned with any government or political party or movement." The submission was initially [absent](https://substack.com/redirect/f018c213-1f53-45c7-94da-8c460e986f51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from the inquiry's published record and was only made available following the intervention of UK Lawyers for Israel.
The Canadian operation has demonstrated similar objectives. In July 2023, Honest Reporting Canada's executive director Mike Fegelman [said](https://substack.com/redirect/31884e27-0c69-4960-a232-531a9fa6c769?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it wanted to "create a digital army for Israel." A [written briefing](https://substack.com/redirect/f9fb30ac-4b04-4bc5-9480-b948830fc93e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the House of Commons' Standing Committee on Canadian Heritage referred to Palestinian journalists killed by Israel as "so-called journalists" with "connections to Palestinian terrorist groups" and claimed media coverage of Gaza "directly contributes to a spike in anti-Jewish hate crimes."
Another significant donor identified in Honest Reporting's 2024 Israeli filings is a vaguely named organization called Canadian Charity Partners, which contributed 507,176 NIS [$137,000]. In January 2026, the Canada Revenue Agency [revoked](https://substack.com/redirect/bc7161e7-7824-4e37-a5ee-88999b348135?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Canadian Charity Partners' charitable status, citing multiple areas of non-compliance including conducting non-charitable activities and failing to maintain adequate books and records.
Honest Reporting Canada has run its own pressure campaigns against journalists and outlets it deems biased against Israel, claiming to have contributed to the dismissal of two Palestinian journalists in October 2023, one of whom was on maternity leave at the time. In November 2024, [Robert Walker](https://substack.com/redirect/d62426d3-fe79-4df3-af80-b7ac46b04981?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the group's assistant director, [was arrested and faced 17 criminal charges](https://substack.com/redirect/e6209e44-5f93-4284-8eb2-c50e2b8b6e50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in connection with a string of anti-Palestinian graffiti in Toronto, including the phrase "Fuck Gaza." The charges were [withdrawn](https://substack.com/redirect/f63c9a8e-127e-49d3-abd6-07a1c4678120?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in March 2025 after a payment to charity. Walker remains employed by the organization.

Honest Reporting, a self-described media watchdog and nonprofit with offices in New York, Jerusalem, and Toronto, that its mission is exposing "media bias, challenging false narratives, and ensuring that reporting on Israel is rooted in facts, context, and accountability." In practice, it operates as a pressure group, monitoring international media coverage of Israel, producing reports attacking coverage it deems unfavorable, running access operations that embed international journalists within curated pro-Israel perspectives, and organizing mass campaigns directing its subscribers to contact newsrooms directly until corrections, retractions, and rewordings are secured. That work has led to the dismissal of journalists at publications around the world. But since October 7, 2023, Honest Reporting's operations have moved into considerably darker territory, and its activities have contributed to the assassination of at least one journalist, Hassan Eslaiah--a freelance photographer and director of the Gaza-based Alam24 news agency whose images had appeared in the Associated Press and CNN. The campaign against Eslaiah was not isolated. Honest Reporting has systematically targeted journalists and news organizations--including Drop Site News--across multiple platforms and countries, employing consistent tactics: publishing posts raising questions about individual journalists' alleged connections to Hamas or other armed groups, characterizing their coverage as propaganda or as "antisemitic," and mobilizing its subscriber network to contact news organizations directly. The cumulative effect of this approach has been to characterize numerous Palestinian journalists as combatants. Despite its record as a pressure group that targets and endangers reporters, in 2023 Honest Reporting's Israeli organization--registered under the name Divuach Ne'eman R''A--received an "emergency" grant of $100,000 from the Knight Foundation, a widely respected U.S.-based foundation that prominently touts a commitment to freedom of press and the safety of journalists. The grant, listed in Honest Reporting's Israeli nonprofit filings for 2024, is not reported in the Knight Foundation's 990 for 2024 or on its website. The Knight Foundation that it primarily funds U.S.-based organizations and that international programs and organizations are among the categories it generally prefers not to fund, making grants outside the United States limited and exceptional by the foundation's own description. Knight's website that "most of our grantmaking is tied to strategies with defined goals and outcomes" and that funding "typically emerges through relationships, research and ongoing work," with most grants initiated by Knight itself rather than through open applications. When approached for comment, Atena Sherry, Knight Foundation's director of communications, initially denied that Knight had provided funding to Honest Reporting: "Knight Foundation did not provide any grant to Honest Reporting, and the foundation has not directed any Knight funds to Honest Reporting" through any third party, Sherry told Drop Site. In a follow-up statement, Sherry said, "We reviewed all documentation. Knight Foundation has never provided any funding to Honest Reporting." According to Honest Reporting, however, "the grantor, Jewish Federations of North America and United Israel Appeal, notified Divuach Ne'eman R"A and HonestReporting.com, Inc. that a donation of $100,000 was made 'on the recommendation of the donor, The Knight Foundation.' Honest Reporting added that "Staff for Divuach Ne'eman R"A and Honest Reporting.com, Inc. were in direct touch with staff at the Knight Foundation throughout the process on the grant and the programs that would benefit from the grant." When Drop Site then asked the Knight Foundation about Honest Reporting's statement, which directly contradicted its own, the Knight Foundation acknowledged that it had provided funds for Media Central, an Honest Reporting program that arranges tours for international journalists. "Knight Foundation did make a one-time, emergency grant of $100,000 in November 2023 to Media Central to support a very specific project: helping international journalists to gain access they wouldn't otherwise have had to report on the facts from the ground in the West Bank," said Alejandro de Onis, vice president for communications, in a statement. "Neither the grant agreement nor the grant file contains any reference to Honest Reporting." Unlike Gaza, the West Bank has remained accessible to international journalists, raising the question of what access Media Central was providing that journalists could not obtain independently, and whether the access in question was in fact embedded reporting alongside the Israeli military. Knight declined to answer additional questions about the specific reporting funded by its grant or how it could have been unaware that Media Central was a program operated by Honest Reporting. Through its Media Central project, Honest Reporting arranges press tours, briefings, and curated access to Israel for international correspondents, as a neutral resource while functioning as an operation designed to shape how journalists understand and cover the country. Honest Reporting's director of press relations, Laura Cornfield, runs the program. In Honest Reporting's 2023 first quarter , Cornfield wrote that: "Journalists met with locals to hear how the Lions' Den terrorist group was using Nablus as its command center. They were then briefed by the IDF to understand the security risks to Israeli civilians," boasting that "MediaCentral staff enabled exclusive access to these unheard, nearly impossible-to-reach voices. The tour was so sought after it was repeated with three groups, and an additional three one-on-one tours were arranged." In that year's second quarter , Cornfield wrote that the group's Media Central program "took foreign media outlets on exclusive tours to hotbeds of terror activity, including Nablus and Jenin, to get an up-close look at what Israeli security forces are facing and how they are addressing the threats." The reports say that journalists from prominent international outlets including the New York Times, the Wall Street Journal, the Economist, the Financial Times, and CNN have participated in its events. The impact report described a media tour of the Israel-Lebanon border, quoting the Israeli military's Lt. Gen. Herzi Halevi and Military Intelligence Directorate chief Aharon Haliva on Hezbollah. It also included a section on "crime in the Arab sector" and said that journalists had gone on "a field tour to Umm Al Fahm and Jaffa of Nazareth to address the surging crime rate," referring to largely Palestinian towns and cities within Israel. More recently, Media Central press tours have taken international journalists to the Aqsa compound and in occupied East Jerusalem and to . Media Central has also hosted exclusive briefings for international journalists with senior Israeli political figures, including a in Tel Aviv with former Israeli Ambassador to the United States Michael Oren and an" with Brigadier General (Res.) Pinchas (Pini) Yungman. Yungman has held senior command roles in the Israeli Air Force and executive positions at the Israeli defense company Rafael. On November 8, 2023, one month into the genocide in Gaza and the same month as the Knight Foundation grant, Honest Reporting published what it classified as an on its website. The article featured photographs of several Palestinian freelance journalists who had been covering the events near the Gaza border on the morning of October 7, among them Hassan Eslaiah. It asked, in language the organization has since described as just "raising questions," whether these journalists could have had advance knowledge of the Hamas attack. The article was then updated to feature a photograph from 2020 of Eslaiah next to Hamas leader Yayha Sinwar--clearly suggesting guilt by association through proximity in a photograph. Within hours, Israel's official X account had the post to its own audience of 1.8 million. The Associated Press reviewed its relationship with Eslaiah and later it, while stating publicly it had found no evidence he had foreknowledge of the attack beyond what was known to journalists routinely working in the border area. When the AP asked Gil Hoffman, then Honest Reporting's executive director, to substantiate the allegations, his was notable. "They acted as if we were stating facts instead of asking questions," Hoffman said. "We don't claim to be a news organization." Jonthan Dagher, head of the Middle East desk of Reporters Without Borders (RSF), described the November 2023 Honest Reporting article as being "full of conjecture" and "based on circumstantial evidence," noting that it "provoked a chain of reactions from Israeli authorities and politicians who started accusing Gazan journalists of belonging to Hamas." RSF named Honest Reporting in its 2025 list of Press Freedom Predators that it says "smear media and promote mistrust of journalists." Eighteen months later, in April 2025, an Israeli airstrike struck a media tent outside Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, two journalists and wounding eight others, Eslaiah was among them. The Israeli military publicly it had deliberately targeted Eslaiah, claiming he was a member of the Khan Younis Brigade and had participated in the attacks of October 7th. Eslaiah survived the strike but his skull was fractured, his body was burned, and he lost two of his fingers. He was admitted to Nasser Hospital's burns unit to recover. On May 13, 2025, while he lay in the burn unit, an Israeli drone bombed the hospital and murdered him. Hours later, the Israeli military admitted to assassinating Eslaiah, calling him "Aslih" and a screenshot of Eslaiah on Oct. 7, 2023 from a video also posted by Honest Reporting in its "expose" and saying: "Don't let Aslih's press vest fool you...Journalist? More like terrorist." Targeting Palestinian Journalists Since the start of the genocide in Gaza, one of Honest Reporting's central goals has been to challenge the records kept by press freedom organizations documenting Palestinian journalists killed in Gaza. The organization has led a sustained pressure campaign against the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ), which maintains the most widely cited casualty list of media workers killed in Gaza. It has also sought to attack and pressure other press freedom bodies such as and the . On June 25, CPJ that it would be "conducting a full review of its database of journalists killed during the Israel-Gaza War." Honest Reporting was quick to victory, that the review had happened because Honest Reporting had "helped put them in an untenable position." In a statement, CPJ denied that Honest Reporting's pressure campaign was responsible for its database review. "The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) is an independent organization. We independently research, source and report information related to attacks on journalists and media workers. When new information becomes available, we update our reporting. Our review of the Israel-Gaza war casualties list was spurred by new information published by Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad that identified as combatants individuals previously listed by CPJ as journalists. Honest Reporting's campaign had absolutely no bearing on the review process or on the decision to remove names from the list." CPJ, which receives major funding from the Knight Foundation, did not respond to questions about the foundation's grant to Honest Reporting. "We condemn any misrepresentation of that process to serve political agendas or to try to obscure the fact Israel has killed more journalists than any other country in the world and been the leading killer of journalists for the past three years," CPJ said in its statement. In response to questions about the direct conflict of interest entailed by funding both a press freedom organization that maintains a database of journalists killed by Israel and a pressure group that targets Palestinian journalists, the Knight Foundation said, "The funding directed to Media Central was specifically and only earmarked to facilitate journalists' access to report on the war in hard to reach areas and there is no ongoing relationship. Nothing in Knight Foundation's grant records reflects any reference to a campaign concerning CPJ, and Knight Foundation has never funded advocacy directed at CPJ." On the same day that CPJ announced its Gaza database review, Jacob Weisberg, chair of CPJ's board of directors, to say that he was establishing a "special task force to reexamine the question of 'Who is a journalist?'" According to in the Columbia Journal Review, Weisberg's initiative was separate from the database review and grew out of a board discussion of an article in the right-wing Washington Free Beacon that largely repackaged Honest Reporting's attacks on CPJ and news organizations that report critically on Israel, including Drop Site. Nika Soon-Shiong, publisher of Drop Site News and a member of the CPJ board, was alarmed by Weisberg's email and requested a vote on the proposal by the full board, according to a letter she posted publicly. She was then informed by Weisberg that her term on the board had expired. On July 1, the board held an emergency meeting and voted to its "existing definition of who is a journalist." Broader Influence Network Honest Reporting's sustained attempts to establish connections between journalists and armed groups, such as Hamas, is particularly striking given the organization's direct ties to AIPAC, the Israeli government, and the Israeli military, which continues to carry out a genocide in the Gaza Strip. Prior to co-founding Honest Reporting, spent 25 years at AIPAC, including 15 years directing its Jerusalem office, before serving three years as deputy chief of mission at the Israeli embassy in Washington. He has with evident pride how an early Honest Reporting campaign crashed CNN's internet servers. The organization he helped build is now by , who spent approximately 15 years at AIPAC before being hired with a mandate to expand Honest Reporting's reach in the United States. National Development Director spent more than eight years as an AIPAC regional director before moving into Honest Reporting's fundraising operation. worked in AIPAC's political department for over ten years before , where he served as a senior foreign policy advisor to Israeli government minister Tzachi Hanegbi, and then joined Honest Reporting. , treasurer of Honest Reporting's U.S. organization, has positions on the boards of AIPAC's Houston Council, Friends of the IDF, the Jewish Federation, Anti-Defamation League, and the United Israel Appeal. He is also as a director of the Foundation for the Defense of Democracies, a pro-Israel think tank. , the group's director of press relations, also runs the program. She attends high-level events within Israeli political circles posing and smiling with U.S ambassador to Israel and . The connections to the Israeli military are equally direct. Multiple staff members served in the Israeli military, a fact Honest Reporting says "should not be a surprise" given Israel's mandatory service requirement. , former executive director and current board member, for example, in an Israeli army artillery unit and later as an Israeli military reserve spokesperson following his emigration to Israel, before his journalism career at the Jerusalem Post. Editorial Director has also served in the Israeli military's press office. , who now appears as a in Honest Reporting's social media output, spent more than two years in the Israeli military press office, where she served as head of its Iranian-language social media desk. In a statement, Honest Reporting denied that it has a formal relationship with the Israeli military. "There is no formal affiliation or partnership between the IDF and Divuach Ne'eman R"A or HonestReporting.com, Inc." Honest Reporting was launched in 2000 in association with the Jerusalem Fund of Aish HaTorah, an Orthodox Jewish outreach movement whose stated mission is encouraging secular Jews to embrace religious observance, but which also operates one of the most extensive pro-Israel advocacy networks in the world. The organization's first executive director was , who simultaneously served as president of the Jerusalem Fund. In 2001, the Jerusalem Fund lent the newly established Middle East Media Watch (Honest Reporting's registered name at the time) $158,724. The following year, Aish HaTorah's Jerusalem operation provided a further $48,100 grant. Honest Reporting's 2006 tax return lists , who heads Aish's operations in Israel, as president. Shore is also one of the founders of the Hasbara Fellowships program--the Israeli Foreign Ministry's campus advocacy initiative that Aish HaTorah was asked to develop and run. His twin brother, Raphael Shore, produced "Obsession: Radical Islam's War Against the West," a controversial 2005 film that Honest Reporting initially promoted as its own project on its website and listed as an affiliate in 2006, before later in its production. When the Israeli Foreign Ministry sought to counter what it characterized as anti-Israel sentiment on university campuses internationally, it turned to Aish HaTorah to design and run the program, which flies hundreds of student leaders to Israel for intensive advocacy training. Multiple current Honest Reporting staff members worked as Hasbara Fellowship lecturers. The financial relationship between Aish HaTorah and Honest Reporting has not been confined to the founding period. Canadian tax filings that Honest Reporting Canada made a donation of $15,000 to Aish HaTorah as recently as 2023, demonstrating that the institutional relationship between the two organizations remains active more than two decades after Honest Reporting's founding. The network around Honest Reporting extends to some of the most controversial pro-Israel blacklisting operations on the internet, including Canary Mission, the pro-Israel doxxing site that publishes dossiers on students, academics, and activists it accused of anti-Semitism or support for Palestinian rights. At least one former employee of has worked at , the Israeli nonprofit organization funding Canary Mission. A Widening Operation According to Honest Reporting's filings with Israel's Corporations Authority, 96.6% of the total 2024 budget of 6,040,198 NIS [$1,632,044] comes from foreign donations. In addition to the $100,000 grant from the Knight Foundation, 4,903,640 NIS [$1,324,950] came directly from Honest Reporting's U.S. organization. The Israeli operation is almost entirely dependent on American dollars. Honest Reporting's recent demonstrate the group's growing ambitions. An update to supporters describes the launch of "Honest Reporting AI Labs," a proprietary system trained to identify "anti-Israel bias" and intercept narratives "before they reach mainstream credibility." The system monitors social media in real time, traces what the organization characterizes as "coordinated narrative pipelines," and feeds findings to what it calls "strategic communications partners," among them the Foundation for Defense of Democracies. In May, for example, Rachel O'Donoghue, an employee of Honest Reporting, was to publish a column in the challenging Nicolas Kristoff's article in the New York Times about Israel's use of sexual violence against Palestinian detainees. The organization's research has also been cited in articles published by the and . The reach of Honest Reporting and its affiliates extends into the legislative institutions of its English-speaking donor base. In 2018, Honest Reporting submitted to the UK Parliament's inquiry into fake news, falsely claiming that "Honest Reporting is not aligned with any government or political party or movement." The submission was initially from the inquiry's published record and was only made available following the intervention of UK Lawyers for Israel. The Canadian operation has demonstrated similar objectives. In July 2023, Honest Reporting Canada's executive director Mike Fegelman it wanted to "create a digital army for Israel." A to the House of Commons' Standing Committee on Canadian Heritage referred to Palestinian journalists killed by Israel as "so-called journalists" with "connections to Palestinian terrorist groups" and claimed media coverage of Gaza "directly contributes to a spike in anti-Jewish hate crimes." Another significant donor identified in Honest Reporting's 2024 Israeli filings is a vaguely named organization called Canadian Charity Partners, which contributed 507,176 NIS [$137,000]. In January 2026, the Canada Revenue Agency Canadian Charity Partners' charitable status, citing multiple areas of non-compliance including conducting non-charitable activities and failing to maintain adequate books and records. Honest Reporting Canada has run its own pressure campaigns against journalists and outlets it deems biased against Israel, claiming to have contributed to the dismissal of two Palestinian journalists in October 2023, one of whom was on maternity leave at the time. In November 2024, , the group's assistant director, in connection with a string of anti-Palestinian graffiti in Toronto, including the phrase "Fuck Gaza." The charges were in March 2025 after a payment to charity. You might be wondering: _Who exactly is Michael Whatley, our Republican opponent in this U.S. Senate race?_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ddcd0c41-3eae-4df3-a440-014d1b63b59b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The short answer is this: He's a Big Oil and utility company lobbyist, Washington DC insider, friend to pedophiles, and MAGA loyalist who was cherry-picked by President Trump to chair the RNC and run for North Carolina's must-win seat.
Whatley's career paints a troubling picture: one filled with scandal and prejudice that somehow always comes back to Trump.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/a4600a2f-fa4c-4663-8c32-006886ba9004?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
In case you didn't already know, here are a few facts about Roy's opponent, Michael Whatley:
1. Whatley has relentlessly pushed policies that have sent his stock portfolio soaring ... while making gas, groceries, utilities and flood and health insurance more expensive for working families.

2. He called President Trump's One Big Beautiful Bill a "huge win," even though it could strip health care from hundreds of thousands North Carolinians and could shutter five rural hospitals.

3. He appointed a convicted child sex offender -- someone who spent six years in prison and over 10 years on the sex offender list -- to powerful positions of leadership when he was the Chair of the North Carolina GOP.

1. He's a guy who has and will continue to put the interests of billionaires, his portfolio, and his well-connected friends over people like us.

While Whatley spent his career lining his pockets and sucking up to Trump, Roy Cooper has been working hard to serve the needs of North Carolinians. And he's got the receipts to prove it.
As Governor, he worked with Republicans to expand Medicaid for over 730,000 people across the state, added hundreds of thousands of good paying jobs, boosted public education, invested in rural communities and so much more.
He stood up to Republicans when they tried to hurt the state and worked across the aisle when it would provide good for the people of North Carolina.
The stakes of this race could not be more clear. **If Whatley wins in North Carolina, the GOP could keep control of the Senate until 2029,** and far-right super PACs are investing nearly $100 million so far to make sure that happens. We need your help to stop them.
If you're ready to help flip this must-win seat and the Senate majority, defeat Whatley and send a powerful message to DC, I hope you'll join me in this fight. We can't do this without you.
Jeff

| | Welcome back to Fact Friday. **Today we're discussing a question I hear often: What does a Member of Congress actually do?** With headlines and clips of members of Congress going viral seemingly every day, it makes a ton of sense why folks would assume most of what we do is have heated debates on the floor of the House chamber. While debating bills is a part of the job, it's just a small part of the work being done in Congress. At a glance, much of what I do is split among equally important responsibilities, like attending committee meetings, drafting, influencing, and voting on critical legislation to be considered in the House, conducting agency oversight, developing budgets for essential government agencies, and my favorite part, meeting with El Pasoans in DC and back home. **Let's break this down a bit more:** **Committees** : Both the House and the Senate have many issues to discuss and agencies to oversee. To make this manageable, these issues are divided into committees with different jurisdictions (basically, topic areas) that determine where we draft and send legislation to address important issues. One of the committees I sit on is the **House Appropriations Committee** _,_ which determines how your tax dollars are allocated to government agencies and programs. I also serve on two subcommittees within the Appropriations Committee: the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) subcommittee and the Military Construction and Veterans Affairs subcommittee. The second committee I sit on is the **House Budget Committee** , which drafts an annual framework for Congressional spending. Whenever a piece of legislation comes before me, I must consider how it will affect my constituents and how it will interact with existing laws. **Serving constituents:** Centering El Paso in the heart of D.C. is why I was elected to my position. In order to confidently and accurately draft legislation and guide the committees I've been appointed to, I need to know what's important to the people in my district so I can draft legislation that is informed by you and addresses the challenges you navigate every day. clean_body: | | | | Welcome back to Fact Friday. Today we're discussing a question I hear often: What does a Member of Congress actually do? With headlines and clips of members of Congress going viral seemingly every day, it makes a ton of sense why folks would assume most of what we do is have heated debates on the floor of the House chamber. While debating bills is a part of the job, it's just a small part of the work being done in Congress. At a glance, much of what I do is split among equally important responsibilities, like attending committee meetings, drafting, influencing, and voting on critical legislation to be considered in the House, conducting agency oversight, developing budgets for essential government agencies, and my favorite part, meeting with El Pasoans in DC and back home. Let's break this down a bit more: Committees : Both the House and the Senate have many issues to discuss and agencies to oversee. To make this manageable, these issues are divided into committees with different jurisdictions (basically, topic areas) that determine where we draft and send legislation to address important issues. One of the committees I sit on is the House Appropriations Committee , which determines how your tax dollars are allocated to government agencies and programs. I also serve on two subcommittees within the Appropriations Committee: the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) subcommittee and the Military Construction and Veterans Affairs subcommittee. The second committee I sit on is the House Budget Committee , which drafts an annual framework for Congressional spending. Whenever a piece of legislation comes before me, I must consider how it will affect my constituents and how it will interact with existing laws. Serving constituents: Centering El Paso in the heart of D.C. is why I was elected to my position. In order to confidently and accurately draft legislation and guide the committees I've been appointed to, I need to know what's important to the people in my district so I can draft legislation that is informed by you and addresses the challenges you navigate every day. But serving constituents also means helping El Pasoans navigate the federal government. My office works with constituents experiencing problems with federal agencies — whether that means getting answers about veterans benefits, Social Security, passports, immigration cases, or other federal services. Oversight and Investigation: A critical part of my job is conducting government oversight, regardless of who's in power, to ensure that once laws are enacted, they are enforced the way they were intended and not misused — a responsibility that I take very seriously. I am especially focused on conducting oversight with regard to my subcommittees (DHS, military construction, and the VA). Some of the clips you've seen of me asking tough and honest questions of elected and appointed officials come from these sorts of oversight hearings as well as my oversight visits to federal facilities within my committee jurisdiction. I take my role as your representative immensely seriously and center your best interests in all that I do. As your representative, I've tirelessly represented and delivered for Texas 16. Please consider= If you want to keep getting clear, fact-based breakdowns of the issues affecting our community, make sure you stay connected and share this with someone who should be paying attention, too. body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26-pan [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26-pan]
Friend, the midterms are around the corner, and they may be the most important elections of our lifetime.
As Attorney General, my team and I have been in court fighting to hold the Trump administration accountable to the law — filing more than 80 lawsuits, protecting billions in federal funding, and securing more than 65 court orders blocking illegal conduct.
We’ve held the line (and will continue to do so!), but the courts can only do so much in the fight for accountability and justice.
If we want to stop Trump’s illegal takeover of our federal government, we also need to win Democratic majorities in Congress. Between now and November, I’ll be highlighting some great Democrats in tough races across California who need our support — starting with my friend, Dr. Richard Pan.
Dr. Richard Pan is running to flip California’s 6th Congressional District. It’s one of the most competitive races in the state, and I’m proud to support him.
Will you split a donation of $20 between our campaigns to help make sure we both win this November? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26-pan]
As a pediatrician, Dr. Pan spent his career caring for thousands of children and their families. He co-founded a nonprofit that helped 65,000 children get health coverage, and in the state legislature, he helped cut the number of uninsured Californians by more than half.
When the Disneyland measles outbreak put thousands of children and their families at risk and overwhelmed local doctors' offices, Dr. Pan jumped into action. He introduced legislation to ensure every child could safely attend school, all while RFK Jr. and the anti-vaccine movement spread misinformation, made threats, and targeted his family.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26-pan [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26-pan]
But Dr. Pan didn’t back down. Instead, he stood with parents, doctors, and public health leaders — and together, they won. As a result, vaccination rates went up, schools were safer, and our state hasn’t had a major measles outbreak since.
Now that RFK Jr. is using his platform within the Trump administration to spread more misinformation and put even more families at risk, Dr. Pan is exactly the kind of leader we need in Washington: one who has experience taking on MAGA Republicans, and who will fight back against extremists in Congress who are working to rip away healthcare from millions of Americans.
Dr. Pan is the experienced fighter and public health leader we need in Congress, and right now he could use your help to make sure he has the resources he needs to win. Will you chip in to support Dr. Pan’s campaign and mine today? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26-pan]

Hi - Matt Maasdam here reaching out to say a HUGE ‘Thank You’. Unfortunately, the result on Tuesday evening wasn’t what we wanted, and we came up short. But I have nothing but gratitude for all of you for being part of the Team. Thousands of people volunteered their time, made phone calls, knocked doors, dropped food off at our offices, made contributions, and provided all kinds of support for what was officially the biggest Team sport I’ve ever played. I wanted to share an excerpt from my statement on election night with you all:
* _From day one this campaign was about nothing other than service to my country. America is the greatest country in the world. It was an honor to fight for it. I’m grateful for the opportunity to throw my hat in the ring and participate in our democracy._
* _I got into this race because I know our country can be doing better than we are right now. And that’s what we heard from voters tonight. Voters told us that they’re sick of seeing no accountability for Donald Trump when he violates the Constitution. They feel like stuff costs way too much, and Tom Barrett and Donald Trump made it worse. And they want corruption out of politics. No more politicians taking care of themselves over the country._
* _And now, we turn to the real mission: beating Tom Barrett in the fall. I look forward to doing everything in my power to make that happen, and help flip the House blue._

This morning I attended the Michigan Democratic Party’s Unity breakfast, where candidates from up and down the ballot gathered to pledge our support for the ticket this fall. I once again congratulated Will Lawrence and let him know I’m on the Team – because we’re not going to stand by and let Donald Trump and Tom Barrett hang on to this seat in MI-07. **If you’re in Michigan, I hope you’ll join some of the other upcoming unity events to turn our attention to November and the mission at hand:**
* **[Detroit rally](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMYKt_PNbTZJM77xb-PM80u4CJaGJ31ZVUC6o4pf1WSYh5giIg6dqVS72XkZ7MRpC4GLOx0F5L8aJGHuSRY_CZYENrmLex1r3nqfh4E9G_OD59c44_IpZB8zWOv4f6KkzyNMcFMXVYptZf1wwlJzdt-D1B2UU-kZTYj5Gzygb9b1O4F0sOJzJCB4_NHdW_IA6ZHRBsQrdxb11eQzfUUcR6zhmRaDf9B0Q7qtIcj8XDgPeRSR-KUJhpc5JM-bpd5D80P4p779pqFoiJcfA5kyDc7w/4sz/EInMs53cSD-IU7gZW_YTZg/h2/h001.1c6vKl8tsY25lFUY7-BV0TiyzlFrTs7CBEA45gijwIk) on Friday, August 7, at 5:00 pm - General Election Kickoff w/ the Ticket: Abdul El-Sayed, Jocelyn Benson, Garlin Gilchrist & Eli Savit, and special guest Pete Buttigieg**
* **[East Lansing - CD7 Post-Primary Unity Event](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.yjJN_MEbNx94PLaWzZ6hWwGamPY7W-vS4bGbFoLcGE_goybYzUFubWM_2Su_UtRTCfxNDbzwsriPOhq0gyQuOK8RoiZI-hdCB_0HUM-x_fCNidxd3J3fYH2_bPROD31fnNbaT8c7TDLzfNgJLiA_eN1aMDeg1kLiRHsqbroDboDE_YZjYG-DXl31jWJiloToETTV9BHluAmlNVwJsUtGFL7wS7VtW9ocVUlP17Y1kUNZYWvPAff7VOIwHgkIMjew_Tvw4pIPCOH1IYF5zsPjGIGTwGfoC8vQ4WfXpMMi-ILD_yPcW9zLmW_CYGDCKA5F-SijeMA0qT6CcenGcE-SamS-VW3R6YHkGV_BsZDmqlYcpTxRNZ5OKVwCAMyhVkIB/4sz/EInMs53cSD-IU7gZW_YTZg/h3/h001.qSLL2YgHxjDIoc9a2AbMZBz8jIcjKTTeAJfiwzhQHdw) on Saturday, August 8 at 4:00 pm**

I got into this race because I know our country can be doing better than we are right now. And that’s what we heard from voters tonight. Voters told us that they’re sick of seeing no accountability for Donald Trump when he violates the Constitution. subject: The GOP is winning at fundraising
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Sara Jacobs for Congress
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25]
Hi friends — did you see this headline from Axios ?
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=10 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=10]
House Republicans are outraising us this summer, and these numbers will impact the work we’re able to do in the months ahead.
(I have a lot more to say about this, but if that’s all you need to hear, click here to make a contribution before our next deadline so we can catch up to the GOP’s fundraising and get ready to win in November.) [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=10]
In the wake of the most recent FEC filings, it’s clear that House Republicans have been raking in serious cash. And while I remain optimistic about our chances at winning a House majority in November, this trend genuinely worries me — because money directly translates to our ability to reach voters, run ads, and organize on the ground.
On top of all that, California’s new congressional maps made my own race a bit more competitive, by about 4-5 points. My team and I have been working hard to make sure we’re reaching voters all over the district these last few months, including the newly added areas.
We’ve also been mapping out all the ways we can continue to support other great Democratic candidates around the country who are working to hold their seats or flip red seats blue.
I’m also thinking beyond November. Flipping the House is the urgent, immediate goal — but it’s not the only one. At the rate this administration is creating chaos and destroying our democracy, House Democrats need to be ready to show up on day one to rebuild what’s been destroyed. And we need to start seeding the ground now to build towards a Democratic trifecta in 2029, so we deliver a better, bolder vision for what comes next.
To do all that, Democratic incumbents like me are going to have to step up our fundraising efforts. Winning a majority will require an all-hands-on-deck approach and a lot of resources, especially with this news about the House GOP’s latest fundraising numbers.
August is a tough fundraising month, but we can’t afford to miss any goals this close to the election, so I’m hoping this team will give what you can. Will you pitch in $10 or whatever amount you can to my re-election campaign today? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=10]

DONATE $100 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?express_lane=true&amount=100] OTHER AMOUNT [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em]
I’m all in on this — winning re-election, supporting Democratic challengers and incumbents, retaking the House majority, and setting Democrats up for more success in the future. I know we can do it if we roll up our sleeves and get to work. Thank you for being a part of that effort.
-Sara

Peter — When it comes to Florida’s soaring utility bills, I’m often asked: _"How would you lower my costs as Attorney General?"_ It's a fair question, and the answer starts with understanding how this actually works. Your utility bills don't go up on their own. They go up through Tallahassee. State government sets the rules, and the Public Service Commission is the body that approves every single rate increase. Most of us live in areas served by the giant utilities that lobby heavily in Tallahassee, and over the last few decades, our light bills have gone _up, and up, and up._ As Attorney General, **I will intervene on our behalf to fight rate increases and argue for rate reductions before the Public Service Commission. And when utilities unfairly bill Florida families, I'll investigate and bring legal action to recover that money.** That's not some radical idea. It's the work Attorneys General do across the country. But here in Florida, we have the opposite: an Attorney General who serves the special interests in Tallahassee instead of the people paying the bills. Right now, roughly half the state — _families and businesses served by Florida Power & Light_ — is facing **$7 billion in rate increases.** And James Uthmeier hasn't lifted a finger to stop it. **[We need an Attorney General who will fight for us, not against us. Every year we go without one, the utilities get bolder, the rate hikes get bigger, and Florida families fall further behind. I'm running to put an end to that. | Peter,

[A Kansas court just permanently struck down a long list of abortion restrictions](https://click.everyaction.com/k/136818837/638699347/2141984067?sourceid=1151522&utm_campaign=27emaus-0801aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=kansas&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MzU1MzFmMC04NTkyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=kBY8giEl4EomNIBJ9sNcw8seajrT-yJHTJeRG24KvEQ=&emci=575531f0-8592-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=635531f0-8592-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=954237)—including a law that forced doctors to tell patients a false, dangerous claim: that medication abortion can be "reversed."

This win didn't happen by chance. [It happened because people like you make it possible for the Center for Reproductive Rights to fight these laws in court, year after year, case after case.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/136818838/638699348/2141984067?sourceid=1151522&utm_campaign=27emaus-0801aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=kansas&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MzU1MzFmMC04NTkyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=kBY8giEl4EomNIBJ9sNcw8seajrT-yJHTJeRG24KvEQ=&emci=575531f0-8592-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=635531f0-8592-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=954237) | [Fund Our Victories](https://click.everyaction.com/k/136818839/638699349/2141984067?sourceid=1151522&utm_campaign=27emaus-0801aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=kansas&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MzU1MzFmMC04NTkyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=kBY8giEl4EomNIBJ9sNcw8seajrT-yJHTJeRG24KvEQ=&emci=575531f0-8592-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=635531f0-8592-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=954237)

Kansans voted in 2022 to protect abortion rights in their state constitution. Politicians tried to override that vote anyway. The courts—with your support behind them—held the line. [This is what's possible when you power the Center for Reproductive Rights. Will you donate today to keep this momentum going?](https://click.everyaction.com/k/136818840/638699350/2141984067?sourceid=1151522&utm_campaign=27emaus-0801aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=kansas&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MzU1MzFmMC04NTkyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=kBY8giEl4EomNIBJ9sNcw8seajrT-yJHTJeRG24KvEQ=&emci=575531f0-8592-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=635531f0-8592-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=954237)

---
For nearly three years, these restrictions delayed care, violated patient privacy, and forced doctors to lie to the people they treat. Dr. Traci Nauser, the lead plaintiff and an OB-GYN with almost 30 years of experience, said it best: [these laws interfered with her ability to do her job and give patients care based on facts, not politics.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/136818842/638699352/2141984067?sourceid=1151522&utm_campaign=27emaus-0801aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=kansas&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MzU1MzFmMC04NTkyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=kBY8giEl4EomNIBJ9sNcw8seajrT-yJHTJeRG24KvEQ=&emci=575531f0-8592-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=635531f0-8592-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=954237)

Today, that interference ends. [Kansas providers can finally treat patients the way they were trained to: with honesty and compassion, not scripted misinformation and forced delays.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/136818843/638699353/2141984067?sourceid=1151522&utm_campaign=27emaus-0801aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=kansas&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MzU1MzFmMC04NTkyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=kBY8giEl4EomNIBJ9sNcw8seajrT-yJHTJeRG24KvEQ=&emci=575531f0-8592-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=635531f0-8592-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=954237)

In this fight together,

Alice Wang

name: Zohran Mamdani
subject: I would like to tell you about some unsolicited advice I got before I was sworn in.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Zohran for NYC 2029**
body:
The only expectation I seek to reset is that of small expectations.
#
A few months ago, as I was preparing to be sworn in as Mayor, I received some unsolicited advice about what I should say in my Inaugural Address.
I was told that this would be the occasion for me to reset expectations. That I should use the opportunity to encourage the people of New York to ask for little and expect even less.
But I did no such thing — because that’s not why I ran for Mayor. Today and every day, I want to reaffirm to you that _the only expectation I seek to reset is that of small expectations._
With you by my side, I will keep uplifting the needs, hopes, and dreams of everyday people. We may not always succeed. **But never will we be accused of lacking the courage to try.**
The powerful movement we’ve built together is about improving working people’s lives. It’s about organizing for progress today so that we can build a better, more affordable tomorrow. That is the work I am asking you to be a part of right now:
**[Will you sign up today to join this movement and help reset expectations for the better?](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22956?t=1&akid=1703%2E2118727%2EGNBqBk)**
Thank you,
Zohran

My thoughts on why I ran | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136818967/638699844/-1967260412?refcode=8.07.26_rs_fr_machine&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODY2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4YjhmODhhNC04NjkyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1QRJN1z1gpDfEZzcsWshchGrhe1omJHGPCg0ehTKrGU=)
---
Peter, Paige here — I wanted to tell you about why I ran for mayor of Scranton. It’s an important part of my story, and key to understanding how this race will decide the future of NEPA. I ran for mayor because I couldn’t raise my family in a place where government corruption is okay. **Corruption was not a theory here; the last Mayor was indicted for extortion.** Enough was enough. That’s why I ran as an Independent and launched the campaign that became known as Paige Against the Machine. I left labels at the door because this was never about party politics. It was about cleaning up a system that rewarded cronies, hid waste, and put private gain ahead of the public good. **I ran to make government work for our kids, our families, and our small businesses, not for insiders.** Running against the local machine was hard. It meant standing up to powerful interests and to people who expected the status quo to continue. But I believed then, as I believe now, that we deserve leaders who are accountable, honest, and focused on results. **We won because people across our city decided they had had enough.** They wanted a government that was practical, not transactional. If you believe our public institutions should serve the public, not the powerful, I hope you’ll stand with me as we keep building that vision in Congress. clean_body: My thoughts on why I ran | = Peter, Paige here — I wanted to tell you about why I ran for mayor of Scranton. It’s an important part of my story, and key to understanding how this race will decide the future of NEPA. I ran for mayor because I couldn’t raise my family in a place where government corruption is okay. Corruption was not a theory here; the last Mayor was indicted for extortion. Enough was enough. That’s why I ran as an Independent and launched the campaign that became known as Paige Against the Machine. I left labels at the door because this was never about party politics. It was about cleaning up a system that rewarded cronies, hid waste, and put private gain ahead of the public good. I ran to make government work for our kids, our families, and our small businesses, not for insiders. Running against the local machine was hard. It meant standing up to powerful interests and to people who expected the status quo to continue. But I believed then, as I believe now, that we deserve leaders who are accountable, honest, and focused on results. We won because people across our city decided they had had enough. They wanted a government that was practical, not transactional. # [Musk's SpaceX climbs 2% despite earnings drop and lockup](https://substack.com/redirect/9615288a-7fdd-4415-a5f1-9ab1dbd78762?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
SpaceX shares **[advanced about 2% this week after a 13.6% post-earnings plunge](https://substack.com/redirect/ce1a612b-99f0-4aba-ba7f-a0ce5e07049b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on AI capital spending of $15.8 billion and a 6.1% rebound as 911.5 million shares unlocked for the first time.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/aa5e47e6-f6a7-41a2-802f-3b9330901029?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Earnings CapEx drives selloff:** Second-quarter results topped estimates for revenue and adjusted EBITDA, yet AI capital expenditures ballooning to $15.8 billion from $7.7 billion **[triggered a 13.6% drop to a new all-time closing low.](https://substack.com/redirect/7ecef9cf-7804-4dbf-b08a-212b48a023d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* **Lockup unlock bucks trend:** Thursday's first and largest of nine staggered unlocks freed 911.5 million shares, about 43% more than the 638.9 million IPO float, lifting the public float to 11.8% from 4.9%, with shares closing 6.1% higher.
* **Tesla batteries power centers:** SpaceX **[purchased $295 million of Tesla Megapacks](https://substack.com/redirect/e6b02b38-946c-42b0-aa3a-f5468d5fcc88?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in the second quarter for a half-year total of $329 million to help power its Colossus AI data centers in Greater Memphis.
* **Musk sets power goals:** On the earnings call Musk stated a tentative target of 20 gigawatts of power and cooling online by the end of next year, expecting something close to 15 gigawatts at the plant level.

* **Abatement fund details:** Of the $567 million, $420 million funds treatment for those harmed by the platforms while the rest supports awareness, prevention, screening, assessment, referrals and evaluation of the response.
* **Age verification upgrades:** Meta must improve age assurance models and tools with AI, attempt to develop a dedicated under-13 prediction model within two years, and partner with schools for underage reporting portals.
* **Teen usage safeguards:** The order **[imposes monthly limits on teen Facebook and Instagram use,](https://substack.com/redirect/2071dd14-97ce-4094-8cfd-9fc27e4e2ead?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** notification restrictions, tighter adult contact controls, AI chatbot safeguards and enhanced child sexual abuse report reviews over five years.
* **Responses from parties:** Meta plans to appeal while stating confidence in its teen protections; Attorney General Raul Torrez called the ruling a blueprint that holds the company accountable for harms to children.

# [SpaceX plans massive 20-gigawatt buildout for AI energy needs](https://substack.com/redirect/9615288a-7fdd-4415-a5f1-9ab1dbd78762?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Elon Musk said **[SpaceX aims for as much as 20 gigawatts of power, cooling and electrical infrastructure](https://substack.com/redirect/bfc3ae50-c92d-46c8-9313-93837d059084?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** by the end of next year for AI hyperscaler ambitions, a clear positive for suppliers.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/aa5e47e6-f6a7-41a2-802f-3b9330901029?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Clear positive signal given:** James West of Melius Research said SpaceX commentary on power got attention and marks a clear positive for equipment suppliers supporting the AI boom.
* **Massive capacity plans set:** Musk expects 2 gigawatts of compute available now with plans for 10 gigawatts online by end of next year while targeting 20 gigawatts of power equipment.
* **Even conservative outlook noted:** Musk noted that even if forecasts fall short the company should still reach around 15 gigawatts of capacity at the power plant level by end of 2027.
* **Key industrial names benefit:** Companies set to benefit include GE Vernova and Baker Hughes for turbines plus power providers Constellation Energy, NextEra Energy, Vistra and EQT Corporation.

# [Google Cloud surges 82% as top AI talent flees](https://substack.com/redirect/9615288a-7fdd-4415-a5f1-9ab1dbd78762?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Google reported 82% second-quarter cloud growth while chief scientist Jeff Dean left after 27 years and Demis Hassabis stepped down as DeepMind CEO, **[underscoring tensions between commercial success and retaining frontier AI researchers.](https://substack.com/redirect/c78db159-5044-441e-b5a7-7fb1468c9ac4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/aa5e47e6-f6a7-41a2-802f-3b9330901029?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Talent exit wave hits:** Jeff Dean left with Sanjay Ghemawat, Oriol Vinyals and Quoc Le to launch Discovery Loop, a Google-backed firm aiming to automate machine learning science and engineering.
* **All transformer authors gone:** All eight authors of the 2017 Attention Is All You Need paper left Google including Noam Shazeer who joined OpenAI in June after nearly $3 billion return deal.
* **Internal compute access friction:** Researchers grow frustrated over scarce computing capacity for ambitious projects while Google Cloud sells TPUs to outside firms like Anthropic according to people familiar.
* **DeepMind leadership roles shift:** Demis Hassabis moves to chairman and Alphabet chief scientist for longer-term work as Koray Kavukcuoglu takes daily management of the unit and next Gemini model.

# [SK Hynix pours $38.1 billion into new AI memory plants](https://substack.com/redirect/9615288a-7fdd-4415-a5f1-9ab1dbd78762?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
SK Hynix will invest 54 trillion Korean won or **[$38.1 billion to build two new memory chip plants](https://substack.com/redirect/9a8c5471-1450-4853-9919-e8e9ccc0eb45?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as AI-driven demand for high-bandwidth memory drives surging prices and supply shortages.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/aa5e47e6-f6a7-41a2-802f-3b9330901029?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Major plant investment split:** The firm earmarked 35.2 trillion won for Yongin Y2 DRAM fab and 19.1 trillion won for Cheongju M17 NAND plant as part of capacity expansion.
* **Construction timelines confirmed now:** Yongin Y2 breaks ground in July 2027 with cleanroom opening June 2029 for HBM while Cheongju starts February 2027 and opens December 2028.
* **Samsung market share pressure:** Samsung reclaimed the number one DRAM market share in second quarter per Counterpoint Research leading SK Hynix to expand for 2029 production and beyond.
* **Memory prices remain firm:** Multi vendor capacity expansions grow supply through 2028 yet demand rises faster so prices unlikely to soften before end of 2028 according to analysis.

# [Chinese robot maker Unitree hits eye-watering $9B valuation in IPO](https://substack.com/redirect/9615288a-7fdd-4415-a5f1-9ab1dbd78762?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Chinese humanoid robot maker Unitree priced its Shanghai initial public offering at 150.8 yuan per share on Thursday,[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/8712a5fc-d658-42da-9f08-bac8b3d2197e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[valuing the firm at around $9.04 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/8712a5fc-d658-42da-9f08-bac8b3d2197e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as the first mainland-listed humanoid robot company.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/aa5e47e6-f6a7-41a2-802f-3b9330901029?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Share sale structure set:** The Hangzhou-based company is selling 40.45 million new shares or 10% of its enlarged share capital on Shanghai's STAR Market seeking to raise 6.1 billion yuan.
* **Strategic investor role confirmed:** Chinese AI company DeepSeek is among the strategic investors in Unitree's IPO according to the Thursday filing submitted to the Shanghai Stock Exchange.
* **Revenue growth details shared:** Overall revenue more than quadrupled to 1.7 billion yuan in 2025 with humanoid robots generating 867.8 million yuan in sales and overtaking four-legged robots.
* **U.S. sales exposure noted:** U.S. sales accounted for 13.3% of Unitree's revenue last year and tariffs limits or lost approvals could hurt overseas growth and disrupt supplies.

* * *
* * *
# [DeepSeek drops $20.8M into Unitree's $9B Shanghai IPO](https://substack.com/redirect/9615288a-7fdd-4415-a5f1-9ab1dbd78762?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Chinese AI startup DeepSeek invested 140.8 million yuan or **[$20.8 million in robot maker Unitree and agreed to jointly develop AI models](https://substack.com/redirect/44c02b75-60e8-4907-b7a6-a683869c8961?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for humanoid machines, a stock-exchange filing showed.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/aa5e47e6-f6a7-41a2-802f-3b9330901029?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Share allocation size set:** DeepSeek received 933399 Unitree shares representing 2.31% of the shares allocated through the Shanghai initial public offering strategic placement.
* **Partnership collaboration plan:** The companies both based in Hangzhou said they would combine DeepSeek's expertise in AI models with Unitree's work in mechanical engineering motion control and embodied intelligence.
* **Mutual preference terms listed:** Unitree would give preference to DeepSeek when procuring model-training services and DeepSeek would similarly favor Unitree when purchasing robots or exploring applications.
* **Targeted development goal set:** The partnership targets a key bottleneck for humanoid developers of building a robot brain capable of understanding surroundings and turning instructions into physical actions.

* * *
* * *
# [Whitmer-backed $292M program accused of funding wrong people](https://substack.com/redirect/9615288a-7fdd-4415-a5f1-9ab1dbd78762?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Michigan's $291.9 million Rx Kids program for pregnant women and new mothers, backed by Gov. Gretchen Whitmer,[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/a1285106-e477-4206-82d5-18958f507092?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[is listed as guaranteed income in the state TANF plan](https://substack.com/redirect/a1285106-e477-4206-82d5-18958f507092?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** while the program denies the label.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/aa5e47e6-f6a7-41a2-802f-3b9330901029?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Program payment details given:** Rx Kids provides pregnant women $1500 and $500 monthly for six or 12 months after birth with no income test or spending restrictions in communities.
* **Official classification conflict:** The Michigan TANF State Plan effective January 1 defines guaranteed-income payments as regular cash with no conditions and explicitly names RX Kids as an example.
* **Low spending so far:** As of June 2 about $10.8 million of nearly $292 million in public appropriations had been spent with 85% going directly to families.
* **No spending oversight exists:** Founder Dr. Mona Hanna said the program does no monitoring of purchases because it is built on trust in mothers and families to meet needs.

* * *
* * *
# [$18.3B welfare loophole still bankrolling parents who shouldn't qualify](https://substack.com/redirect/9615288a-7fdd-4415-a5f1-9ab1dbd78762?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nearly **[30 years after Congress banned illegal aliens from welfare,](https://substack.com/redirect/d08763a3-abd5-4d7b-8628-1cb2838880f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** $18.3 billion in cash assistance has flowed to households with an ineligible parent through the child-only TANF loophole that remains open.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/aa5e47e6-f6a7-41a2-802f-3b9330901029?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Recent spending scale shown:** In fiscal year 2024 those cases accounted for nearly $760 million roughly 9% of all TANF basic-assistance spending with more than 85200 families collecting.
* **How the loophole works:** Eligible child is listed as the beneficiary while the parent receives and controls the payment avoiding work mandates and the 60-month lifetime benefit limit.
* **California dominates totals now:** California accounted for $617 million paid to nearly 60000 households or 81% of the national total for these cases.
* **Call for state action made:** Foundation for Government Accountability urges states to change their own eligibility rules via block grants since Congress left the child-only path open.

| | **In 72 Hours, September 16 Swung From Leaning-Toward-Hold Back to a Possible Hike. The Energy Reversal Handed the Three Dissenters Exactly the Supply Shock They Warned About. Here Is What It Means for Your Rates.**
---
| | The energy reversal this week has direct consequences for the September 16 Fed decision. On Wednesday, with Brent below $79 on the interim proposal, a September hold looked to be strengthening — energy disinflation pulling the August 14 CPI toward 3.7% and weakening the three dissenters’ argument. By Friday, with Brent back above $83 on Iran’s restrictive draft and multi-front supply fears, that dynamic has fully reversed. **An inflationary impulse from energy, explicitly noted by the bond market selling off, is precisely the environment in which Hammack, Kashkari, and Logan’s case for an immediate hike gains strength.**
---
| | The three dissenters argued on July 29 that five years of above-target inflation cannot be cured by one good CPI print, and that energy and supply-chain pressures posed ongoing upside risk. Friday’s events — a restrictive Iranian Hormuz draft, Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure, Russian refinery outages — validate that argument in real time. **For the American investor in or near retirement, the practical consequence is that a September hike would push the 30-year Treasury from 5.193% toward 5.4–5.5%, raising mortgage rates and compressing REIT and utility valuations.** The favorable portfolio scenario of midweek — energy disinflation enabling a Fed hold that keeps rates stable — has receded. The defensive position remains the capital-light and near-term-visible AI names whose cash flows are less sensitive to the long-rate discount.

https://rokhanna.com [https://rokhanna.com]
Peter,
Campaign donations should help elect leaders—not help politicians escape accountability.
Right now, federal candidates and officeholders can use campaign contributions and legal-defense funds to fight sexual misconduct claims, pay settlements, and even hire investigators to dig into accusers.
That creates a culture of impunity in Washington. It gives powerful politicians an extraordinary legal advantage—and leaves survivors facing campaign war chests built with donor money.
No one contributes to a campaign so their donation can be used to intimidate an accuser or cover the costs of alleged misconduct.
That’s why I’ve partnered with Representative Anna Paulina Luna to introduce [https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/07/28/unlikely-duo-seeks-ban-using-campaign-funds-fight-sexual-harassment-claims/] the bipartisan No Campaign Funded Cover-Ups Act.
Our bill would prohibit federal politicians from using political funds for legal expenses, settlements, judgments, or investigations connected to claims of sexual assault, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment.

Thank you for helping Rep. Bera reach his end-of-month fundraising goal!

Every day, Ami is fighting for his constituents. And he always meets the moment — introducing measures to safeguard a woman’s right to choose, championing bills that will improve the lives of every American, and standing up to harmful actions taken by the Trump administration.

We wanted to make sure you are up to date with his work. A bill introduced by Dr. Bera and his Congressional Doctors Caucus would increase protections for the professionals who provide legal abortion care nationwide. → **Ami is fighting to accelerate lifesaving pediatric cancer research.** The bipartisan _Accelerating Innovation in Medicine for Kids with Cancer Act_ would leverage cutting-edge AI and data tools to improve pediatric cancer research, strengthen clinical trials, and help deliver more personalized treatment options for young patients. → **He’s pushing back against the president’s election denialism.** Rep. Peter, it's David Hogg with one more victory to report before the weekend. 🎉
**Last night, Representative Justin J. Pearson won his primary in TN-09 — and this win is _so much bigger_ than just one race.**
At Donald Trump’s request, Tennessee’s GOP-controlled legislature redistricted TN-09 back in May, _completely dismantling the state’s only majority Black and Democratic-held seat._
That blatant Republican power grab came on the heels of SCOTUS’ decision to gut the remainder of the Voting Rights Act earlier this year — leaving folks in majority-Black Memphis with diluted voting power.
But last night, on the 61st anniversary of the VRA’s passage, Justin got one step closer to Congress anyway.
**At Leaders We Deserve, we’ve been incredibly proud to back Justin in his fight to bring clean air and water, affordable healthcare, and lower utility bills to his community. And we’re not done yet, Peter.**

Peter,
In a few days, voters in Wisconsin’s 7th District will walk into the booth and decide who they trust to represent Northern Wisconsin in Congress.
For me, this race comes down to three things: accessible health care, affordability, and clean government.
I’ve spent my life working in the forests and communities of this state, and I’ve seen what happens when health care is too far away or too expensive, when small towns lose good jobs, and what we all lose when members of Congress answer to the powerful instead of answering to us. That’s what I’m running to change.
The endorsements I have earned from former members of Congress, state and local leaders, educators, and community members show we have a serious coalition behind this campaign. But what matters most right now is whether you and your neighbors in Park Falls, Rhinelander, Hayward, Superior and Wausau know that there’s a choice on the ballot that puts us all first.
I am running to be the Congressman for All of Us. If you share this vision and want it to be on every screen and in every mailbox we can reach, I’m asking you to invest in these final hours.
Will you chip in $25, $50, or whatever is meaningful for you before August 11? You’ll help us hit the ground running on August 12 with a campaign that showed up for every voter we could reach.

But what matters most right now is whether you and your neighbors in Park Falls, Rhinelander, Hayward, Superior and Wausau know that there’s a choice on the ballot that puts us all first. I am running to be the Congressman for All of Us. If you share this vision and want it to be on every screen and in every mailbox we can reach, I’m asking you to invest in these final hours. Will you chip in $25, $50, or whatever is meaningful for you before August 11? You’ll help us hit the ground running on August 12 with a campaign that showed up for every voter we could reach. Chip in now → [] If you’ve already been a supporter or a volunteer, THANK YOU for everything you’ve already done. Let’s finish this primary the right way and let’s do it together. Onward!
