Matt Little and Kaela Berg at a January debate at Carleton College. Photo: YouTube.
Four super PACs with ties to AIPAC and Democratic Majority for Israel have surged into a Minnesota House race in the final months of the campaign, hoping to fend off the latest progressive insurgent.
In the three-way race, one candidate, Matt Klein, is unapologetically supportive of Israel, while two others, Matt Little and Kaela Berg, have been critics to varying degrees. Little, however, has the support of the group A New Policy, which was founded to support pro-Palestinian candidates and lobby Congress against Israeli interests. Another PAC, called American Priorities, which was organized to be a counterweight to AIPAC, [has jumped into the race](https://substack.com/redirect/9330f5f7-accc-44ab-bbd7-875a11d4e459?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to support Little with a spend of some $60,000.
314 Action, a super PAC ostensibly organized to support scientists and medical professionals, [this week reported spending nearly $2.5 million](https://substack.com/redirect/eac6aad8-04cf-4849-9439-467b69ed0ecf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) supporting Klein, a staggering amount in a previously sleepy race, given that the PAC has raised just $15 million for the full cycle. (A spokesperson for 314 insists none of the funds have come from AIPAC or its allied organizations.)
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZHJvcHNpdGVuZXdzLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.Z5Q-DqzO-lxeGp6yxu0VXc6Iw4ZkBIbelpGlAHKrxlw?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=210246671)
In a strategy that has been deployed in other races, the pro-Israel money is boosting Klein, the pro-Israel candidate, while other PACs with ties to AIPAC are boosting the alternative progressive candidate who is trailing in the polls, hoping to draw votes away from Little.
The race was reshaped on May 9, when Little won the endorsement of the Minnesota Democratic Farmers and Labor Party. On May 1, [AIPAC's super PAC had transferred ](https://substack.com/redirect/b5269c1b-c6aa-4560-9416-7ae1f3d9e5fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)$350,000 to EDW Action Fund, followed by $100,000 on May 10 and another $400,000 on May 20, money that would soon end up in the Minnesota race. (EDW did not respond to requests for clarification on why the money was moved and where it was ultimately spent.)
Little released an internal survey conducted between May 18 and 20, which found him well ahead, taking 41% of the vote, with Berg and Klein far behind in a statistical tie for second, with Berg at 13% and Klein at 11%. A little more than a week later, Klein fielded his own poll, which found Little at 26%, only 7 points over Klein's 19%. Berg was in third with 16%. The largest group of the 403 likely voters surveyed in the poll, 39%, said they "don't know" who they'd vote for. While Klein's internal poll demonstrates that Little was firmly the frontrunner in the race two months before election day, it was conducted before the surge in outside spending began.
The congressional seat is being vacated by Democrat Angie Craig, who is running for Senate. The primary is on Tuesday.
Given the numbers, the path to victory for Klein was clear: He needed Little to be brought down by boosting Berg--splitting the vote between the two progressives--and needed big money to get himself past both of them.
In stepped the PACs organized to support women, which were funded by AIPAC and DMFI. EDW Action [spent](https://substack.com/redirect/49131250-55bd-4190-8f87-3bb301bc3d10?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) roughly $395,000 supporting Berg between June 26 and August 3. Of the $395,000 burned, $99,999 came directly from EDW and $295,000 came from its sister organization called Pro-Choice Majority Action, a hybrid PAC recently formed on May 1 as a legal affiliate of EDW Action. EDW [transferred $626,000 and $100,000](https://substack.com/redirect/584d99e5-24c7-495c-afd8-e29ca878c8f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Pro-Choice Majority Action on May 21 and May 22 respectively, on the two days after receiving the final batch of AIPAC's $850,000 dump, and sent another $150,000 a week later on May 29, helping to enable Pro-Choice Majority's ensuing spend on Berg's behalf and more.
Moving money between multiple PACs before spending it doesn't necessarily make it much harder to trace, but it does make it more confusing for voters and local reporters covering the race. AIPAC, for its part, [accuses reporters](https://substack.com/redirect/c36d01b4-d8ce-4e22-85b9-b511dbfa9be3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of antisemitism for following AIPAC money through the FEC files toward its final destination. Candidates like Little risk being called conspiracy theorists when they point to the clear source of the money. Indeed, after Drop Site reached out to Berg's campaign for comment, Berg [posted a video on X](https://substack.com/redirect/12b51b42-f8e5-4ea6-8b0a-d37c00a958cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) accusing Little of lying about her and insisting that she doesn't take AIPAC money: "I never have, and I never will."
It is true she has not taken AIPAC money directly, but on May 13, four days after Little won the DFL endorsement, DMFI transferred [$500,000](https://substack.com/redirect/468d21bb-6eb4-4ef5-a03b-b0e223d4d45c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Women Vote, the independent expenditure arm of EMILY's List, a pro-choice PAC. Then, less than a month later, Women Vote [spent $584,448 in independent expenditures](https://substack.com/redirect/3ebc556e-af07-47bc-8900-41ee31bc5666?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) supporting Berg.
"Women Vote works with a variety of partners to elect Democratic pro-choice women and build winning coalitions," a source familiar with Women Vote's spending told Drop Site. "The donation referenced was for a program in a different race and has nothing to do with Kaela Berg or this race."
Though the source did not disclose the recipient of the $500,000, Women Vote did spend a total of $653,885 supporting Shannon Bird, a [DMFI-endorsee](https://substack.com/redirect/646ef38f-bd1b-4b1d-b761-b30e1ff08d76?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), in her unsuccessful bid to become the Democratic nominee in Colorado's 8th congressional district. Despite securing DMFI's endorsement, Bird, who ultimately lost to Manny Rutinel, [does not list the PACs support on her website](https://substack.com/redirect/942c3cee-e319-4996-8533-3d1051547b6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Nevertheless, the total dollars spent on Berg's behalf by PACs that have been used as pro-Israel passthroughs at some point, including Women Vote, amounts to $979,448 since June 11. Now, the fact that PACs linked to AIPAC are spending to boost Berg doesn't mean Berg herself is aware of the links, and doesn't mean pro-Israel donors affirmatively want Berg to win. DMFI, when reached for comment, rejected any involvement with Women Vote's support for Berg's campaign.
"DMFI PAC endorsed Matt Klein in this race. Kaela Berg's views are equally as anti-Israel as Matt Little's," a DMFI spokesperson told Drop Site.
Again, while it's true that Berg and Little share some of the same criticisms of Israel, the polls have Berg far behind, meaning that voters drawn from Little to Berg are a boost to Klein, DMFI's candidate.
A Berg spokesperson rejected any relation between these groups' spending in the race and the pro-Israel lobby's donations to the spenders.
"Matt Little agrees with Kaela on Israel and AIPAC, that's why AIPAC is funneling millions in dark money into this race at the 11th hour to support Matt Klein," the spokesperson told Drop Site. "As the only woman running for Congress, Kaela is proud to have the support of the same organizations that have supported Peggy Flanagan and every woman in the MN Congressional Delegation. The truth is, Benjamin Netanyahu continues to be a danger to the world and if she's elected to Congress, Kaela will do everything in her power to stop the genocide and Netanyahu's government."
Berg has earned support from three state senators, 28 of her colleagues in the Minnesota House of Representatives, and national progressive organizations like Our Revolution and End Citizens United. She has also received some support from D.C., racking up endorsements from Rep. Chris Deluzio, who [many speculate is eyeing a primary challenge](https://substack.com/redirect/5eee1ca9-0c30-43ff-885d-bc3e94c4436d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Sen. John Fetterman (D-Penn.) in 2028, and Rep. Val Hoyle (D-Ore.).
Aside from securing the coveted Minnesota DFL endorsement, Little has also picked up backing from the state's Attorney General Keith Ellison, and key figures within the existing progressive infrastructure in Congress. Rep. Greg Casar, chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, Rep. Pramila Jayapal, former CPC chair, and Rep. Maxwell Frost, one of CPC's vice chairs, have all publicly supported his candidacy.
The CPC's PAC is also supporting Little.
Klein, for his part, has also seen a flood of supportive outside spending. 314 Action Fund is a super PAC which backs candidates who are involved in science or medicine, but has [sometimes acted in the past ](https://substack.com/redirect/a95c2792-6648-41ac-bc97-0041ac5f2609?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)as an AIPAC passthrough. FEC records show that the super PAC [spent](https://substack.com/redirect/af046e72-4bb6-452a-b9c4-51e0d88ef9a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) $1,261,341 in independent expenditures backing Klein in four installments between July 20 and July 30. On August 5, 314 Action dropped another $1.2 million into the race.
The state senator has also received an additional $138,440 from 57 individual donors who have also given to AIPAC, UDP, or DMFI. All of the individual donations were [given on the same day](https://substack.com/redirect/2f018282-4f33-4e18-b41d-d933e6795f77?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), June 28, many divided in various increments amounting to the maximum $3,500 individual contribution each.
Among those individuals is James Sprayregen, who sits on the National Board of AIPAC and serves on the Board of Governors for the American Jewish Committee. Sprayregen contributed $129,500 to the pro-Israel groups and to Klein in three separate same-day installments amounting to $3,499.99, one cent below the legal maximum, possibly to avoid being classified as a max-out donor.
Also listed among the individual donors pooled by AIPAC on Klein's behalf are Jody Forchheimer, who gave $283,456 to pro-Israel PACs and $3,500 to Klein, and Gadi Maier, who gave $135,000 to pro-Israel PACs and $3,500 to Klein. Forchheimer is a Senior Legal Fellow at the Louis D. Brandeis Center, a pro-Israel legal organization fighting antisemitism cases, and publicly discussed her role in pro-Israel advocacy at the AIPAC policy conference in 2019. Maier is an Israeli-American tech entrepreneur who is founder and CEO of ID Handshake, the first and a current board member at Forter, a fraud prevention platform, and formerly served as CEO of both FraudSciences and FreeMonee.
When asked about 314 Action Fund backing Klein's campaign and an inquiry about the aforementioned prominent pro-Israel donors, the campaign manager provided a statement in response to the latter.
"Our campaign is powered by thousands of supporters from every background and every faith--because that's who we are, and that's who I've spent my career serving," Klein told Drop Site. "As a doctor, I've cared for Jewish families, Muslim families, Christian families, and families of no faith at all, and I've never once asked who they were before helping them. This campaign is no different. I'm proud of the support we've received from neighbors, community leaders, and working families of all denominations."
Addressing the first question, the spokesperson added, "You should talk with 314 about their funding. I have copied Eden from their team on this email."
The move was eyebrow-raising, as campaigns and independent expenditure groups are not allowed to coordinate campaign activity. Though it is not considered best practice for campaigns and independent expenditure arms to communicate at all, it is legal to discuss some information as long as it doesn't amount to coordination.
314 Action also received a $2.5 million donation from pro-Israel billionaire Michael Bloomberg on May 4, just months before its spending blitz in Minnesota. Whether Bloomberg's money is earmarked to the Klein race is unclear; it would be odd if so, as Berg is endorsed by the organization Everytown for Gun Safety, which Bloomberg founded and primarily finances. That would mean Bloomberg was spending against himself in the same race.
Joshua Morrow, 314 Action Fund's president, said in a statement that the group is not funneling pro-Israel PAC money into the race. "As we have said multiple times, 314 Action Fund has not taken money from AIPAC or its affiliated entities this cycle and we won't," Morrow said. "We have spent over $14.5 million supporting STEM candidates in 2026 and not a cent has come from AIPAC, UDP, DMFI or affiliated entities. Similarly, our investments in Dr. Matt Klein are not from AIPAC or affiliated entities, and any suggestion otherwise is false, sensationalized and reported without sources."
Still, Klein refuses to recognize the genocide in Gaza, instead broadly calling for a two-state solution. Berg and Little, backed by David Hogg's Leaders We Deserve, on the other hand, have publicly called it one. Little differentiates himself from Berg, however, in supporting a suspension on any further U.S. military aid to Israel, while the latter has [advocated for conditioning it](https://substack.com/redirect/6a98bfdb-f967-44af-8103-1dc92218ce22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). In a video posted Wednesday, she calls for an end "to all weapons sales to Israel," going further than she had previously.
Klein has racked up endorsements from 19 colleagues in the Minnesota state senate, but has not received any explicit endorsements from Washington. The two-term state senator has also faced some scandal in the race, having placed a $50 wager on Kalshi, a prediction market service, betting that he'd win the MN-02 primary, which ultimately led to an April 2026 fine and five-year ban from the platform. Klein introduced an ultimately unsuccessful bill in the state legislature in 2024 that would have weakened regulations on sports gambling, a highly profitable path for companies like Kalshi.

clean_body: Progressive Matt Little is getting hit from both sides as a flurry of PACs intervene in three-way Democratic primary. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more Progressive Matt Little is getting hit from both sides as a flurry of PACs intervene in three-way Democratic primary. | | and | Aug 7 | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Matt Little and Kaela Berg at a January debate at Carleton College. Photo: YouTube. Four super PACs with ties to AIPAC and Democratic Majority for Israel have surged into a Minnesota House race in the final months of the campaign, hoping to fend off the latest progressive insurgent. In the three-way race, one candidate, Matt Klein, is unapologetically supportive of Israel, while two others, Matt Little and Kaela Berg, have been critics to varying degrees. Little, however, has the support of the group A New Policy, which was founded to support pro-Palestinian candidates and lobby Congress against Israeli interests. Another PAC, called American Priorities, which was organized to be a counterweight to AIPAC, to support Little with a spend of some $60,000. 314 Action, a super PAC ostensibly organized to support scientists and medical professionals, supporting Klein, a staggering amount in a previously sleepy race, given that the PAC has raised just $15 million for the full cycle. (A spokesperson for 314 insists none of the funds have come from AIPAC or its allied organizations.) In a strategy that has been deployed in other races, the pro-Israel money is boosting Klein, the pro-Israel candidate, while other PACs with ties to AIPAC are boosting the alternative progressive candidate who is trailing in the polls, hoping to draw votes away from Little. The race was reshaped on May 9, when Little won the endorsement of the Minnesota Democratic Farmers and Labor Party. On May 1, to EDW Action Fund, followed by $100,000 on May 10 and another $400,000 on May 20, money that would soon end up in the Minnesota race. (EDW did not respond to requests for clarification on why the money was moved and where it was ultimately spent.) Little released an internal survey conducted between May 18 and 20, which found him well ahead, taking 41% of the vote, with Berg and Klein far behind in a statistical tie for second, with Berg at 13% and Klein at 11%. A little more than a week later, Klein fielded his own poll, which found Little at 26%, only 7 points over Klein's 19%. Berg was in third with 16%. The largest group of the 403 likely voters surveyed in the poll, 39%, said they "don't know" who they'd vote for. While Klein's internal poll demonstrates that Little was firmly the frontrunner in the race two months before election day, it was conducted before the surge in outside spending began. The congressional seat is being vacated by Democrat Angie Craig, who is running for Senate. The primary is on Tuesday. Given the numbers, the path to victory for Klein was clear: He needed Little to be brought down by boosting Berg--splitting the vote between the two progressives--and needed big money to get himself past both of them. In stepped the PACs organized to support women, which were funded by AIPAC and DMFI. EDW Action roughly $395,000 supporting Berg between June 26 and August 3. Of the $395,000 burned, $99,999 came directly from EDW and $295,000 came from its sister organization called Pro-Choice Majority Action, a hybrid PAC recently formed on May 1 as a legal affiliate of EDW Action. EDW to Pro-Choice Majority Action on May 21 and May 22 respectively, on the two days after receiving the final batch of AIPAC's $850,000 dump, and sent another $150,000 a week later on May 29, helping to enable Pro-Choice Majority's ensuing spend on Berg's behalf and more. Moving money between multiple PACs before spending it doesn't necessarily make it much harder to trace, but it does make it more confusing for voters and local reporters covering the race. AIPAC, for its part, of antisemitism for following AIPAC money through the FEC files toward its final destination. Candidates like Little risk being called conspiracy theorists when they point to the clear source of the money. Indeed, after Drop Site reached out to Berg's campaign for comment, Berg accusing Little of lying about her and insisting that she doesn't take AIPAC money: "I never have, and I never will." It is true she has not taken AIPAC money directly, but on May 13, four days after Little won the DFL endorsement, DMFI transferred to Women Vote, the independent expenditure arm of EMILY's List, a pro-choice PAC. Then, less than a month later, Women Vote supporting Berg. "Women Vote works with a variety of partners to elect Democratic pro-choice women and build winning coalitions," a source familiar with Women Vote's spending told Drop Site. "The donation referenced was for a program in a different race and has nothing to do with Kaela Berg or this race." Though the source did not disclose the recipient of the $500,000, Women Vote did spend a total of $653,885 supporting Shannon Bird, a , in her unsuccessful bid to become the Democratic nominee in Colorado's 8th congressional district. Despite securing DMFI's endorsement, Bird, who ultimately lost to Manny Rutinel, . Nevertheless, the total dollars spent on Berg's behalf by PACs that have been used as pro-Israel passthroughs at some point, including Women Vote, amounts to $979,448 since June 11. Now, the fact that PACs linked to AIPAC are spending to boost Berg doesn't mean Berg herself is aware of the links, and doesn't mean pro-Israel donors affirmatively want Berg to win. DMFI, when reached for comment, rejected any involvement with Women Vote's support for Berg's campaign. "DMFI PAC endorsed Matt Klein in this race. Kaela Berg's views are equally as anti-Israel as Matt Little's," a DMFI spokesperson told Drop Site. Again, while it's true that Berg and Little share some of the same criticisms of Israel, the polls have Berg far behind, meaning that voters drawn from Little to Berg are a boost to Klein, DMFI's candidate. A Berg spokesperson rejected any relation between these groups' spending in the race and the pro-Israel lobby's donations to the spenders. "Matt Little agrees with Kaela on Israel and AIPAC, that's why AIPAC is funneling millions in dark money into this race at the 11th hour to support Matt Klein," the spokesperson told Drop Site. "As the only woman running for Congress, Kaela is proud to have the support of the same organizations that have supported Peggy Flanagan and every woman in the MN Congressional Delegation. The truth is, Benjamin Netanyahu continues to be a danger to the world and if she's elected to Congress, Kaela will do everything in her power to stop the genocide and Netanyahu's government." Berg has earned support from three state senators, 28 of her colleagues in the Minnesota House of Representatives, and national progressive organizations like Our Revolution and End Citizens United. She has also received some support from D.C., racking up endorsements from Rep. Chris Deluzio, who to Sen. John Fetterman (D-Penn.) in 2028, and Rep. Val Hoyle (D-Ore.). Aside from securing the coveted Minnesota DFL endorsement, Little has also picked up backing from the state's Attorney General Keith Ellison, and key figures within the existing progressive infrastructure in Congress. Rep. Greg Casar, chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, Rep. Pramila Jayapal, former CPC chair, and Rep. Maxwell Frost, one of CPC's vice chairs, have all publicly supported his candidacy. The CPC's PAC is also supporting Little. Klein, for his part, has also seen a flood of supportive outside spending. 314 Action Fund is a super PAC which backs candidates who are involved in science or medicine, but has an AIPAC passthrough. FEC records show that the super PAC $1,261,341 in independent expenditures backing Klein in four installments between July 20 and July 30. On August 5, 314 Action dropped another $1.2 million into the race. The state senator has also received an additional $138,440 from 57 individual donors who have also given to AIPAC, UDP, or DMFI. All of the individual donations were , June 28, many divided in various increments amounting to the maximum $3,500 individual contribution each. Among those individuals is James Sprayregen, who sits on the National Board of AIPAC and serves on the Board of Governors for the American Jewish Committee. Sprayregen contributed $129,500 to the pro-Israel groups and to Klein in three separate same-day installments amounting to $3,499.99, one cent below the legal maximum, possibly to avoid being classified as a max-out donor. Also listed among the individual donors pooled by AIPAC on Klein's behalf are Jody Forchheimer, who gave $283,456 to pro-Israel PACs and $3,500 to Klein, and Gadi Maier, who gave $135,000 to pro-Israel PACs and $3,500 to Klein. Forchheimer is a Senior Legal Fellow at the Louis D. Brandeis Center, a pro-Israel legal organization fighting antisemitism cases, and publicly discussed her role in pro-Israel advocacy at the AIPAC policy conference in 2019. Maier is an Israeli-American tech entrepreneur who is founder and CEO of ID Handshake, the first and a current board member at Forter, a fraud prevention platform, and formerly served as CEO of both FraudSciences and FreeMonee. When asked about 314 Action Fund backing Klein's campaign and an inquiry about the aforementioned prominent pro-Israel donors, the campaign manager provided a statement in response to the latter. "Our campaign is powered by thousands of supporters from every background and every faith--because that's who we are, and that's who I've spent my career serving," Klein told Drop Site. "As a doctor, I've cared for Jewish families, Muslim families, Christian families, and families of no faith at all, and I've never once asked who they were before helping them. This campaign is no different. I'm proud of the support we've received from neighbors, community leaders, and working families of all denominations." Addressing the first question, the spokesperson added, "You should talk with 314 about their funding. I have copied Eden from their team on this email." The move was eyebrow-raising, as campaigns and independent expenditure groups are not allowed to coordinate campaign activity. Though it is not considered best practice for campaigns and independent expenditure arms to communicate at all, it is legal to discuss some information as long as it doesn't amount to coordination. 314 Action also received a $2.5 million donation from pro-Israel billionaire Michael Bloomberg on May 4, just months before its spending blitz in Minnesota. Whether Bloomberg's money is earmarked to the Klein race is unclear; it would be odd if so, as Berg is endorsed by the organization Everytown for Gun Safety, which Bloomberg founded and primarily finances. That would mean Bloomberg was spending against himself in the same race. Joshua Morrow, 314 Action Fund's president, said in a statement that the group is not funneling pro-Israel PAC money into the race. "As we have said multiple times, 314 Action Fund has not taken money from AIPAC or its affiliated entities this cycle and we won't," Morrow said. "We have spent over $14.5 million supporting STEM candidates in 2026 and not a cent has come from AIPAC, UDP, DMFI or affiliated entities. Similarly, our investments in Dr. Matt Klein are not from AIPAC or affiliated entities, and any suggestion otherwise is false, sensationalized and reported without sources." Still, Klein refuses to recognize the genocide in Gaza, instead broadly calling for a two-state solution. Berg and Little, backed by David Hogg's Leaders We Deserve, on the other hand, have publicly called it one. Little differentiates himself from Berg, however, in supporting a suspension on any further U.S. military aid to Israel, while the latter has . In a video posted Wednesday, she calls for an end "to all weapons sales to Israel," going further than she had previously. Klein has racked up endorsements from 19 colleagues in the Minnesota state senate, but has not received any explicit endorsements from Washington. The two-term state senator has also faced some scandal in the race, having placed a $50 wager on Kalshi, a prediction market service, betting that he'd win the MN-02 primary, which ultimately led to an April 2026 fine and five-year ban from the platform. clean_body: Peter, I'm going to make a prediction... When the votes are counted this November, the radical left is going to be in a state of total shock. And the political establishment is going to spend weeks trying to explain what hit them. But that only happens if Republicans like you are on record before the Midterms. That is how consequential this moment is. But here is the part the pundits won't tell you. None of that happens automatically. The Democrats are at war with the American people -- open borders, defunding ICE, eliminating voter ID, putting men in women's sports. You name it, they are on the wrong side of it. And yet they are running the most radical, well-funded Senate candidates in states across this country who are counting on Republicans to stay home and let them walk right in. I will not let that happen. And I don't think you will either. I made you a prediction at the beginning of this email. I stand by every word of it. But that prediction is built on one assumption -- that Republicans like you are engaged and ready to fight. That is where your assessment comes in. Sincerely, Newt Gingrich Former Speaker of the House | Paid for by the NRSC. Not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee. |

I am inspired by the way she confronts fear and tirelessly acts to build solidarity and help people in need (you might remember our visit to the MGB picket line to stand in solidarity with nurses last month or the food drive June helped organize when the food pantry in Laconia ran empty). [](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/SBfG5CXjXMpPnRea4Kihqw~~/AAUS1hA~/HyqtKXfQoiQ05prim4flNihzWqCAUuZAomYC3zsOy66piHX0mDzqnR_4Yu2-dBGcg_UZp_4pGNO60hAoHfeGpZGT7OF0VkVvCzgma2FfRGyWnDa4Q4pu-QLzym3ntD113pyKaXIm9umaiH6AQ0z69xngNfJFvlnHzwDBFemeC_E~) In her book, _Hey! I Could Use a Little Help Here_ , June describes her experiences as a psychiatric and operating room nurse as well as an assault she suffered at work. Since retiring in 2025, she’s been a vocal advocate for healthcare professionals. Her willingness to talk about what happened to her is important because it is, unfortunately, a much needed reminder that being assaulted should not be considered just ‘a part of the jobʼ for the people who take care of people who are hurting. Workplace violence against nurses is way too common and our current healthcare system too often fails nurses, while they are caring for the most vulnerable people in our communities. In the podcast, we discussed the important role unions play in ensuring safety and protections for nurses, and how policymakers can do a better job listening to nurses and crafting policy, like the Workplace Violence Prevention for Health Care and Social Service Workers Act. There is bipartisan legislation we can support to protect and support healthcare and social service workers. Supporting nurses is common sense and itʼs the right thing to do. We have to do a better job taking care of the people who take care of us. That’s why I stood with Mass General Brigham nurses in their strike, and why I’m so honored to work alongside June. As I said on the podcast, my take-home message is thank you to June for sharing her story even when itʼs really hard to relieve the experience of her assault and for being willing to organize to build power so we can make change. clean_body: He's litigating the past. I'm fighting for what matters. | | Friend, Let's not forget that a few weeks ago, Donald Trump delivered a prime-time address to the entire country about his unfounded grievances over the 2020 election. It wasn't about real issues families are struggling with. The cost of groceries, skyrocketing healthcare premiums, hospitals on the verge of collapse. It's about an election he lost fair and square six years ago. This administration has time for grievance theater about a six-year-old loss, but no time to sit down and actually help working families keep up with the cost of living. That's the real story here. I didn't run for Congress to relitigate the past. I ran to fight for the people of NJ-09, right now, on the things that actually affect their lives: healthcare, affordability, and a government that works for them instead of obsessing over itself. = | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your secure donation will go through immediately. clean_body: I looked at the numbers. Your file is empty. Let's fix that right now. | Peter, I have spent thirty years reading voter data. I know what a healthy file looks like -- and I know what a gap looks like. Right now, your file has a gap. Here's why this matters more than you might think. When we sit down to build our Senate strategy for November, we go list by list, zip code by zip code. We look at who responded, what they care about, and where the intensity is. That data is how we decide where to fight, where to spend, and where to hold the line. Democrats are not leaving blank files. Their activists are filling out every survey, returning every call, and showing up at every meeting. They are building the most complete voter intelligence operation this party has ever run -- and they are doing it right now, while most conservatives are still enjoying their summer. I have seen elections lost in the data room before the first ad ever runs. Your answers matter. Your file matters. And right now -- your response is the one we're still waiting on. clean_body: | Peter, I'm going to make a prediction... When the votes are counted this November, the radical left is going to be in a state of total shock. And the political establishment is going to spend weeks trying to explain what hit them. But that only happens if Republicans like you are on record before the Midterms. That is how consequential this moment is. But here is the part the pundits won't tell you. None of that happens automatically. The Democrats are at war with the American people -- open borders, defunding ICE, eliminating voter ID, putting men in women's sports. You name it, they are on the wrong side of it. And yet they are running the most radical, well-funded Senate candidates in states across this country who are counting on Republicans to stay home and let them walk right in. I will not let that happen. And I don't think you will either. I made you a prediction at the beginning of this email. I stand by every word of it. But that prediction is built on one assumption -- that Republicans like you are engaged and ready to fight. That is where your assessment comes in. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. # [Will El-Sayed's Centrist Opponents "Vote Blue No Matter Who"?](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4981170&post_id=210237024&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjEwMjM3MDI0LCJpYXQiOjE3ODYxMjkwMzIsImV4cCI6MTc4ODcyMTAzMiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTQ5ODExNzAiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.fWpFjzohkGnCbqY7W6I0D5k5DDYYVwY70VmMAyEUeZE)
### It's time to unite to defeat MAGA.
| | [Aaron Regunberg](https://substack.com/@aaronregunberg)
---
| Aug 7
---
| [](https://substack.com/@aaronregunberg)

| | [](https://open.substack.com/pub/aaronregunberg/p/will-el-sayeds-centrist-opponents?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-restack-comment&action=restack-comment&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjEwMjM3MDI0LCJpYXQiOjE3ODYxMjkwMzMsImV4cCI6MTc4ODcyMTAzMywiaXNzIjoicHViLTQ5ODExNzAiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.HLAzvQJ5tYZLJTj7fuKEBPQmeuAzFLaW5q0OxYhCbQU&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)

---

Call it a sweep. On Tuesday, progressives ran the table in the Michigan Democratic primary, with Donovan McKinney, Will Lawrence, and Abdul El-Sayed each dispatching their corporate-backed opponents despite a barrage of dark-money-funded attack ads against them--including [$70 million](https://substack.com/redirect/592d32da-7798-4552-bec1-631353d5abcc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) spent against El-Sayed, whose campaign overcame an 11-to-one spending disadvantage to secure his remarkable victory.
The big question, now, is whether the Democratic establishment that opposed these candidates so vehemently in the primary will rally around the nominees their voters elected--particularly El-Sayed, whose race is a must-win for Democrats if they are going to take back the Senate.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..NnXg0d1L1nGxjZxfJY5VgvNSUsb7s8EO2vK11ibBG2A?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=210237024)
Fortunately, a number of major party leaders have already announced their endorsement of El-Sayed. Representative Haley Stevens released a [classy concession statement](https://substack.com/redirect/fa03958a-6ce1-4629-9ffe-dff1713b172b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) saying she is "proud to offer" her support in the general election against Mike Rogers. Governor Gretchen Whitmer, who backed Stevens in the primary, also [endorsed](https://substack.com/redirect/c322d9e9-0487-4cbf-9692-20fda80a14b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) El-Sayed, saying, "We're all united by our shared goal of getting things done for the people in Michigan." Kamala Harris [sent out](https://substack.com/redirect/abe82a21-ec85-4b57-9d54-b55368c6c893?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a fundraising e-mail for him. And the machinery of the party is kicking into gear--the Democrats' Senate Majority PAC has [already put out](https://substack.com/redirect/ad9e5908-b843-4247-8aa9-c58eadbb60b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a genuinely moving ad for El-Sayed, set to Journey's "Don't Stop Believing."
This shows how far the center of gravity in the party has shifted--and quickly. After all, it was only last year when a number of centrist leaders, including Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer, refused to endorse Zohran Mamdani after Democratic voters in New York City decisively chose him as their mayoral nominee. Democratic Senator Kirsten Gillibrand even went on to [falsely claim](https://substack.com/redirect/8e9893cf-bc2b-4861-81f5-c4523203154b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Mamdani supported "global jihad," a message [echoed](https://substack.com/redirect/cd1f2242-ede1-4eb5-89df-b2518cf9cac8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Democratic Representatives Tom Suozzi and Laura Gillen. Today, of course, Mamdani is one of the most [popular](https://substack.com/redirect/2dfb0c77-9d9b-468f-9531-2875bd3183bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Democrats in the country.
And yet, despite all this progress, it's clear that we still have a long way to go until the left flank of the Democratic Party is broadly accepted as a legitimate, equal partner--and potentially a future senior partner--in the Democratic coalition, as evidenced by the significant array of party leaders who have not been so forthcoming in their support for the newly minted Michigan Senate nominee.
When asked, prior to Tuesday, if she would back the Muslim-American El-Sayed if he won the primary, Michigan Democratic Representative Hillary Scholten [said](https://substack.com/redirect/8a5115fe-81dd-4711-a2e1-226ed20eb6a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "I will not stand beside someone who has allowed distinctly anti-American sentiment to enter our public dialogue." Since then, she's [refused](https://substack.com/redirect/d6179041-685a-48be-ac10-e309719122f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to respond to a request about whether she would be endorsing him.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/76c6b31e-224d-4f65-b3d0-1cfd8040f347?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Michael LaRosa, who served as press secretary for first lady Jill Biden and special assistant to President Joe Biden, went further. "If [El-Sayed] wins, I will do everything I can to make sure he loses," he [posted](https://substack.com/redirect/b3601e21-eade-413b-97df-97dda64e59c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) before the primary, a position he's [doubled down](https://substack.com/redirect/897be628-b125-4f1d-bb1e-d5a93d8895e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on since. Other right-leaning Democratic influencers have shared [similar sentiments](https://substack.com/redirect/2bfc6254-22fa-4bf2-b526-478cced93bc8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d830a9e3-f3f9-48d6-a80e-377f44b3b462?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Then there's Neera Tanden, president of the Center for American Progress--ostensibly the leading establishment think tank of the Democratic Party--who spent the last month relentlessly attacking El-Sayed on social media. So far, she has not changed her tune, offering no public statements of support for the Democratic nominee--just a [bunch](https://substack.com/redirect/ceb7a69d-503d-4d9b-8d06-06898cc22e6a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of [posts](https://substack.com/redirect/b3c607d5-ce66-4a83-b5ae-13af5069f77f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [implying](https://substack.com/redirect/43dcca59-b404-478b-a2a4-c228d3a3911f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that he lacks backing from the working class. Meanwhile the corporatist think tank Third Way responded to El-Sayed's win not with a call to unify against the MAGA right but with the announcement of a $15 million campaign to "discredit" democratic socialism, despite concerns, as _The New York Times_ [put it](https://substack.com/redirect/83faf58e-d8f8-4149-8025-1dce1326dd13?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), of "potentially undercutting Democratic nominees in swing-state races and undermining the party's chances of retaking Congress."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dd0f4f60-e1de-423e-b151-2e85e87b7192?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This refusal--whether real or threatened--to, in centrist parlance, "Vote Blue No Matter Who," is particularly ironic given that it's the very crime many of these same establishment figures spent [months](https://substack.com/redirect/099deff8-887c-46f0-a4ef-f8ba6fc5a2b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [accusing](https://substack.com/redirect/55a1b59f-9da7-4981-8990-4fdc20e654e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) El-Sayed of committing. The difference is that, in contrast to today's centrist threats, El-Sayed never betrayed the Democratic Party. The attacks from the right focused on El-Sayed's support of the Uncommitted movement, an attempt to push Biden on his disastrous Gaza policy during the 2024 primaries--and only during the primaries. As Waleed Shahid, an Uncommitted organizer, [explained](https://substack.com/redirect/3da381a7-b4b7-4415-ac49-56b277a7f536?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "We weren't trying to blow up the coalition. We were trying to keep it alive." Indeed, El-Sayed endorsed Kamala Harris the morning after she launched her 2024 campaign.
It seems, then, that we will soon see what counts as a greater betrayal among certain members of the Democratic establishment: using your primary vote to try to persuade a presumptive Democratic nominee to change course on an issue that was (empirically) an electoral catastrophe, or actively undermining the general election campaign of your party's confirmed nominee in a must-win battleground seat.
Just the fact that this is a question demonstrates the hypocrisy behind some centrists' past evocation of "Vote Blue No Matter Who," a line that's long been used to discipline progressives. What made those admonitions so galling was that progressive Democrats _have_ been overwhelmingly voting blue no matter who, election after election. A [higher percentage](https://substack.com/redirect/8a813fea-85fa-4bc9-86c6-21e9b5ab609d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of Bernie's voters backed Hillary Clinton in 2016 than Clinton's supporters in the 2008 presidential primary backed Barack Obama's general election campaign. The same is true of the 2020 election, when progressives aggressively rallied behind Biden, and the 2024 election, when they did the same for Harris (as I can attest to firsthand, as one of the organizers of the "[Progressives for Harris](https://substack.com/redirect/dfec17dc-3c92-47f4-a087-7cc4b0a34658?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" effort).
The truth is, it's very easy to say "Vote Blue No Matter Who" when that means voting for your own worldview and interests. It's a lot harder when it requires supporting someone who is on the opposite side of issues that are deeply important to you. Progressives spend their entire lives swallowing their feelings to do the latter and _still_ get attacked by the establishment for disloyalty. But the moment this dynamic flips--as occurred in Michigan this week, thanks to an array of superior candidates running superior campaigns with a superior capacity to meet this moment--key members of the centrist establishment have shown that their loyalty is not to the Democratic Party but to their side's control of the party.
Hopefully, this time around, these figures will choose to act with more grace. Hopefully, Democratic elected officials like Scholten will put aside their factional grievances and join the majority of their party's voters and leaders in helping Democratic nominees defeat the Republicans rubber-stamping Trump's authoritarian power grabs. Hopefully, centrists can start taking a page from the most committed base of the Democratic coalition--the progressives who have again and again shifted gears from disappointing primary losses to supporting the Democratic nominees in the general election, the ones they had, at one point, campaigned against. If nothing else, hopefully the "Vote Blue No Matter Who" Democrats can muster the basic wherewithal to actually vote blue no matter who.

Today, of course, Mamdani is one of the most Democrats in the country. And yet, despite all this progress, it's clear that we still have a long way to go until the left flank of the Democratic Party is broadly accepted as a legitimate, equal partner--and potentially a future senior partner--in the Democratic coalition, as evidenced by the significant array of party leaders who have not been so forthcoming in their support for the newly minted Michigan Senate nominee. When asked, prior to Tuesday, if she would back the Muslim-American El-Sayed if he won the primary, Michigan Democratic Representative Hillary Scholten , "I will not stand beside someone who has allowed distinctly anti-American sentiment to enter our public dialogue." Since then, she's to respond to a request about whether she would be endorsing him. | | ---|---|--- Michael LaRosa, who served as press secretary for first lady Jill Biden and special assistant to President Joe Biden, went further. "If [El-Sayed] wins, I will do everything I can to make sure he loses," he before the primary, a position he's on since. Other right-leaning Democratic influencers have shared . | | ---|---|--- Then there's Neera Tanden, president of the Center for American Progress--ostensibly the leading establishment think tank of the Democratic Party--who spent the last month relentlessly attacking El-Sayed on social media. So far, she has not changed her tune, offering no public statements of support for the Democratic nominee--just a of that he lacks backing from the working class. Meanwhile the corporatist think tank Third Way responded to El-Sayed's win not with a call to unify against the MAGA right but with the announcement of a $15 million campaign to "discredit" democratic socialism, despite concerns, as The New York Times , of "potentially undercutting Democratic nominees in swing-state races and undermining the party's chances of retaking Congress." | | ---|---|--- This refusal--whether real or threatened--to, in centrist parlance, "Vote Blue No Matter Who," is particularly ironic given that it's the very crime many of these same establishment figures spent El-Sayed of committing. The difference is that, in contrast to today's centrist threats, El-Sayed never betrayed the Democratic Party. The attacks from the right focused on El-Sayed's support of the Uncommitted movement, an attempt to push Biden on his disastrous Gaza policy during the 2024 primaries--and only during the primaries. As Waleed Shahid, an Uncommitted organizer, , "We weren't trying to blow up the coalition. We were trying to keep it alive." Indeed, El-Sayed endorsed Kamala Harris the morning after she launched her 2024 campaign. It seems, then, that we will soon see what counts as a greater betrayal among certain members of the Democratic establishment: using your primary vote to try to persuade a presumptive Democratic nominee to change course on an issue that was (empirically) an electoral catastrophe, or actively undermining the general election campaign of your party's confirmed nominee in a must-win battleground seat. Just the fact that this is a question demonstrates the hypocrisy behind some centrists' past evocation of "Vote Blue No Matter Who," a line that's long been used to discipline progressives. What made those admonitions so galling was that progressive Democrats have been overwhelmingly voting blue no matter who, election after election. A of Bernie's voters backed Hillary Clinton in 2016 than Clinton's supporters in the 2008 presidential primary backed Barack Obama's general election campaign. The same is true of the 2020 election, when progressives aggressively rallied behind Biden, and the 2024 election, when they did the same for Harris (as I can attest to firsthand, as one of the organizers of the "" effort). The truth is, it's very easy to say "Vote Blue No Matter Who" when that means voting for your own worldview and interests. It's a lot harder when it requires supporting someone who is on the opposite side of issues that are deeply important to you. Progressives spend their entire lives swallowing their feelings to do the latter and still get attacked by the establishment for disloyalty. But the moment this dynamic flips--as occurred in Michigan this week, thanks to an array of superior candidates running superior campaigns with a superior capacity to meet this moment--key members of the centrist establishment have shown that their loyalty is not to the Democratic Party but to their side's control of the party. Hopefully, this time around, these figures will choose to act with more grace. Hopefully, Democratic elected officials like Scholten will put aside their factional grievances and join the majority of their party's voters and leaders in helping Democratic nominees defeat the Republicans rubber-stamping Trump's authoritarian power grabs. Hopefully, centrists can start taking a page from the most committed base of the Democratic coalition--the progressives who have again and again shifted gears from disappointing primary losses to supporting the Democratic nominees in the general election, the ones they had, at one point, campaigned against. If nothing else, hopefully the "Vote Blue No Matter Who" Democrats can muster the basic wherewithal to actually vote blue no matter who. | | ---|---|--- This piece was published by . clean_body: We did the impossible, let's do it again. | Friend, Yesterday, we did the impossible. And the best part?We did it together. Following a decisive victory in the Democratic primary, capturing nearly 70% of the vote and over 240,000 ballots across all 95 counties, Jerri Green has officially secured the Democratic nomination for Governor of Tennessee. Jerri shattered a glass ceiling, becoming __the first woman from either major political party ever nominated for Governor of Tennessee. This historic win belongs to every single one of us who believed that a grassroots, kitchen-table problem-solver could beat an entrenched machine. Our Republican opponent, Marsha Blackburn only won her primary with 44% of the vote. That means 56% of Republican primary voters actively rejected her as our movement heads into November unified, battle-tested, and ready to win. "Tennesseans are tired of being treated as an afterthought by a political establishment that looks backward and protects the wealthy while working families get left with the bill... They told us taking on this machine was too difficult, but like I always tell my kids: hard is not impossible. We are taking this fight to November, we are going to beat Marsha Blackburn, and we are going to build a Tennessee that finally puts working people first." - Jerri Green Now, the real work begins. We are going up against a massive, corporate-backed opponent who has spent decades stripping away healthcare access, defunding our public schools with voucher schemes, and dividing our communities through culture war politics. To beat Marsha Blackburn and take back our state,we won't ever compromise our values. That means we are not seeking or taking any big corporate PAC money. Since day one, our campaign has built a strong foundation on small-dollar, grassroots contributions from everyday Tennesseans. **[Colorado campaign connects hungry families with local farmers](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [SCOTTKJAMES.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_A new fund connects Colorado farmers with hungry families directly — no bureaucracy required — proving neighborly common sense still works._
* **A simple bridge between two problems:** Feeding Colorado, Colorado Proud, and the Colorado Department of Agriculture launched the 150 Colorado Agricultural Legacy Fund, raising money from Colorado Day through Labor Day to buy Colorado-grown food for distribution through nearly 800 hunger-relief partners statewide.
* **Local producers get real customers, not speeches:** The funds go exclusively toward Colorado Proud products, giving farmers and ranchers dependable buyers for food they've already produced while ensuring families receive fresh, local food rather than "leftovers from somebody's press conference."
* **A model built on dignity, not bureaucracy:** Columnist Scott K. James praises the initiative for skipping layers of red tape and government fog, arguing it shows how helping hungry families and supporting local agriculture can be "the same job" when responsibility stays close to home.

Our movement to protect our fundamental right to vote has seen many setbacks at the Supreme Court over the last two decades. Those hurdles have only pushed us to work harder to defend vote-by-mail, increase voter participation, and make every eligible vote count.

The ruling makes it nearly impossible to challenge district maps that dilute the power of underrepresented communities. Representatives can now choose their voters instead of the other way around.
What happened in the aftermath? Hours after the decision, Florida lawmakers passed a new congressional map designed to flip four U.S. House seats. States across the South began redrawing their maps, even in states where voters had already cast their ballots in primaries.
The Supreme Court didn't just fail to protect your vote. The Court’s Trump-appointed or MAGA-aligned majority actively dismantled the protections designed to make it count.

Power, Prosperity, Peace
| Hi Friends! It's Team Paige with another **EXCITING** update! We have a cool new way to get our campaign signs out there! We've kicked off an **"[Adopt a Road Sign](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/VEtQg5XcqQUhwlYDldDlsfnTB4zu9CjV/click?signature=48de12cc2cf0b2341428b4f05edbb669a2bcf20d&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.paigefornh.com%2Fsigns2)"** program.

* * *
**HERE'S HOW IT WORKS**
1. **You pick the spot.**
Know a prime location where you wish you could see a Paige Beauchemin for Congress sign? Pick a spot that gets good visibility and let us know where it is.

2. **You sponsor the sign.
** Adopt a road sign through [our website](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/VEtQg5XcqQUhwlYDldDlsfnTB4zu9CjV/click?signature=48de12cc2cf0b2341428b4f05edbb669a2bcf20d&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.paigefornh.com%2Fsigns2) and send us the location you have in mind.

3. **We do the rest!
** We’ll bring the sign out and put it up ourselves. And while we’re there, **we’ll clean up any trash** in the immediate area. **
**

* * *
Paige means it when she says she won't wait until she's elected to start getting to work!

Hi Peter, Yesterday was a historic day for Tennessee Democrats. Voters across the state didn't just set our Democratic slate for November. They delivered real wins. We flipped control of the Knox County Board of Education, the Montgomery County Commission, and the Hamilton County Commission. We ended the Republican supermajority on the Rutherford County Commission. And we flipped key races in Anderson, Coffee, Hamblen, Maury, Putnam, Sumner, Washington, Williamson, Wilson, and more. Tennessee is ready for a new direction. Yesterday proved it. First, I want to say THANK YOU to every single candidate who put their name on the ballot this cycle. Running for office in Tennessee takes immense courage, sacrifice, and an unwavering belief in our communities. For the first time in decades, we competed in every single corner of the state — organizing in all 95 counties to ensure no family was written off and no community was left without a voice on the ballot. **Now, we have our candidates.** Jerri Green for Governor. Marquita Bradshaw for U.S. Senate. And nine Democratic congressional candidates ready to fight for every corner of this state. **The primary is over. Hi Friend,
Welcome to the latest New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) newsletter!
Earlier this week, the PA [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] House State Government Committee [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] [https://www.politicspa.com/could-changes-finally-be-coming-to-pa-election-laws/141393/] voted on two bills that have the potential to impact our voting rights: State Rep Mehaffie's Voter ID bill (HB771) and State Rep. McClinton's omnibus bill (HB1396). Both passed out of committee this week and will now be voted on by the full house.
An omnibus bill is a legislative bill that combines multiple, sometimes unrelated, provisions or bills into one single bill. It's essentially a package deal of different legislative proposals, often used to facilitate the passage of legislation, particularly appropriations bills.
HB 771 is sponsored by State Rep. Thomas Mehaffie (Dauphin) and “would require all voters arriving at their election precincts to show identification or attest under penalty of law that they are legally able to vote in Pennsylvania.”
State Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta (Philadelphia) voiced his opposition to the bill. The bill doesn’t address [https://www.politicspa.com/state-government-committee-sends-voter-id-election-omnibus-bills-to-house-floor/141399] the real issues at stake. “We need to solve problems of voter irregularities and voter fraud,” he said. “We do not have demonstrable evidence that leads us to make the point that we need to address voter ID in this way. Let’s talk about the issues that do exist. This legislation doesn’t address those.”
HB 1396 has a more recognizable name behind it – Speaker of the State House Joanna McClinton (Delaware/Philadelphia). State Rep. Ben Waxman (Philadelphia) complemented the Speaker, saying that the legislation is a “comprehensive approach to election reform that tries to dramatically improve the process and makes administration of elections much smoother.”
Among other changes, [https://penncapital-star.com/campaigns-elections/voter-id-and-vote-by-mail-reform-bills-move-to-pa-house] House Bill 1396 would also give election workers up to a week before Election Day to prepare to count mail-in ballots, a process that has been a bottleneck for election results in parts of the state, providing fodder for election deniers.
The vote-by-mail provision has been the subject of numerous lawsuits, including one now before the U.S. Supreme Court, as candidates and parties have argued over how election officials should handle irregularities, such as errors on completed ballots, that are not explicitly addressed.
The bill would make clear that county election officials are required to notify voters if their mail-in ballots have been rejected for the lack of a signature and give the voter an opportunity to “cure” the error.

She co-founded Young Professionals of Color–Greater Harrisburg (YPOC), an organization dedicated to fostering leadership, advocacy, and professional growth for communities of color.

[https://d15k2d11r6t6rl.cloudfront.net/public/users/Integrators/04eaa6b2-88f4-43b4-b978-7bb0708f5838/7237344C447445787878394747342B75584E47375A57552F745265427662334B544A4A36505A58657A5871474B7A5A6E53705571424758325657365969365747/editor_images/WCM%20logo.JPG] #CourtsMatter
This past Friday, Courts delivered wins for Pennsylvania voters [https://www.democracydocket.com/news-alerts/a-double-win-for-voters-in-pennsylvania] . One ruling ensured that undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots will be counted, while the other rejected a bid to purge more than 277,000 from the state’s voter rolls.
First, the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/445-2025-04-24-Order-denying-PA-Attorney-Generals-motion-to-intervene.pdf] a request by Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday (R), on behalf of the state, to halt a recent federal court ruling that Pennsylvania must count undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots.
The ruling stemmed from a lawsuit originally filed [https://www.democracydocket.com/cases/pennsylvania-undated-and-wrongly-dated-mail-in-ballots-challenge-eakin/] in 2022, challenging the state’s instructions to county boards of elections that any mail-in ballot that’s timely cast but either missing a date or containing the wrong date on the outer return envelopes should not be counted.
After the federal judge’s ruling in March of this year, the plaintiffs appealed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/441-2025-04-02-Notice-Of-Appeal-.pdf] the decision to the 3rd Circuit. The appeal remains ongoing, but today’s order ensures that counties will count wrongly dated and undated ballots during this month’s primary.
Second, a Pennsylvania district court judge dismissed a lawsuit by the 1789 Foundation to have hundreds of thousands of voters purged from Pennsylvania’s voter rolls.The 1789 Foundation, also known as Citizen_AG, filed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/1-2024-10-29-Complaint.pdf] a lawsuit in October against Pennsylvania Secretary of State Al Schmidt (R) claiming Schmidt failed to maintain voter rolls in line with the National Voter Registration Act.
The group wanted the court to force Pennsylvania to remove 277,000 registrants who did not respond to confirmation notices in the 2020 general election cycle removed from the voter rolls.
District Court judge Robert Mariani dismissed [https://www.democracydocket.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/67-2025-05-02-Memorandum-.pdf] the 1789 Foundation’s lawsuit on the grounds that the organization lacked standing to bring the case in the first place.
In law, standing [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standing_(law)] is a condition that a party seeking a legal remedy must show they have, by demonstrating to the court, sufficient connection to and harm from the law or action challenged to support the party's participation in the case.
In other news, this year marks the 15th anniversary of a landmark U.S. Supreme Court ruling that fundamentally reshaped the world of campaign finance. For good-government supporters, it’s a somber milestone. Find out why in Spotlight PA’s full report. [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/citizens-united-supreme-court-ruling-campaign-finance-dark-money]
The 2010 decision in Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission , they say, vastly expanded the role of big money in politics and ushered in an era of unprecedented — and in some cases, untraceable — spending on elections by ultra-wealthy special interests.
In Pennsylvania, the court decision’s impact on races for state and local offices was muted — at least early on. That is because of Pennsylvania’s notoriously lax campaign finance laws. Some state lawmakers have sought to tighten rules around so-called “dark money” groups, but their legislation didn’t make it through the full legislature. Continue reading for more on Citizens United and its lasting impact [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/citizens-united-supreme-court-ruling-campaign-finance-dark-money] .

Let's provide civic education together!
We're looking for people passionate about voting rights in Philadelphia, Allegheny, Erie, Lawrence, Bucks, Montgomery, Chester, and Delaware County to help us shape the future of Pennsylvania.
Join our team and help us provide civic education in our communities and register folks to vote!
Positions start at $20 an hour.
Interested? Contact jobs@nppef.org [jobs@nppef.org]
EMAIL US [jobs@nppef.org]
News You Can Use
There are things every one of us can do [https://www.democracydocket.com/opinion/we-have-more-power-than-trump-wants-us-to-believe-heres-what-you-can-do/] in our daily lives to help ensure free and fair elections. Some actions are small — so small that you might dismiss them as unimportant. Don’t. Every important journey begins with a single step, and the first is no less important than the last.
1. Educate Yourself
Elections can be complicated. The rules vary from state to state — and sometimes even from county to county. These rules also change frequently due to new laws, policies or court rulings. My first recommendation: spend time each month learning what’s happening with voting laws in your state and nationally.
Spotlight PA has an 2025 Election Center [https://www.spotlightpa.org/elections] with all the information you need to be prepared to vote this year, including guides to the big races, key dates, and more.
* New: Which Pittsburgh mayoral candidate most aligns with you? Take our quiz [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pittsburgh-mayor-election-2025-candidates-quiz]
* Get answers to your questions with our AI-powered Election Assistant [https://www.spotlightpa.org/elections/assistant/]
* Everything you need to know about mail voting [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-mail-ballot-how-to-request-fill-out-return] , becoming a poll worker [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-how-to-be-poll-worker-guide]
* Everything you need to know about how to vote and where to vote [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pennsylvania-primary-election-day-2025-voter-information-registration]
* Guides to Commonwealth, Superior Courts [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-commonwealth-superior-court-candidates] , vetting judicial candidates [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-candidate-vetting-guide]
* Guides to State College school board [https://www.spotlightpa.org/statecollege/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-state-college-school-board-anderson-huff-barlow-black-desmarais-mcternan-sogor] , Reading City Council president [https://www.spotlightpa.org/berks/2025/04/reading-city-council-president-primary-election-2025]
* Guides to voting as a college student [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-college-student-voting-guide]
En Español
* Guía para votar por correo [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pensilvania-elecciones-primarias-2025-votar-correo-como-llenar] , la presidencia del Concejo Municipal de Reading [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/reading-concejo-municipal-primarias-elecciones-2025]
* Guía para quién está en la papeleta de las primarias [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pensilvania-primarias-elecciones-2025-votar-informacion] , cómo convertirse en trabajador electoral el 20 de mayo [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/05/pensilvania-elecciones-2025-como-convertirse-trabajador-electoral]
2. Stay Engaged
To protect democracy, we all must stay engaged day in and day out. We can’t just show up right before an election and tune out afterward. If we remain committed, democracy will win.
Check out a Montgomery County Commissioner’s effort to educate voters. It's now an emmy-nominated short film. “Running elections in Pennsylvania's third-most-populous county, Neil Makhija said he’s seen the slippery slope from election misinformation to political violence.” ( Philadelphia Inquirer [https://www.inquirer.com/politics/pennsylvania/montgomery-county-commissioner-neil-makhija-emmy-20250508.html] )
3. Share What You Learn
Once you’ve figured out what’s going on, share that information with your networks and community. It might feel awkward to bring up voter suppression or changes in election laws when we’re not in the middle of a major election — but local elections happen in off years, and special elections are more common than you think. Now is the perfect time to start conversations about voting.
Here, in Pennsylvania, we vote every year, twice a year!
4. Join or Support Pro-Democracy Organizations
Is partisan politics not for you? There are numerous nonprofits and grassroots organizations working every day to protect voting rights and ensure free and fair elections. Supporting these groups with your time or resources helps these groups do their work.
Check out the work New PA Project has been up to lately below. AND , check out our upcoming events listed above!
5. Become a Trained Poll Worker
Many counties face a shortage of poll workers, especially during election season. Being a poll worker requires dedication, attention to detail and a willingness to be trained. It’s a meaningful way to serve your community and help protect the integrity of the voting process.
Here are some resources that may be helpful:
Pennsylvania Capital-Star - Advocacy groups offer training for Pa. primary poll watchers [https://penncapital-star.com/briefs/advocacy-groups-offer-training-for-pa-primary-poll-watchers/]
Spotlight PA - Election 2025: How to become a poll worker for the PA primary [https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2025/04/pennsylvania-primary-election-2025-how-to-be-poll-worker-guide/]
Franklin County Free Press - Poll Workers Needed for Pennsylvania’s 2025 Primary Election [https://fcfreepresspa.com/poll-workers-needed-for-pennsylvanias-2025-primary-election/]
6. Engage Your Elected Officials
Call and write your elected officials at the federal, state and local levels. Tell them that protecting voting rights and ensuring free and fair elections are your top priorities. Even better, show up at public meetings. Ask them directly what they’re doing to combat voter suppression. Be informed about pending legislation and urge them to support pro-democracy initiatives. This applies no matter where you live or who represents you — Democrat or Republican. Constituent pressure always matters. Don’t let anyone tell you otherwise.
7. Vote in Every Election
Yes — every election. That means local elections, primary elections and special elections. Become a super-voter. The more you vote, the more informed and engaged you become. You’ll also be better positioned to notice and report problems — like changes to polling locations or voting equipment — that could impact turnout or accessibility.
Make a plan to vote in the primary election, Tuesday, May 20th. When are you voting this year? Who are you going with? How are you voting this year -- by mail or on Election Day? As a reminder, the last day to request a mail ballot is Tuesday, May 13th!
