clean_body: [] Hi Friend, Welcome to the latest New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) newsletter! Earlier this week, the PA [] House State Government Committee [] [] voted on two bills that have the potential to impact our voting rights: State Rep Mehaffie's Voter ID bill (HB771) and State Rep. McClinton's omnibus bill (HB1396). Both passed out of committee this week and will now be voted on by the full house. An omnibus bill is a legislative bill that combines multiple, sometimes unrelated, provisions or bills into one single bill. It's essentially a package deal of different legislative proposals, often used to facilitate the passage of legislation, particularly appropriations bills. HB 771 is sponsored by State Rep. Thomas Mehaffie (Dauphin) and “would require all voters arriving at their election precincts to show identification or attest under penalty of law that they are legally able to vote in Pennsylvania.” State Rep. Malcolm Kenyatta (Philadelphia) voiced his opposition to the bill. The bill doesn’t address [] the real issues at stake. “We need to solve problems of voter irregularities and voter fraud,” he said. “We do not have demonstrable evidence that leads us to make the point that we need to address voter ID in this way. Let’s talk about the issues that do exist. This legislation doesn’t address those.” HB 1396 has a more recognizable name behind it – Speaker of the State House Joanna McClinton (Delaware/Philadelphia). State Rep. Ben Waxman (Philadelphia) complemented the Speaker, saying that the legislation is a “comprehensive approach to election reform that tries to dramatically improve the process and makes administration of elections much smoother.” Among other changes, [] House Bill 1396 would also give election workers up to a week before Election Day to prepare to count mail-in ballots, a process that has been a bottleneck for election results in parts of the state, providing fodder for election deniers. The vote-by-mail provision has been the subject of numerous lawsuits, including one now before the U.S. Supreme Court, as candidates and parties have argued over how election officials should handle irregularities, such as errors on completed ballots, that are not explicitly addressed. The bill would make clear that county election officials are required to notify voters if their mail-in ballots have been rejected for the lack of a signature and give the voter an opportunity to “cure” the error. Upcoming events As Allegheny County voters prepare for the pivotal 2025 local, municipal and judicial elections, the New PA Project Education Fund (NPPEF) is hosting two critical public candidate forums to give community members the chance to hear directly from the candidates shaping our schools and courts. These moderated discussions will allow voters to ask questions and learn more about each candidate’s priorities and qualifications before heading to the polls. [] Meet the candidates running for the Pittsburgh School Board and hear how they plan to impact our schools and students. Moderator: Dr. Kimeka Campbell is our Senior Director of Campaigns and Engagement. She is a recognized community activist, political strategist, and civic engagement leader. With over 15 years of experience in community organizing, political consulting, and nonprofit leadership, Dr. Campbell has been instrumental in shaping voter engagement strategies and building coalitions for progressive change. She co-founded Young Professionals of Color–Greater Harrisburg (YPOC), an organization dedicated to fostering leadership, advocacy, and professional growth for communities of color. When: Friday, May 9, 2025 | 6:00 PM – 7:30 PM Where: Hosanna House, 807 Wallace Ave, Wilkinsburg, PA 15221 RSVP [] [] Get to know the Allegheny County Common Pleas judicial candidates before you cast your ballot. Your vote shapes our justice system! Moderator: Rachel Bracken, Alliance for Justice (AFJ), Senior Regional State Courts Manager Rachel is a Senior Regional State Courts Manager with Alliance for Justice/AFJ Action. In this position, she manages AFJ/AFJ Action’s involvement in state supreme court justice elections and selection processes. Prior to joining the Justice Team, Rachel was on AFJ’s Outreach Team where she helped create AFJ’s State Court Justice Project and launch AFJ Action’s State Courts Matter initiative. She also coordinated AFJ’s networks of law professors, attorneys, and political donors to advocate around federal judicial nominations and federal courts’ impact on our constitutional rights and freedoms. When: Monday, May 12, 2025 | 6:00 PM – 8:00 PM Where: Hosanna House, 807 Wallace Ave, Wilkinsburg, PA 15221 RSVP [] Social Media of the Week [] The deadline to request your mail-in ballot for the primary election is May 13th at 5PM. Request a mail-in ballot or find your local ballot drop-off location here [vote.pa] Your county election office must receive your completed mail ballot by 8PM on May 20th. We recommend mailing it at least 5 days prior, or delivering it by hand at an official ballot drop off location. #GoVotePA SHARE ON INSTAGRAM [] [] #CourtsMatter This past Friday, Courts delivered wins for Pennsylvania voters [] . One ruling ensured that undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots will be counted, while the other rejected a bid to purge more than 277,000 from the state’s voter rolls. First, the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied [] a request by Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday (R), on behalf of the state, to halt a recent federal court ruling that Pennsylvania must count undated or wrongly dated mail-in ballots. The ruling stemmed from a lawsuit originally filed [] in 2022, challenging the state’s instructions to county boards of elections that any mail-in ballot that’s timely cast but either missing a date or containing the wrong date on the outer return envelopes should not be counted. After the federal judge’s ruling in March of this year, the plaintiffs appealed [] the decision to the 3rd Circuit. The appeal remains ongoing, but today’s order ensures that counties will count wrongly dated and undated ballots during this month’s primary. Second, a Pennsylvania district court judge dismissed a lawsuit by the 1789 Foundation to have hundreds of thousands of voters purged from Pennsylvania’s voter rolls.The 1789 Foundation, also known as CitizenAG, filed [] a lawsuit in October against Pennsylvania Secretary of State Al Schmidt (R) claiming Schmidt failed to maintain voter rolls in line with the National Voter Registration Act. The group wanted the court to force Pennsylvania to remove 277,000 registrants who did not respond to confirmation notices in the 2020 general election cycle removed from the voter rolls. District Court judge Robert Mariani dismissed [] the 1789 Foundation’s lawsuit on the grounds that the organization lacked standing to bring the case in the first place. In law, standing [)] is a condition that a party seeking a legal remedy must show they have, by demonstrating to the court, sufficient connection to and harm from the law or action challenged to support the party's participation in the case. In other news, this year marks the 15th anniversary of a landmark U.S. Supreme Court ruling that fundamentally reshaped the world of campaign finance. For good-government supporters, it’s a somber milestone. Find out why in Spotlight PA’s full report. [] The 2010 decision in Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission , they say, vastly expanded the role of big money in politics and ushered in an era of unprecedented — and in some cases, untraceable — spending on elections by ultra-wealthy special interests. In Pennsylvania, the court decision’s impact on races for state and local offices was muted — at least early on. That is because of Pennsylvania’s notoriously lax campaign finance laws. Some state lawmakers have sought to tighten rules around so-called “dark money” groups, but their legislation didn’t make it through the full legislature. Continue reading for more on Citizens United and its lasting impact [] . [] We are hiring! Let's provide civic education together! We're looking for people passionate about voting rights in Philadelphia, Allegheny, Erie, Lawrence, Bucks, Montgomery, Chester, and Delaware County to help us shape the future of Pennsylvania. Join our team and help us provide civic education in our communities and register folks to vote! Positions start at $20 an hour. Interested? Contact jobs@nppef.org [jobs@nppef.org] EMAIL US [jobs@nppef.org] News You Can Use There are things every one of us can do [] in our daily lives to help ensure free and fair elections. Some actions are small — so small that you might dismiss them as unimportant. Don’t. Every important journey begins with a single step, and the first is no less important than the last. 1. Educate Yourself Elections can be complicated. The rules vary from state to state — and sometimes even from county to county. These rules also change frequently due to new laws, policies or court rulings. My first recommendation: spend time each month learning what’s happening with voting laws in your state and nationally. Spotlight PA has an 2025 Election Center [] with all the information you need to be prepared to vote this year, including guides to the big races, key dates, and more. New: Which Pittsburgh mayoral candidate most aligns with you? Take our quiz [] Get answers to your questions with our AI-powered Election Assistant [] Everything you need to know about mail voting [] , becoming a poll worker [] Everything you need to know about how to vote and where to vote [] Guides to Commonwealth, Superior Courts [] , vetting judicial candidates [] Guides to State College school board [] , Reading City Council president [] Guides to voting as a college student [] En Español Guía para votar por correo [] , la presidencia del Concejo Municipal de Reading [] * Guía para quién está en la papeleta de las primarias [] , cómo convertirse en trabajador electoral el 20 de mayo [] 2. Stay Engaged To protect democracy, we all must stay engaged day in and day out. We can’t just show up right before an election and tune out afterward. If we remain committed, democracy will win. Check out a Montgomery County Commissioner’s effort to educate voters. It's now an emmy-nominated short film. “Running elections in Pennsylvania's third-most-populous county, Neil Makhija said he’s seen the slippery slope from election misinformation to political violence.” ( Philadelphia Inquirer [] ) 3. Share What You Learn Once you’ve figured out what’s going on, share that information with your networks and community. It might feel awkward to bring up voter suppression or changes in election laws when we’re not in the middle of a major election — but local elections happen in off years, and special elections are more common than you think. Now is the perfect time to start conversations about voting. Here, in Pennsylvania, we vote every year, twice a year! 4. Join or Support Pro-Democracy Organizations Is partisan politics not for you? There are numerous nonprofits and grassroots organizations working every day to protect voting rights and ensure free and fair elections. Supporting these groups with your time or resources helps these groups do their work. Check out the work New PA Project has been up to lately below. AND , check out our upcoming events listed above! 5. Become a Trained Poll Worker Many counties face a shortage of poll workers, especially during election season. Being a poll worker requires dedication, attention to detail and a willingness to be trained. It’s a meaningful way to serve your community and help protect the integrity of the voting process. Here are some resources that may be helpful: Pennsylvania Capital-Star - Advocacy groups offer training for Pa. primary poll watchers [] Spotlight PA - Election 2025: How to become a poll worker for the PA primary [] Franklin County Free Press - Poll Workers Needed for Pennsylvania’s 2025 Primary Election [] 6. Engage Your Elected Officials Call and write your elected officials at the federal, state and local levels. Tell them that protecting voting rights and ensuring free and fair elections are your top priorities. Even better, show up at public meetings. Ask them directly what they’re doing to combat voter suppression. Be informed about pending legislation and urge them to support pro-democracy initiatives. This applies no matter where you live or who represents you — Democrat or Republican. Constituent pressure always matters. Don’t let anyone tell you otherwise. 7. Vote in Every Election Yes — every election. That means local elections, primary elections and special elections. Become a super-voter. The more you vote, the more informed and engaged you become. You’ll also be better positioned to notice and report problems — like changes to polling locations or voting equipment — that could impact turnout or accessibility. Make a plan to vote in the primary election, Tuesday, May 20th. When are you voting this year? Who are you going with? How are you voting this year -- by mail or on Election Day? As a reminder, the last day to request a mail ballot is Tuesday, May 13th! Recent Events [] Solidarity for Immigrants On Monday, May 5th, also Cinco de Mayo, over 300 people, representing 18 community organizations from across Pennsylvania, gathered at the State Capitol in Harrisburg to rally for immigrant rights. We amplified voices that have been silenced, advocated against injustice, and showed that solidarity is not just a word—it is a force that creates change. This event was a declaration that Pennsylvania stands against injustice and division. [] [] [] NPPEF on the Ground [] Last Monday, May 5th was the last day to register to vote for the primary election! Our teams were out in their communities leading up to the voter registration deadline on Monday. We helped folks ensure they have the ability to exercise their right to vote in the primary on Tuesday, May 20th. Our teams are currently getting ready for GOTV - a time of year where we are on the ground connecting with our communities and mobilizing them to vote. It's our favorite time of year to build relationships with those we hope to uplift. Dauphin County [] [] Delaware County [] [] Luzerne County [] [] Super voters vote twice a year, every year ! Thank you for doing your part to stay informed and engaged! The House passed the SAVE America Act three times. Senate Democrats have blocked it every single time.

| | | | Fellow American, For the third time, House Republicans passed the SAVE America Act -- legislation that requires voters to prove they are American citizens before casting a ballot in American elections. Voter ID. Proof of citizenship. The most basic, common-sense election integrity measure imaginable. They passed it three times. Every single House Republican voted for it. _Now it sits in the Senate. And Chuck Schumer is sharpening his knife._

name: Fran Hong
subject: The one thing that worries me
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Francesca Hong
body:
New polling on WI gov race
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260807-3128)
Peter,
State Navigate released [another poll](https://act.francescahong.com/go/17711?t=1&akid=3128%2E105371%2E1q5zoh) this morning, and the topline looks great: We're up 22 points on our closest primary rival. If you're riding the pollercoaster with us, I get it, that number feels like it should be enough to relax. It's not.
**[Before I explain why, let me just ask you directly: can you chip in $10 today? I promise the reasoning below will make it worth your two minutes.](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260806.hUrGfv&refcode=em20260807-3128&t=2&akid=3128%2E105371%2E1q5zoh)**
Here's the number buried in the crosstabs that actually worries me: Among voters who've shown up for every primary in the last four cycles, our lead shrinks to just 8 points. Our strongest supporters are the ones with the least practice showing up to vote. That's exactly what we need to fix in the next four days.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260806.hUrGfv&refcode=em20260807-3128&t=3&akid=3128%2E105371%2E1q5zoh)
_Source: State Navigate poll of 1,473 likely Wisconsin Democratic primary voters, conducted Aug. 3–6, 2026. Margin of error ±2.3%_
We've done this with almost no traditional media spending and not a dime of corporate PAC money. It's the energy on the ground from YOU that got us here, and it's the only thing that gets us over the finish line.
More than one in five likely voters surveyed here have already cast their ballot. If you haven't yet, this weekend is your last chance before Tuesday. Whatever showing up looks like for you—voting, knocking doors, donating, or talking to your family—it's the difference between a comfortable lead and a locked-in win.
**[Will you contribute $10, $25, or $50 today to help us reach every voter we can in the final four days?](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260806.hUrGfv&refcode=em20260807-3128&t=4&akid=3128%2E105371%2E1q5zoh)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260806.hUrGfv&amount=5&refcode=em20260807-3128&t=7&akid=3128%2E105371%2E1q5zoh)**
With gratitude,
Fran
**[P.S. Click this link to join us at one of our many GOTV events this weekend. See you there!](https://act.francescahong.com/go/17712?t=8&akid=3128%2E105371%2E1q5zoh)**

Our strongest supporters are the ones with the least practice showing up to vote. That's exactly what we need to fix in the next four days. Source: State Navigate poll of 1,473 likely Wisconsin Democratic primary voters, conducted Aug. 3–6, 2026. Margin of error ±2.3% We've done this with almost no traditional media spending and not a dime of corporate PAC money. It's the energy on the ground from YOU that got us here, and it's the only thing that gets us over the finish line. More than one in five likely voters surveyed here have already cast their ballot. If you haven't yet, this weekend is your last chance before Tuesday. Whatever showing up looks like for you—voting, knocking doors, donating, or talking to your family—it's the difference between a comfortable lead and a locked-in win. Peter,
**We're less than 90 days out from the midterm elections, so I’ll keep this quick:**
1\. Republicans are scared the people will hold them accountable for their billionaires-first agenda and are trying to tip the scales in their favor through redistricting, making it harder to vote, and so much more. But despite all their efforts, the House is still favored to flip blue.
2\. The only way to put a stop to Trump's blatant corruption and start holding his administration accountable to the fullest extent of the law is to flip the Senate, too. That means Democrats need to flip at least FOUR seats on a map that inherently favors the GOP, so it’s an uphill battle now through November.

## Boy's Butterfly Study Stuns Scientists
Jo Nagai started raising swallowtail butterflies at his home in Kobe, Japan, as a second grader. When he released them into the wild, he noticed they would linger and sometimes fly right back to him. It made him wonder whether the [butterflies could remember experiences from their caterpillar days](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHSnSAQBeCn0Y47K3qRW1CksfvTpnRWWYQEwYH1d3z7jHmF9Ge-Oef8-pq_MMSQtp-4k3Gbm9nlOdFVIzFTmbd7T1i5nmkphH9wiVSPUALPEqQSoAWMs8UQ73lorXFEkvqWTDdq1fU9yKH15qMWsMvqdLeMnVQS4D3Cqt1oScEHdRvMo4GGUQL0w_By6k3weWulNEpE2wxANnAur985JPbk4p2_qbzWvLfReOajNv2PRk6NnK7rep3HlQv7-wk0cmJK4iYsIkcrlvOZ5uItClXCsnoqwoa6PmIV7JHFTnsugarAJBYSB9ZKVth8JcG-5HPzYqNEBTnkVBs5tcXY4woxhqrGZoBtxxD_1eP__vXbyL8BAAD__7MUktA). To find out, the boy wrote a four-page letter to Dr. Martha Weiss, a Georgetown University entomologist who had studied memory in moths. What followed was a [years-long collaboration](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSnDAQRL8GMlFaiQUuUOBks3PqkBqJEcxZaChp2C3-3rV24A-4sIN-1f1-fc6fQIny-hN2dHGNs0SeM75qQhEs83rtGarUM_uC8Bt8wnpQIZmNNoPSk9LjvACla-7bxUVEg7ZFdxun4WatNn27OW2j1RiDt4D4oYfRoLHe62Dvo71N2JJ70_SkR6O17fsuDnfUH_dpGCYwAEvTa1xIuHRfTFk2jOniJ5Yu8N4mt4kctbE_GvNozMMTJ16vbkUuKwq_cofL2ZjH-5eqwuX6F9TBS4AqKiLIWbCq_xWFWXh_g6hKVYFTAs8FhDirF8mmjoKBA_FZv-CAjBWVP9_SYrpUwYpQwoalMY-2uOV4UUpUh7Hp9boDpb_T5dvOn878CQAA__-nQZ8B) between a world-renowned scientist and a grade schooler working from a makeshift lab in his house. Jo trained caterpillars to avoid the scent of lavender, then waited to see if the learned behavior survived metamorphosis. It did. The adult butterflies overwhelmingly avoided the scent after undergoing complete metamorphosis inside the chrysalis. Then came the bigger discovery. Jo bred those butterflies and [tested their offspring](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D3O4yAUheHV4M4RvhAgBcU07jLtlOg6XBwy_ERAEnn3o8wWvvpIj3TeP1d3xZhi2X9jJhv24EaortCnJxqDmtuPXLCP_ipbI_yLW6L-jC0OBxzUzM3MtfMY0-Hk5G0gAhIT2UUbtQjBQU53a0hLf1FB32BBob2WAhcQWzgbugi-TdF-NW64Bs6FlKegzsQvZ6OUQUD0THLycdR2etRYxp1COuqb2ulW85TsfYxnZ-IXg5XBmo9cPbWSaXx3BuujzgV3jPP2-r4K6Zj7ePmDwTo165-fmFLsSjPJ94wx_WfHj3u8LfwLAAD__32ydwc), and then their grandchildren. Without ever receiving any training themselves, subsequent generations also avoided lavender. At 10 years old, Jo had produced evidence suggesting transgenerational inheritance of the learned behavior in a 33-page research paper and presented his findings at the International Congress of Entomology in 2024. "_I really want to prove it's possible that my butterflies can remember what they learned as a caterpillar_ ," [Jo had written to Dr. Weiss early on](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb8GOtBgiHEKF9vQZdstrcEek9k1GNlOkP9-lSe9L3jFbe_ROX8e5oEc-Nh-407ab94UH81BVw5UCiWz1f3AXPLrWBPhP1wD5ZMTFyNAyA5UB7NxyKGaqXXaEwkaW9LDrOQwjiCm9qmdvIOkgSYcwc7DYOFu7UhqGGAFT6pl_XkDBbMAGKep9_JGcL8pKRUKRNdMQI5LTP3fyEd5kg81vin1Nu5t0M9SztyMvxqxNGK5rqvfYnTf621sxIKpsA2UG7Gsr4-bD7WzWOjkEDB1O-0x1W6NtTtTdLzVNml3XhwCZzk3E2w7cvgilh-nemvxPwAA__8mRIIC). "_I don't want to give up now_."

Boy's Butterfly Study Stuns Scientists Jo Nagai started raising swallowtail butterflies at his home in Kobe, Japan, as a second grader. When he released them into the wild, he noticed they would linger and sometimes fly right back to him. It made him wonder whether the . To find out, the boy wrote a four-page letter to Dr. Martha Weiss, a Georgetown University entomologist who had studied memory in moths. What followed was a between a world-renowned scientist and a grade schooler working from a makeshift lab in his house. Jo trained caterpillars to avoid the scent of lavender, then waited to see if the learned behavior survived metamorphosis. It did. The adult butterflies overwhelmingly avoided the scent after undergoing complete metamorphosis inside the chrysalis. Then came the bigger discovery. Jo bred those butterflies and , and then their grandchildren. Without ever receiving any training themselves, subsequent generations also avoided lavender. At 10 years old, Jo had produced evidence suggesting transgenerational inheritance of the learned behavior in a 33-page research paper and presented his findings at the International Congress of Entomology in 2024. _Medicaid Cuts Hit Hoosier Families Hard _
[__](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136829451/638727415/1922226100?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2Y2RmYTZmNi05YTkyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=X72o1bb7nxrxnFBZYCOPio6C8DK95DHsWpzDERZ46FE=&emci=1cab63fe-7c92-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=6cdfa6f6-9a92-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=4925535) Due to provisions in Big Bad Bill and in new state laws, over 174,000 Hoosier children have lost access to healthcare in just one year. When adding in adults who have lost Medicaid coverage, the figure grows to over 343,000 Hoosiers. Republicans claim this has lowered Mediciad enrollment in Indiana [by 23%](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136829452/638727416/-67444446?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2Y2RmYTZmNi05YTkyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=X72o1bb7nxrxnFBZYCOPio6C8DK95DHsWpzDERZ46FE=&emci=1cab63fe-7c92-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=6cdfa6f6-9a92-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=4925535) but saved the state only 2% in the past year. While the state coffers might keep a few more dollars, these changes are costing Hoosier families more and more every day. Enrollment and eligibility paperwork is taking families longer than ever to navigate. This is forcing many to ration medication and go without the equipment their children need. Republicans can't be trusted on healthcare. Remember, there's room in the budget for $8 billion in tax breaks for data centers, but not a tiny of fraction of that for Hoosier families needing care. It's time for a change in priorities at the Statehouse this November. _See You on The Porch – French Lick 2026_ _[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136829453/638727417/-875741559?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2Y2RmYTZmNi05YTkyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=X72o1bb7nxrxnFBZYCOPio6C8DK95DHsWpzDERZ46FE=&emci=1cab63fe-7c92-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=6cdfa6f6-9a92-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=4925535)_**ROOM BLOCK NEARLY FULL! _Braun Fires Utility Commissioner Just Eight Months After Appointment_
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136829455/638727419/1821432695?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2Y2RmYTZmNi05YTkyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=X72o1bb7nxrxnFBZYCOPio6C8DK95DHsWpzDERZ46FE=&emci=1cab63fe-7c92-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=6cdfa6f6-9a92-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=4925535) In January, Mike Braun appointed former Republican State Senator Andy Zay to be the next Chair of the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission. By early August, he had been fired. In that time, Zay cast the deciding vote for AES Indiana's massive rate increase case. Governor Braun knew the AES case was on the docket when he appointed Zay earlier this year. He waited until Zay approved the increase, and then fired him by faking shock at the decision. Governor, your party's policies have led to this mess, and every rate increase over the past 20+ years is because of Republican policies. But the Governor chose to appoint him anyway. Hoosiers need new leaders at the Statehouse who will stand up to corporate greed and fight for Hoosier families. The only commissioner to vote against the increase was former Democratic State Senator Bob Deig. _Each week, the State Party will highlight key policy or programs from Democrats at the Statehouse or across the state. Democrats deliver a better future for Hoosier families, and we urge you to share this information with your networks._ _Hoosiers Stand Up to Oppose Central Indiana Hate Rally_ [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136829456/638727420/-1566565729?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2Y2RmYTZmNi05YTkyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=X72o1bb7nxrxnFBZYCOPio6C8DK95DHsWpzDERZ46FE=&emci=1cab63fe-7c92-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&emdi=6cdfa6f6-9a92-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&ceid=4925535) Last weekend, former Border Patrol commander Gregory Bovino headlined a rally for a pro-mass deportation group in a pole tent in an undisclosed location in central Indiana. However, since the announcement of the event, Hoosiers organized to oppose it and send a message that all legal immigrants are welcome in our state. Around 1,000 Hoosiers -- over 10x the number who attended the "rally" -- marched in a Fishers park to send a message that the hatred sold by Republicans who support Bovino wont be tolerated in our communities. Reports from the hate rally showed that Lt. Governor Micah Beckwith and Attorney General Todd Rokita both delivered video remarks to attendees. Bovino also thanked several Indiana Republicans for their support from the stage, including State Rep. Jim Lucas who attended the event. Hoosiers will not stand for hate in our communities. name: Adam Dunigan
subject: The Night is Always Darkest Before the Dawn
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Adam for Congress[Vote](https://us
body:
And a selection of other platitudes people say when they lose elections!

| | | | | |
---
| | | | | |
Good afternoon, everybody!
It’s your boy Adam here. As always, from the heart.
First of all, thank you. Thank you to everyone who came along on this crazy ride for the last seven months. Several people on this email have been there since day one, some of you only joined this ragtag team in the last couple weeks, but everyone contributed in their own way to something amazing.
Obviously, Tuesday felt like a big disappointment to many of us. I took it hard; I knew it was a long shot but I thought we’d have more turnout and more enthusiasm. We didn’t get that, and that’s going to sting. But even if it won’t feel like it for a little while, I know objectively we did better, against bad odds, than anyone could have reasonably expected for a first-time, dark horse candidate.
We survived so many setbacks. From first time jitters, to the Virginia congressional redistricting, to Supreme Court shenanigans, to being overshadowed by the tides of national politics. This was, by all accounts, the worst possible year to enter congressional politics. And we still carved out a respectable swatch of vote share and awareness. It wasn’t enough to win, but it also was nothing to scoff at.
And here would be the time, in a normal campaign, that I’d offer a platitude. I’d say something like, “we’re taking time to reassess," or, “I’m going to focus on my family before making any decisions.” But I don’t have a family, and the core of our mission will never change. All I can do right now is dust myself off and get back to work. So that’s what I’m going to do, and I hope you’ll join me for the next phase.
I’m going to take these next few weeks to close out the 2026 campaign logistics, compile a retrospective on lessons learned, and collect ideas and talent for our 2028 campaign. We will enthusiastically support Congressman Beyer on November 3rd. But November 4th, we take the field again. And this time, we play to win. The establishment is on notice, and they will either see the light or feel the heat. They’ll make their choices. But either way, in the immortal words of Leonardo DiCaprio in _The Wolf of Wallstreet_ , “I’m not leaving.”
So, if you’re in your own feelings about the primary results across the country this year, so am I. But take heart: This was a prologue. Chapter 1 starts now. I hope you’ll be a part of it. And for all of those feeling uncertain, know this: The gates don’t ever come down with one strike of the battering ram, and a siege is never won in a single day. If Tuesday was our Dunkirk, it’s time to plan Normandy.
---
| |

clean_body: And a selection of other platitudes people say when they lose elections! | | | | | | | | | | | | Good afternoon, everybody! It’s your boy Adam here. As always, from the heart. First of all, thank you. Thank you to everyone who came along on this crazy ride for the last seven months. Several people on this email have been there since day one, some of you only joined this ragtag team in the last couple weeks, but everyone contributed in their own way to something amazing. Obviously, Tuesday felt like a big disappointment to many of us. I took it hard; I knew it was a long shot but I thought we’d have more turnout and more enthusiasm. We didn’t get that, and that’s going to sting. But even if it won’t feel like it for a little while, I know objectively we did better, against bad odds, than anyone could have reasonably expected for a first-time, dark horse candidate. We survived so many setbacks. From first time jitters, to the Virginia congressional redistricting, to Supreme Court shenanigans, to being overshadowed by the tides of national politics. This was, by all accounts, the worst possible year to enter congressional politics. And we still carved out a respectable swatch of vote share and awareness. It wasn’t enough to win, but it also was nothing to scoff at. And here would be the time, in a normal campaign, that I’d offer a platitude. I’d say something like, “we’re taking time to reassess," or, “I’m going to focus on my family before making any decisions.” But I don’t have a family, and the core of our mission will never change. All I can do right now is dust myself off and get back to work. So that’s what I’m going to do, and I hope you’ll join me for the next phase. I’m going to take these next few weeks to close out the 2026 campaign logistics, compile a retrospective on lessons learned, and collect ideas and talent for our 2028 campaign. We will enthusiastically support Congressman Beyer on November 3rd. But November 4th, we take the field again. And this time, we play to win. The establishment is on notice, and they will either see the light or feel the heat. They’ll make their choices. But either way, in the immortal words of Leonardo DiCaprio in The Wolf of Wallstreet , “I’m not leaving.” So, if you’re in your own feelings about the primary results across the country this year, so am I. But take heart: This was a prologue. Chapter 1 starts now. I hope you’ll be a part of it. And for all of those feeling uncertain, know this: The gates don’t ever come down with one strike of the battering ram, and a siege is never won in a single day. If Tuesday was our Dunkirk, it’s time to plan Normandy. | | Your friend,Adam Dunigan Future* Congressional CandidateVirginia's 8th District | | | | | | Paid for by Adam for Congress | | | | | | | or |

Jeremy Kernodle, appointed by Trump to the federal bench, blocked the
FTC's updated merger disclosure rule — a rule that would have forced
companies to disclose more information before major mergers.

...now they don’t have to.

Here's who wins: big corporations and Wall Street dealmakers who want to
merge, consolidate, and squeeze out competition with as little scrutiny as
possible.

Here's who loses: everyone else. Every small business trying to compete.
Every family paying higher prices. Every worker whose job depends on
markets that aren't rigged by monopolies.

That’s Trump’s whole plan. He appointed judges to tilt the scales toward
billionaires and powerful corporations, and away from working Americans.
Judge Kernodle is doing exactly what he was put on the bench to do.

Demand Justice exists to fight back. We expose judges like Kernodle. We
hold the federal bench accountable. And we make sure people know when a
ruling isn't about the law, but about who the judge was sent there to
protect.

| | | Peter,
---
Growing up in Allagash and spending years working 80-hour weeks in the woods to make ends meet, I know firsthand what working Mainers need from our government.
And for 30 years, Susan Collins has failed us. Time and again, she has sold us out to Donald Trump and his MAGA agenda while pretending we’re too dumb to notice. **And I’m sick of it. **
My name is Troy Jackson. I’m a proud Mainer, father, and fifth-generation logger.
[**_I officially earned the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate. Now it’s time to defeat Susan Collins and her billionaire backers. So I’m asking you to split a donation between my campaign and April Delaney to become a Founding Donor to my campaign right now and help us win the most important Senate race in the country. _**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136829880/638728875/1716773837?refcode=BLU_EM_AMDC_2026-08-07_02&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDkxNzIiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNGIzMTM5YzYtOWM5Mi1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAwZDNhMTFmYTMwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=sq5ELuDg_ro7JRP2JpV0gLj_yvfNMp1O8vlsbH0Myxw=)

| | | Peter, let me tell you a bit about what this race means to me.
---
When I was growing up, I was a poor kid in a town full of poor kids. My family relied on food assistance at times. I distinctly remember when I was 13 years old, we didn’t have heat or running water, and I heard my mother quietly crying to herself, wishing she could do more for us.
After high school, I became a logger like my dad, and his dad, and his dad before him. When a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and me out of fair wages, I fought back. A whole bunch of politicians, including then-first-term Senator Susan Collins, promised to listen, but they left us high and dry — and I realized that _nothing would change_ unless there were working-class voices in power.
So I ran for the Maine legislature, where I served 20 years, including six years as the President of the Maine Senate. It’s been the honor of my life to fight for working people.
I drove hours each way between the North Woods and the State Capitol, because that's what the job required. I won those elections in a district that went for Trump by 20 points, because up here, people care less about a label and more about whether you give a damn about their family.
I’m building this campaign the right way. With grassroots support from folks like you. I’m not running to impress the billionaires or the corporate class. I’m running for the mom who’s worried about how she’ll fill her gas tank this week. I’m running for the kid whose whole life will be determined by the quality of his education. I’m running to ensure every working family in Maine has the government they deserve.

Derek, if you’ve
turned on your TV anytime in the last few weeks, you might’ve seen
something: My far-right opponent has officially launched her first attack
ads against me.

I won’t lie to you — this wasn’t unexpected. I’ve run in competitive races
like this one before, so I’m not a stranger to the smears and lies that
are being spread.

I also know that these attacks are only going to get more frequent — and
more ugly — the closer we get to November 3rd.

Here’s the reality of this race: We can’t control what the other side
does. We can’t stop them from buying air time or spreading lies about this
campaign. But we can control how we respond.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/5687?t=1002&akid=177%2E245147%2EUYipNV ]It’s now more urgent than ever that we have the resources to correct
the record, defend ourselves from the other side’s attacks, and reach
undecided voters with the truth about our movement. That’s why I’m
reaching out today — can I count on you to pitch in whatever you can to
help me fight back?

If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your

Look, I’m used to the odds being stacked against me.
I grew up in a mobile home park, the daughter of a hardworking single mom. I worked two jobs to put myself through college. I fought to adopt my son while a state government tried to stop me, because having two moms wasn’t in the “best interests” of my child. And I flipped a red Congressional seat blue, while the GOP spent millions to try to defeat me.

Peter, The other night in McKinney, a routine procedural vote on a mosque that had already met every one of the city's zoning requirements turned into a circus. **Keith Self made sure of it. ** He showed up and started cranking out the greatest hits of his routine racist lies. clean_body: | Peter, I'm going to make a prediction... When the votes are counted this November, the radical left is going to be in a state of total shock. And the political establishment is going to spend weeks trying to explain what hit them. But that only happens if Republicans like you are on record before the Midterms. That is how consequential this moment is. But here is the part the pundits won't tell you. None of that happens automatically. The Democrats are at war with the American people -- open borders, defunding ICE, eliminating voter ID, putting men in women's sports. You name it, they are on the wrong side of it. And yet they are running the most radical, well-funded Senate candidates in states across this country who are counting on Republicans to stay home and let them walk right in. I will not let that happen. And I don't think you will either. I made you a prediction at the beginning of this email. I stand by every word of it. But that prediction is built on one assumption -- that Republicans like you are engaged and ready to fight. That is where your assessment comes in. **Monday, August 10 | 6:30 -7:30 PM (ET)**
**Virtual via Zoom** **Register here:**
[https://us06web.zoom.us/meeting/register/-qYJ-7aVTuq4x3vsabo4Fg](https://clicksp.bradstockforcongress.com/f/a/MZiU0O7djHruADZYpB144A~~/AAPPABA~/EjvNR6mmBN8T5UbjY3_W6vHiKbo1hFviliy-uFPFEHgcjGWR8Se2kV9Ixxyy9Esc3rHIu_FHY7uRKNKoN4L1OKDMWL-JZbfQcbwYxSUfbxGsZJeAXqy5CkynDVnqdQBtd0Z4_r8cP1YP62EqdP5Jh4pnYBn5CLysSZBz_wRMqc5ee_dgIHacC6B5bN2tygcD_tIt1164HGtt1BwgFH8t9CEVst3IaVGr3GAs7OJ8OG8UsMBdw74XV_n_HBK1DLnMxdwmQTpxvpLUIyxEQqZ6-XbbQCjIhy-2P2CQXFjlxOx7akP9DOZ8nmPK80FU9BLV) Reach is a free app that lets you volunteer from anywhere--whether you live in Pennsylvania's 14th Congressional District or across the country. Think of it as **door-knocking from your phone.** Instead of knocking on strangers' doors, you'll connect with friends, family, neighbors, coworkers, and others you already know, having the conversations that are often the most effective at persuading voters. During the webinar, you'll learn how to:
* Build your personal network in Reach.
* Canvas anyone in PA-14 using built-in scripts and survey questions.
* Share campaign content with any contact in your phone.
* Invite friends and family to events and volunteer opportunities.
* Identify supporters and encourage them to vote.
* Volunteer anytime, from anywhere, using just your phone.

clean_body: | | Dear Friend, Winning campaigns aren't built only through television ads or door knocking--they're built through trusted conversations between friends, family, neighbors, and coworkers. Join Alan Bradstock and our campaign team on Monday evening for a special Reach & Relational Organizing Webinar. Alan will share why personal conversations are critical to winning this race before our team demonstrates how Reach helps every supporter become an effective volunteer. 📅 Reach & Relational Organizing Webinar Monday, August 10 | 6:30 -7:30 PM (ET) Virtual via Zoom Register here: Reach is a free app that lets you volunteer from anywhere--whether you live in Pennsylvania's 14th Congressional District or across the country. Think of it as door-knocking from your phone. Instead of knocking on strangers' doors, you'll connect with friends, family, neighbors, coworkers, and others you already know, having the conversations that are often the most effective at persuading voters. During the webinar, you'll learn how to: Build your personal network in Reach. Canvas anyone in PA-14 using built-in scripts and survey questions. Share campaign content with any contact in your phone. Invite friends and family to events and volunteer opportunities. Identify supporters and encourage them to vote. Volunteer anytime, from anywhere, using just your phone. You can also download Reach, join the Bradstock campaign, and learn more about relational organizing anytime at ~~ Every new Reach volunteer helps us expand our campaign one conversation at a time. We look forward to seeing you on Monday as we continue building the grassroots movement that will help elect Alan Bradstock to Congress. Thank you for being part of Team Bradstock! Phillip Whoriskey Field Director Bradstock for Congress 703-869-4480 BradstockforCongress.com P.S. Every volunteer helps us reach more voters, and every contribution helps us organize more volunteers. If you'd like to support our field program, please consider making a contribution of any amount to help us continue growing our grassroots campaign. ➡️ ~~ | ~~ "Facebook" "Instagram" mailto:info@bradstockforcongress.com "Email" ~ "Bluesky" "X" ~ "YouTube" Bradstock for Congress P.O. name: Chris Pappas
subject: Outspent 2:1.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
For every dollar our campaign is putting into reaching voters, Republicans and their outside groups are spending twice as much to flood New Hampshire’s airwaves with attack ads.
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=8174%2E582294%2EhHAuIj)
It’s Chris.
I wish I didn’t have to write this email, but I need to be transparent with you about what we’re up against:
_Right now we’re being outspent 2:1._
**For every dollar our campaign is putting into reaching voters, Republicans and their outside groups are spending twice as much to flood New Hampshire’s airwaves with attack ads.**
National GOP groups are pouring millions into the Granite State because they know what happens here could decide control of the Senate.
Their strategy is simple: spend as much as they can, as fast as they can, and try to drown out our message to voters.
But Granite Staters don’t let outside groups decide their elections. They want to hear directly from candidates. They want to know who will fight to lower costs, protect reproductive freedom, and deliver results for their families.
**That’s why we need to make sure our campaign message can break through.**
Our campaign is powered by grassroots supporters – people who believe New Hampshire deserves a senator who answers to them, not Washington insiders or special interests.
But when the other side has a 2-to-1 spending advantage, we need your help to keep pace.
**[Can you chip in $5 today to help us fight back against this unprecedented flood of spending and make sure voters across New Hampshire hear our message?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260807_3.XfaNR0&refcode=em20260807-3&t=2&akid=8174%2E582294%2EhHAuIj)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260807_3.XfaNR0&amount=5&refcode=em20260807-3&t=21&akid=8174%2E582294%2EhHAuIj)**
Our campaign is entirely funded by grassroots supporters just like you, stepping up and chipping in whatever they can.
With this race entering its final stretch, your contribution is important now more than ever. **[Will you make a donation of $5 or more today?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260807_3.XfaNR0&refcode=em20260807-3&t=22&akid=8174%2E582294%2EhHAuIj)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260807_3.XfaNR0&amount=5&refcode=em20260807-3&t=23&akid=8174%2E582294%2EhHAuIj)**
Thank you for being part of this.
Chris
**New Hampshire is poised to be one of the closest Senate races in the country. Will you chip in today to help Chris stop the Republicans from flipping the Granite State red and expanding their Senate majority?**
**[Donate »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_cp_footer?refcode=em20260807-3&t=24&refcode2=8174_582294_hHAuIj&akid=8174%2E582294%2EhHAuIj)**

The NHGOP Victory Report - 8/7/26

| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Dear Friend,

**A Note from the Chairman:**

Republicans across New Hampshire have a lot to be proud of—and even more to look forward to.Our party is moving forward. We are working every day to build a stronger, more modern, and more effective Republican Party that reaches more Granite Staters and gives our candidates the tools they need to win.We are expanding our presence on social media, strengthening our communications, supporting our local committees, and finding new ways to grow our grassroots movement. But none of that happens without the people who make up this party.**The New Hampshire Republican Party is not just a committee or a set of social media accounts. It is you.** Our strength comes from Republicans who are willing to show up, get involved, and work together. Whether you have been involved for decades or are just getting started, **we need you.** The road to victory in November starts now—in our communities and neighborhoods. Talk to your friends and neighbors. Attend a local meeting. Volunteer. Support a candidate. Share our message. Bring someone new into our movement.When our grassroots are strong, our party is strong. And when we are united and working together, **we win elections.** As we head toward the 2026 elections, I am asking Republicans across New Hampshire to take the next step and find a way to get involved. There is a place for you in this movement.**We are building momentum. We are building our party. And together, we are building the foundation for victory in November.** Thank you for being part of the New Hampshire Republican Party. I look forward to seeing you on the campaign trail, in our communities, and at events across the state.
---
| | | | | | **Mammoth Brigade:** On July 30th, we launched the Mammoth Brigade, a new grassroots movement dedicated to increasing Republican voter turnout across New Hampshire.The mission is simple: when Republicans vote, Republicans win. Your commitment can help expand our reach, strengthen Republican turnout, and build the momentum needed for victory in 2026.Sign up today and commit to casting your ballot, and helping others do the same. Together, we can win in November! [**JOIN THE MAMMOTH BRIGADE**](https://us.list-manage.com/spKS3fS2xxT?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=ufQ9FudTC3uvHgEaZaiRvTpkVB1olg-sGW9ZOE0hpcH3QtxzjOsFj7nH4Q==)******Every vote at the ballot box counts because every vote in Concord and Washington, DC counts.**
---
| | | | | | **Unity Breakfast:** We are thrilled to announce the date for our historic Unity Breakfast! Mark your calendars and stay tuned for more information coming soon!
---
|
---
| |
**NHGOP on Air!** Chairman Maltzie was on Jack Heath’s The Pulse of NH yesterday! Listen to the full interview [here](https://us.list-manage.com/d4zRaiKQf7a?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=dTLVxjQnUxZ2MqkCN99rM18_MYmbCfNIuEEtfT0HduMhzm_TSrRBFZXkpw==)

Looking for upcoming Republican events across New Hampshire? Visit the [**Calendar**](https://us.list-manage.com/EiOqbe33GC3?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=jANGMCONjF9iozZloZRTxlKo1vsQML1epYGbCJnIAhjnYysjM2knqbvPbg==) section of our website for a full list of events.Have an event we’re missing? Click the red **“Submit My Event”** button on the calendar page to add it to our list!

**Legislative Update:** On Wednesday, August 19, the House will convene at 10:00 a.m., followed by the Senate at 1:00 p.m., to consider the Governor’s vetoes.

**Social Media:** Be sure to follow us on social media!We encourage you to share our posts so that we can continue to reach more people!

**TikTok:** [https://www.tiktok.com/@nhrepublicanparty](https://us.list-manage.com/CJqJQtNr42_?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=iw1GYp95B3s5CzhgNMyMMQrMhHLa6RDUKSUbnwzRvQljS3toGWdlf09V2A==) (nhrepublicanparty)
**YouTube:** [https://www.youtube.com/@NH_GOP](https://us.list-manage.com/BdiJuL1LkQb?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=URjT_cOZ5HcUj3mFZ1LcMWKf3cj4btV2wJNxJqzqgsrI583RJ0i_WfUowg==) (NH_GOP)

Check out our July recap [video](https://us.list-manage.com/12CUSxobKu1?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=OP2JE5fmi-5kX6vXCm_qPQuagDisVf_elQz_0fGJ5q84gfL0wLKciN8U1Q==)!

**Grassroots Givers:** Become a Grassroots Giver today!With $10/month or $120/year you help us:
* Target 20,000 voters through Facebook and Google ads
* Send 1500 texts to targeted voters to Get Out The Vote
* Send 325 mail pieces targeting vulnerable State House Democrats
* Pay half the cost of an ad on TV promoting our candidates
* Purchase a digital billboard for an entire day

Our goal is to have 1,000 Grassroots Givers. Won't you join us in investing in YOUR New Hampshire Republican Party?[https://secure.winred.com/new-hampshire-gop/grassroots-givers](https://us.list-manage.com/ZhuAeXQLU_r?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=0hNbMygM5eP7XVOB8lz4sfEyO7k8OAA_eSjdqDTEjVpNLamIpE9rMGEFFg==)

**Stay tuned for our next newsletter, featuring a fresh new look and a revamped format!**

Sincerely,

Scott MaltzieChairman

Donald Trump is going back to the same playbook.
Instead of answering for rising costs, attacks on healthcare, or the damage his policies have done to working families, he's reviving long-debunked conspiracy theories about the 2020 election.
Why? Because it's easier to distract Americans than defend a failed record.

Way to Lead didn't wait for national Democrats to tell us these races were winnable. We got in early because that's exactly the strategy we need.
Now the DCCC's list of competitive districts has grown to 59 seats, and all but one of the races we identified in January are now on their list. That's real validation of what we've believed all along: some of the best pickup opportunities are in places national groups overlook until the candidates and organizers on the ground prove them wrong.
At the start of this year, many Democrats were still playing defense when they needed to be on offense. We knew we had to take the fight to Republicans and go after their territory to punish them for what they’re doing right now—and we knew that if we approached it with a careful strategy, it was possible. **We just needed to get more people to expand their imagination.**
This is also exactly why we've been doubling down on the South and Southwest. These regions are historically the core of Republican power, and the 2030 census will shift even more congressional seats and electoral power there. body:
Meet Ismael, Daniel, and Nikhil.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260807-2&t=1&akid=3841%2E587540%2ET7JjXt)
Peter, I’m very excited to share our latest endorsements with you:
**Leaders We Deserve is officially endorsing Ismael Luna for WI-AD-08, Daniel Lander for MA-SD-Suffolk & Middlesex, and Nikhil Goyal for VT-SD-Chittenden Central!**
These candidates come from different backgrounds and different communities, but they're united by a common belief: **government should work for everyday people — not corporate interests or the political establishment.**
They're exactly the kind of bold, values-driven leaders our movement exists to support.
**[Will you split a contribution of $5 between Leaders We Deserve and these three incredible candidates today?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260807_2_sle.cQu74w&refcode=em20260807-3841&amount=5&t=2&akid=3841%2E587540%2ET7JjXt)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260807_2_sle.cQu74w&amount=5&refcode=em20260807-3841&t=3&akid=3841%2E587540%2ET7JjXt)**
**Ismael Luna knows firsthand what it means to overcome hardship.** Raised by immigrant parents, Ismael experienced homelessness as a teenager. Today, he works at a homeless shelter helping others find stability and has dedicated years to serving his community through homeless outreach, food programs, substance use recovery efforts, and the American Red Cross.
Now he's running because he believes Wisconsin's South Side deserves leadership rooted in lived experience. He'll fight to fully fund public schools, lower costs for working families, expand affordable housing and health care, invest in recovery programs, protect immigrant families, and create safer communities through prevention — _not_ punishment. Ismael is running against Democratic incumbent Sylvia Ortiz-Vele, who in the past year was both briefly barred from the Statehouse for allegedly threatening her fellow Democratic colleagues with an automatic weapon and faced charges of disorderly conduct for alleged threats made to another fellow representative. If we want voters to have faith in our party again, we can’t afford to let Democrats like Ortiz-Vele keep their seats.
**Daniel Lander has spent the last four years helping make Boston a more affordable place to live as a senior policy advisor to Mayor Michelle Wu.** He helped identify land for hundreds of affordable homes, cut permitting delays for affordable housing, expanded free access to cultural institutions for families, preserved affordable music rehearsal space while creating new affordable housing, and supported dozens of local small businesses.
Now Daniel is running to bring that same results-driven leadership to the Massachusetts Senate. He'll fight to protect immigrant communities from unlawful federal attacks, defend LGBTQ+ people, strengthen public education, tackle the housing crisis, and stand up as an independent progressive voice willing to challenge the status quo. Daniel is running against Democratic incumbent William Brownsberger who, during his tenure as State Senator, has killed affordable housing bills, backed regressive tax cuts, fought against unions, and opposed municipal negotiations for employee health care.
**Nikhil Goyal has spent his career fighting for children, educators, and working families.** The son of Indian immigrants, Nikhil served as a senior policy advisor to Senator Bernie Sanders on education and children's issues, teaches sociology at the University of Vermont, and helped lead statewide coalitions defending public education and protecting juvenile justice reforms.
He's running because Vermont deserves bold leadership that puts people first. Nikhil will fight for universal health care, affordable housing, strong public schools, immigrant communities, public transit, climate action, and an economy that works for working families — not just the wealthy.
**These candidates represent a new generation of leaders who aren't afraid to challenge the status quo, reject corporate influence, and fight for their communities.**
But people-powered campaigns don't have mega-donors or corporate PACs to fall back on. They rely on grassroots supporters stepping up early so they can compete, organize, and win.
Together, we can help elect leaders who will fight for working people — and inspire the next generation to do the same. **[So, Peter, will you split a contribution of $5 between Leaders We Deserve and the campaigns of Ismael Luna, Daniel Lander, and Nikhil Goyal today?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260807_2_sle.cQu74w&refcode=em20260807-3841&amount=5&t=4&akid=3841%2E587540%2ET7JjXt)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260807_2_sle.cQu74w&amount=5&refcode=em20260807-3841&t=23&akid=3841%2E587540%2ET7JjXt)**
With gratitude,
David Hogg

body:
https://www.apipennsylvania.org [https://www.apipennsylvania.org]
Hi Peter,
Even though I only spent the first three years of my life with my grandfather, Agha Gak, it feels like his shadow follows me to this day. Growing up in Pakistan, I knew him as a schoolteacher and lover of learning. Even more, I knew him to be gentle, humble, and silly. He was ridiculed by other men in our community for being “too” expressive and for encouraging his wife and daughters’ independence. To them, he was failing in his duty to be the domineering, stoic, and strict male head of the family. To him, he was following the sunnah, or the life of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. To me, he was modeling a way of being in the world that I would never stop clinging to.
Unfortunately, Agha Gak was not able to join us when we immigrated to the United States. Despite this, we carry him fondly in our hearts and tongues, invoking his memory and character whenever this world becomes too heavy for us. These days, I think of him when I give my little brother advice. He’s 12 years younger than me, and advising him often feels scary because the world feels like it’s on fire: Tech oligarchs are exploiting our data and building data centers in our communities, genocides are happening across the world, the climate crisis is escalating, and ICE is kidnapping our neighbors from our communities. What are we supposed to do amidst all this?
Mariame Kaba says that “hope is a discipline,” and that’s why I pull on my grandfather’s memory when I advise my brother. Because he taught me that there is a better world - one that we can build with our actions today - in spite of the grave things we see around us. We can put power back into the hands of the people, end U.S. aid to Israeli apartheid, abolish ICE, end the climate crisis, and so much more. It certainly starts with embodying the kind of softness, compassion, and open-mindedness that we seek from others, but this work also needs a home. API PA is a movement center where all of us, no matter our age, can develop hope, find community, take collective action, and build intergenerational power.
If you’re interested in finding a home like this, I encourage you to read more.
Sameem Ahmadzai
Eastern Pennsylvania Voter Registration Manager
Asian Pacific Islander Political Alliance
Protecting Philly Small Businesses
Philadelphia’s small businesses are the heart of our neighborhoods, and protecting them means building a city where everyone has a fair shot to thrive. We’re calling on city leaders to make sure wealthy corporations pay what they owe in taxes so Philadelphia can invest in the things our communities need: good public schools for our children, reliable SEPTA service to get us where we're going, and strong public services to help all of us thrive. Sign our petition today and join us in demanding a Philadelphia that works for everyone. Ending collaboration with ICE in Dauphin County
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AV001/1/82704/images/07.23.2026%20Harrisburg%20Community%20Check%20In.jpg]
Everyone should be able to access public services, seek help, and care for their families without fear that doing so could lead to immigration enforcement. We’re working with community members to urge the Dauphin County Commissioners to pass a Welcoming County Resolution that protects residents’ privacy and ends unnecessary collaboration between county agencies and ICE. By ensuring personal information is not shared without a judicial warrant and that county resources are not used to assist immigration enforcement, we can help build a Dauphin County where immigrant and refugee families are treated with dignity, feel safe asking for help, and know that their county government is there to support them.
Sign the Petition [https://www.apipennsylvania.org/welcoming-dauphin?contactdata=dMtLESsKAlxa0DjzZ+O3yqYY/iLa9d5pVIXzf2s3Ho3gVLqrHDKdfn78lhxnc1JJho7KO/zM7004ql6mptOYsSEdmlqOh9ap2aDDBRrRPtvaP/bwJs+1GpDzFgoyMivPh1w4oD9hushAYgeHF7j23i8PQCYbirEtBT/21XVXrzc=]

We can put power back into the hands of the people, end U.S. aid to Israeli apartheid, abolish ICE, end the climate crisis, and so much more. It certainly starts with embodying the kind of softness, compassion, and open-mindedness that we seek from others, but this work also needs a home. API PA is a movement center where all of us, no matter our age, can develop hope, find community, take collective action, and build intergenerational power. If you’re interested in finding a home like this, I encourage you to read more. Sameem Ahmadzai Eastern Pennsylvania Voter Registration Manager Asian Pacific Islander Political Alliance Protecting Philly Small Businesses Philadelphia’s small businesses are the heart of our neighborhoods, and protecting them means building a city where everyone has a fair shot to thrive. We’re calling on city leaders to make sure wealthy corporations pay what they owe in taxes so Philadelphia can invest in the things our communities need: good public schools for our children, reliable SEPTA service to get us where we're going, and strong public services to help all of us thrive. Sign our petition today and join us in demanding a Philadelphia that works for everyone. [=] Sign the Petition [=] Ending collaboration with ICE in Dauphin County [] Everyone should be able to access public services, seek help, and care for their families without fear that doing so could lead to immigration enforcement. We’re working with community members to urge the Dauphin County Commissioners to pass a Welcoming County Resolution that protects residents’ privacy and ends unnecessary collaboration between county agencies and ICE. By ensuring personal information is not shared without a judicial warrant and that county resources are not used to assist immigration enforcement, we can help build a Dauphin County where immigrant and refugee families are treated with dignity, feel safe asking for help, and know that their county government is there to support them. Sign the Petition [=] Upcoming Events Philadelphia Philadelphia General Meeting [=] - Come meet other Asian American community members at our next general meeting on Thursday, August 13th at 7 PM. We’ll have a meal and hear from special guests from " Tax Billionaires, Fund PA [] " Volunteer with Asian Americans United to support immigrants [] - Many of our community members are being detained each day when they arrive for their legally mandated check-in appointments with ICE. Asian Americans United is training volunteers to provide resources directly to people going into the ICE office in Center City. Affordability Outreach - Join us on August 16th [=] , August 18th [=] , or August 27th [=] to talk with our neighbors about how rising prices are affecting their families, businesses, and everyday lives. Your conversations will help us better understand what our communities need and build the power to fight for a Philadelphia where everyone can afford to thrive. Harrisburg Harrisburg Community Check-in [=] - Have a meal and spend time with your fellow Asian Americans in the Harrisburg area on August 27th at 7 PM. We'll discuss ways to get involved in our ongoing campaigns to protect and take care of our communities. Upcoming Events By becoming a member of API PA, you'll help us expand multilingual outreach, develop resources in more languages, and ensure that every Asian American community in Pennsylvania has the information they need to stay informed, engaged, and empowered. subject: Judicial Watch Seeks Biden DOJ Lawfare Evidence
body:
Kamala’s Costly Border Project Fails

[INSIDE JW]

JUDICIAL WATCH SEEKS EVIDENCE OF BIDEN JUSTICE DEPARTMENT’S LAWFARE

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84633&L=38434&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly95b3V0dS5iZS9sd2lLY3U1bmYtST91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=ac0cecc1533e53f0ee561243e5baaa539456f78d3097da7dc436d475f16ed923]

Judicial Watch joined Victoria Toensing, a former attorney for
President Donald J. Trump, in filing
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84633&L=38432&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL3RvZW5zaW5nLW1vdGlvbi10by11bnNlYWwtYXVndXN0LTIwMjYvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=9280a99dedba0d0ec3efd0e601997f930eee1825701a9ee9b90ec3b167389279]
a motion to unseal materials related to three search warrants
targeting Toensing’s iCloud account, Gmail account, and cell phone
(_In re Search Warrants Executed on April 28, 2021_ (No. 21-mc-00425
(JPO))).

We filed the motion before U.S. District Judge J. Paul Oetken of the
U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, seeking
materials related to:

> • A November 4, 2019, warrant authorizing the government to seize
> and search all records contained in Toensing’s iCloud account;
>
> • A December 13, 2019, warrant authorizing the government to seize
> and search Toensing’s Gmail account; and
>
> • An April 28, 2021, warrant authorizing the government to search
> the contents of the cell phone federal agents seized from Toensing
> at her Maryland residence.

On April 22, 2021, shortly after President Biden took office, the U.S.
District Court for the District of Maryland issued a warrant
authorizing federal agents to search Toensing’s Maryland home,
including all locked and closed containers within it, to find and
seize her cell phone and iPad. The warrant also authorized agents to
compel Toensing to unlock the devices using her fingerprints and/or
facial recognition.

Agents seized her cell phone, which was then transported to the
Southern District of New York, where the government obtained a warrant
to search its entire contents. The seizure occurred on the same day
the FBI raided the home and office of former New York City Mayor Rudy
Giuliani. The warrants, applications, affidavits, and related
materials remain under seal to this day, and Toensing has never been
told the reasons for the searches.

Toensing is a lawyer and legal commentator, a former federal
prosecutor and Deputy Assistant Attorney General, and former Chief
Counsel of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence. To her
knowledge, she has never been the target of an investigation. She has
never been charged with any crime.

In their motion, Toensing and Judicial Watch state:

> Here, Judicial Watch is investigating the potential politicization
> of numerous federal law enforcement agencies and whether they abused
> their powers to attack associates of a political opponent.

***

> Here, the presumption of public access clearly outweighs any
> countervailing factors. The records are being sought to enhance the
> public’s understanding of the United States’ targeting of
> President Trump’s attorney by the Biden administration. The public
> has a real interest in knowing the evidence underlying the search
> warrant application and whether the warrant was sought for
> legitimate law enforcement purposes rather than to target a
> political opponent’s ally. These questions cannot be examined
> while the materials remain sealed.

***

> In addition, the investigation appears to have concluded, and
> Toensing was never charged. There is no ongoing prosecution that
> disclosure could jeopardize, no witness whose safety is at risk, and
> no trial whose fairness could be compromised.

Toensing and Judicial Watch also have a motion pending in the U.S.
District Court for the District of Maryland to unseal the materials
related to the April 22, 2021, warrant used to search her home (No.
21-mj-01202-GLS).

“The Biden Administration targeted Rudy Giuliani and me as
retaliation for exposing Biden family corruption in Ukraine. In doing
so, the Biden DOJ and FBI created a pretextual criminal investigation
of us,” Toensing said. “Justice requires that we learn the false
statements used to punish us for speaking the truth.”

The American people have a right to know why the Biden Justice
Department secretly targeted President Trump’s attorney Victoria
Toensing. These ‘lawfare’ search warrant records have remained
hidden for years, even though Toensing was never charged with a crime.

We have taken a leading role in exposing the politicization and
weaponization of federal law enforcement. We recently moved to unseal
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84633&L=38117&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvbWljaGFlbC1jYXB1dG9zLWdvb2dsZS1hY2NvdW50Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=73c5fc415ee4be3e21c3605e76662a5204d059787dd5bbae1054a51c0233ca9d] the
search warrant materials related to a November 18, 2024, warrant that
authorized the federal government to seize the entire Google account
of Michael Caputo, a longtime ally and policy advisor to President
Donald J. Trump.

We also previously moved to unseal
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84633&L=27830&F=T&&hash=1403a0b3312523bd4a3e190ab53e1bdbb7d698cf7d2e98f2910a108b8b07019b]
the search warrant materials used in the FBI’s August 2022 raid on
Trump’s Mar-a-Lago home and to publish
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84633&L=38095&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvanVkaWNpYWwtd2F0Y2gtYXNrcy1jb3VydC1mb3ItY2FydGVyLXBhZ2UtZmlzYS13YXJyYW50LWhlYXJpbmctdHJhbnNjcmlwdHMvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&hash=8a66a48f3c2ed269275caead9d8ddeb70c7f28a7f106c4c8ab2137b6cc86e21e]
the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court transcripts relating to
the surveillance of former Trump campaign advisor Carter Page.

In addition, we are currently pursuing multiple Freedom of Information
Act (FOIA) lawsuits for records about the investigations of other
Trump allies.

In April 2026, we sued
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84633&L=37550&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvcmFpZC1vbi1ydWR5LWdpdWxpYW5pLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=3a4eafe631aef830f305833ad8dc8df74b0d413806be978e4cce106f721efc43] the Justice
Department for records on the Biden FBI’s search warrants used in
the April 2021 raid on former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani’s
residence and office (_Judicial Watch Inc. v. U.S. Department of
Justice_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84633&L=37561&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLWdpdWxpYW5pLWNvbXBsYWludC0wMTE1OC9dXz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=4df601fc84f0032af4c39745efe6bf484126cd2a59e48d80bef643a72282ba4c _(No.
1:26-cv-01158)). Giuliani served as a personal attorney and informal
advisor to Trump.

In November 2025, we sued
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=84633&L=38097&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLWxpbmRlbGwtY29tcGxhaW50LTAzODUwLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&hash=b805d2de62e0d4ae09fbb67d1c367c18ba165e83bfd10daf38028ee83c5dbb59]

On April 22, 2021, shortly after President Biden took office, the U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland issued a warrant authorizing federal agents to search Toensing’s Maryland home, including all locked and closed containers within it, to find and seize her cell phone and iPad. The warrant also authorized agents to compel Toensing to unlock the devices using her fingerprints and/or facial recognition. Agents seized her cell phone, which was then transported to the Southern District of New York, where the government obtained a warrant to search its entire contents. The seizure occurred on the same day the FBI raided the home and office of former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani. The warrants, applications, affidavits, and related materials remain under seal to this day, and Toensing has never been told the reasons for the searches. Toensing is a lawyer and legal commentator, a former federal prosecutor and Deputy Assistant Attorney General, and former Chief Counsel of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence. To her knowledge, she has never been the target of an investigation. She has never been charged with any crime. | | | | | |
Peter,
I’ll be honest with you... I’m not great at asking for money. It’s the part of this job I hate the most.
I didn’t spend my twenties learning how to fundraise to run for office. I spent them flying H-46 helicopters for the Navy and deploying to the Persian Gulf.
And when I came home, I didn’t become a lobbyist who took clients out to expensive dinners. I used my GI Bill to become a Geriatric Nurse Practitioner. My "networking" was holding the hands of our seniors and listening to their stories, not cutting backroom deals.
That’s really who I am...a Helicopter Pilot...a Nurse Practitioner... and a Mom trying to raise four happy and healthy kids in a world that feels like it’s going in the wrong direction most days.
[I didn't run for Congress for the title. I ran because I looked at the country my children were inheriting, and I felt sick to my stomach. I couldn't just sit there.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDgwN19WNy1STy4xMTAxMTdfdDE5ODM0NDQtMjA2OCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA4MDdfVjctUk8uMTEwMTE3X3QxOTgzNDQ0LTIwNjgifQ/jGhPPNNwMFGmv49KggfMEA)
But here is the hard truth: fighting the radical Left and standing up for our values is incredibly expensive. I don’t have a massive machine behind me. I don’t have someone who can write blank checks on a whim.
[I just have normal folks like you.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDgwN19WNy1STy4xMTAxMTdfdDE5ODM0NDQtMjA2OCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA4MDdfVjctUk8uMTEwMTE3X3QxOTgzNDQ0LTIwNjgifQ/Tdpl_axnz45hkodvm5fu8Q)
I know things are tight right now. I see it at the grocery store just like you do. But if you can spare even $5 to help keep a Navy Vet and a Nurse Practitioner in this fight, it would mean the world to me.

clean_body: Not what I spent my time doing | | | | | | Peter, I’ll be honest with you... I’m not great at asking for money. It’s the part of this job I hate the most. I didn’t spend my twenties learning how to fundraise to run for office. I spent them flying H-46 helicopters for the Navy and deploying to the Persian Gulf. And when I came home, I didn’t become a lobbyist who took clients out to expensive dinners. I used my GI Bill to become a Geriatric Nurse Practitioner. My "networking" was holding the hands of our seniors and listening to their stories, not cutting backroom deals. That’s really who I am...a Helicopter Pilot...a Nurse Practitioner... and a Mom trying to raise four happy and healthy kids in a world that feels like it’s going in the wrong direction most days. But here is the hard truth: fighting the radical Left and standing up for our values is incredibly expensive. I don’t have a massive machine behind me. I don’t have someone who can write blank checks on a whim. I know things are tight right now. I see it at the grocery store just like you do.
