Towards the end of last night's KCDP Election Night watch party, I was chatting with one of Knox County's most dedicated canvassers. He, like I, had been door knocking until the last minute, trying to get every possible voter to the polls.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/0d313962-7ab6-47fe-93cb-40c16eebe190?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
KCDP Watch Party. Photo credit: Emery Ball
He told me that at one door, the man shared that he had voted just two hours earlier. Some canvassers might just thank them and move on, but he knew there was more to this door. The voter shared that he didn't like his options on the Republican side, both in the primary and for the local general, but he had voted for them anyway.
**They talked for several more minutes about the candidates and what they stand for, at which point the voter shared, "If you had been here two hours earlier, I would have voted differently."**
The conversation didn't end there - they talked about the November election, and Tim Burchett, and Marsha Blackburn. My friend shared that as a result of this conversation, that voter plans to cast votes in the general for me and Jerri Green.
We're Democrats in East Tennessee. We know we're the underdogs.
But we do this work because we believe in what's possible for our community.
Well-funded public schools to educate the next generation.
Healthcare we can afford.
For our young people to not have to move away to find opportunity.
Equal protection for **all** East Tennesseans under the law.
A government that serves **us** , not corporate interests.
**We can 't expect voters to come to us - we have to go to them. To talk to them about what's making their life harder, and how we can come together to solve the problems we can't fix by ourselves.**
That's why I'm doing 100 days of door knocking leading up to the November 3rd election (today is day 13 - you can follow along on social media or [YouTube](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/6a6d350c-8349-4015-a28c-ba512273b757?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)).
And that's what our local candidates did, from Blount county to Claiborne, leading up to yesterday's elections. I am so, so proud of my fellow East Tennesseans who stepped up to run, knowing the personal sacrifice it requires and the amount of work it demands.
And that work paid off, and also showed us where we have more work to do until November and beyond.
In Blount, Terri Klozik lost by just 16 votes for County Commission. Sixteen votes. (Don't let anyone tell you that your vote doesn't matter, and that volunteering for a Democrat in East Tennessee won't make a difference).
Across our district, turnout was up 64%, and our rural supporters showed up like never before.
In Jefferson and Loudon counties, Democratic turnout was up more than 80%.
In Grainger County, I received more than DOUBLE the votes of the 2022 Democratic nominee.
In Knox county, Democrats flipped a county commission seat. We held on to a competitive school board seat. _**And we flipped a school board seat, which flipped the school board!**_
The Republican nominee with an entire MAGA machine behind her barely squeaked out a victory for the mayor's race.
There's something else I'm taking away from the Knox county mayor's race: the margin wasn't determined by party members turning out to cast their ballot for their party's nominee. It wasn't just Republicans voting red and Democrats voting blue.
And in that race, about 2,000 Republicans and Independents voted for the Democratic candidate but didn't vote for other Democrats down ballot. While I wish they had, you know what that means?
**There 's a not-insignificant portion of voters willing to reject polarizing, partisan, culture-war candidates. Sounds a lot like the incumbent I'm running against.**
That's why it was no surprise to find out that more than 18,000 Republicans who voted in this election did NOT vote for Tim.
We have 87 days until midterms. We've spent the last ten months building the infrastructure for this movement, and we're ready for exponential growth to get our message out: **Congress isn 't working for us, but it **_**should**_**.** And Michaela Barnett is the person to make it happen.
I'll be door knocking every single day until November 3rd. Join me? [Sign up](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/ae3431bd-036b-45ad-aeb5-8182ca6b2e7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to volunteer to speak with your East Tennessee neighbors through door knocking, phone banking, text banking, post carding, and more.

Peter,
Greg Abbott relies on a handful of mega-donors writing half-a-million-dollar checks just to keep him in power.
But not us. **Our campaign relies on hardworking people who’ve supported this campaign from the start and believe in Gina’s vision for a better Texas.**
Since Gina launched her campaign, we’ve built our movement across Texas — from the Panhandle down to the Rio Grande Valley, and all the small towns and big cities in between.
Normally, when we reach out, we ask for $2.54 — a single penny for every county in Texas that Greg Abbott has ignored.
**But today we have a different request — we’re asking 254 people from 18326 to chip in $1 today, so we can keep our organizers on the ground across the state.**
**[If you’re ready to help us reach Texans across this huge state, will you be one of the 254 people from 18326 who pitch in just $1 right now?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1992?c0=em_ms_gh_20260807_3_1ask.uaRs_K&refcode=em20260807-1780&t=1&akid=1780%2E299639%2EazLv8l)**

A 2001 ruling from the U.S. Supreme Court has allowed thousands of illegal aliens to be released into American communities without proper vetting. According to Zadvydas v. Davis, most unauthorized foreigners are required to be discharged from detention centers after six months if no country has accepted them for deportation.

On Thursday, U.S. Sen. Katie Britt (R-Montgomery) led the introduction of the Keep Our Communities Safe Act of 2026, a bill designed to address the issue.

"America is a nation of laws, and if you violate our laws and are subject to removal from the United States, you should remain in detention until the point of deportation,” said Britt. "Zadvydas v. Davis created a legal loophole that forces the release of aliens into our communities after six months simply because no country has agreed to take them back."

U.S. Senators Katie Britt and Tommy Tuberville, both R-Alabama, are introducing legislation that would tie the postmaster general’s performance bonuses to the U.S. Postal Service’s delivery and financial results.

The Postal Executive Responsibility, Fiscal Oversight, and Results-based Management Act, known as the PERFORM Act, would prohibit the postmaster general from receiving a performance-based bonus if the Postal Service failed to meet key operational or financial benchmarks during the previous fiscal year.

I have good news and bad news. I am going to start with the good, because I think you deserve to hear it. **July was the strongest grassroots fundraising month of this entire campaign.** While Sabato's Crystal Ball was moving 14 races toward Democrats. While James Talarico's billionaire backers were writing $10 million checks. While the national environment was shifting against Republicans at every turn, Texas conservatives showed up in a way that I will never forget. You gave more in July than in any month since this campaign began. Not because a single mega-donor wrote a massive check. Because thousands of grassroots conservatives across this state and this country decided that Texas was worth fighting for. That is the good news. And it is genuinely great news. **Now here is the bad news.** **Fox News just released a new poll showing James Talarico leading me 51% to 48%. This is Fox News. Not a Democratic pollster. Not a liberal outlet._Fox News_. And their poll shows Talarico over 50% for the first time in this race.** Here is what the numbers show. Talarico has 98% of Democrats. He has 68% of independents. And 24% of non-MAGA Republicans are supporting him. That last number is the one that concerns me most. Nearly one in four Republicans who did not back President Trump is currently planning to vote for a Democrat who believes God is nonbinary, calls the American flag a complicated symbol, and wants a welcome mat at the southern border. **_I am not going to sugarcoat this. These numbers are serious._** But here is what I know. The margin of error on the Fox News poll is plus or minus 3 points. This race is not over. Among undecided voters, more lean toward me than toward Talarico. And the grassroots momentum we built in July proves that when conservatives show up, we can compete. clean_body: I have good news and bad news... I have good news and bad news... | | | | | | | Peter, I have good news and bad news. I am going to start with the good, because I think you deserve to hear it. July was the strongest grassroots fundraising month of this entire campaign. While Sabato's Crystal Ball was moving 14 races toward Democrats. While James Talarico's billionaire backers were writing $10 million checks. While the national environment was shifting against Republicans at every turn, Texas conservatives showed up in a way that I will never forget. You gave more in July than in any month since this campaign began. Not because a single mega-donor wrote a massive check. Because thousands of grassroots conservatives across this state and this country decided that Texas was worth fighting for. That is the good news. And it is genuinely great news. Now here is the bad news. Fox News just released a new poll showing James Talarico leading me 51% to 48%. This is Fox News. Not a Democratic pollster. Not a liberal outlet.Fox News. And their poll shows Talarico over 50% for the first time in this race. Here is what the numbers show. Talarico has 98% of Democrats. He has 68% of independents. And 24% of non-MAGA Republicans are supporting him. That last number is the one that concerns me most. Nearly one in four Republicans who did not back President Trump is currently planning to vote for a Democrat who believes God is nonbinary, calls the American flag a complicated symbol, and wants a welcome mat at the southern border. I am not going to sugarcoat this. These numbers are serious. But here is what I know. The margin of error on the Fox News poll is plus or minus 3 points. This race is not over. Among undecided voters, more lean toward me than toward Talarico. And the grassroots momentum we built in July proves that when conservatives show up, we can compete. The question is whether we can keep that momentum going into August... James Talarico has raised $70 million. He has the national media telling the story he wants told. What I have is you, and the strongest grassroots month this campaign has ever seen. Let us make August even stronger. Thank you, Ken Paxton P.S. -- Fox News showed Talarico at 51%. Peter, Americans are struggling to pay for housing and health care, groceries and gas. And even when we participate in the system that’s _supposed_ to solve these problems for us, little changes. **That’s because voting for candidates with good policy isn’t enough when the system itself is broken.** In a time when our Supreme Court and government have been captured by dark money and wealthy interests, the only real solution _is to change the system._ For months, we have been demanding to hear a plan from politicians. It’s important to get them on the record _before_ voters head to the polls. **We need more than vague promises. We must push politicians to commit to the structural reforms that will lead to real change. Our**** _Future on Record Tour_****is doing just that. We’re documenting where political leaders stand and helping elevate a question that too often goes unanswered:****If the current political system repeatedly prevents government from acting on the issues Americans care about most, what will our leaders do to change the system itself?** **[Rep. Ro Khanna was just in Pennsylvania, and he gave a full, substantive answer. Watch what he has to say, and then chip in to help hold our electeds accountable for real change?](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqsGaD5Q6vfHCa40eon2HvvuRtIy1QzvLTl4JVcv-DVvo0r074tprzGq0Riu4E-8juBeehRW743Od3JZY-zN6Ox_gT0zFQxpZgFW3SFGG4ilu3BCCq8c6KQa_MNNUJpfLnlxuRaXcPeTSbC7OBXDCUF7N0mwR5S1uQiWwUuB96qavTQJ2Q3_FecoGaEH2T6lZFuDEEpIKBfTgF6GTn4eg88ssEbiE-GJ5jyXqdL3m7xkre6TCL-E6a0kw8mpR6SL6_vlT2RkLa_zj4EDy-0od8bIitfD_mseP9FBiOaRYmIGhlF0XnIgFPq49wcg8eOmP2N_HxlORDfKoqkZ5Zo_KwVoPlx860jvL0KOpgSwvZtZ3GRwHH2YUP0Qjl_vHFSrhgy91zbF_bA9ORnzFYIJJLzm/4sz/WELe8QSfQhqdU6-pYDluOw/h0/h001.q5Mp0NR8vyMEUfBjkQRx_gMkV1KVLJZpSYwy0Xnkx7o)** [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqsGaD5Q6vfHCa40eon2HvvuRtIy1QzvLTl4JVcv-DVvo0r074tprzGq0Riu4E-8juAF22Pd0M0qx6EZW26ll11N0wQnJmHdwDpilBd_feqlbi828-P_VxnEKMg8r2qj8bBpJf-ZVzpgV_KoGnb8VMhFeAuY077E36RCsTGuG6bqMlka4eGx__AumFh9ziKVIXkE8PVY33AS2-_keFFnA_KQtcEbYW0Eu6sgc53vvs2vZGxW6us0TNl1_0KruR-yufsfGAJomrnmkP1YYe05NTsw2B9xy2orxD7rj1YDDrsfcX4oWgMMZ0uUBVeufJmJRZfUYeH9aSOdci6WDlDPRMscotsw37p3LG65w2wA02v319I_mcMmMVMl-nlovG5snq2uC0wWuRUQK2qK0WWjVLzt/4sz/WELe8QSfQhqdU6-pYDluOw/h1/h001.PfnQ6hWyLeU1Lqg3C9lcS6dcZx5lOjWm5yVTjeVPW4w)Let’s face it: if dark money continues to run the show, even good ideas with broad support won’t get anywhere because the system itself is rigged. Our _Future on Record Tour_ demands that candidates answer voters’ most important question: _“If the current political system prevents government from acting on the issues Americans care about most, what will_** _you_** _do to change it?”_ **Or to put it even more bluntly, “**** _Which side are you on? As fun as it sounds, there’s more to it. When you chip in $5 – about the price of a happy hour beer – it sets us up to keep this seat blue and reach voters. Let me explain.
Long before I ever walked into the world of politics, I was pouring my energy into the Wynkoop, Colorado's first brewpub. Our flagship brews were Timberline Pale Ale and Sagebrush Stout (with just the faintest hint of a prairie bouquet). We sold them for just $2.25 a pint — 50 cents less than a pint of an import.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136834283/638742638/-1114402239?amounts=5,10,15,25,50,100&amount=5&refcode=email_080726_beerday-RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZDZlODQ5MS1hZjkyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=-1o28Vfhj8GO5-IN4bFj40oqNKoDJxWSahyt6aJ8gDI=)
Wynkoop was more than just a business venture for me. It was about creating a gathering place for people of all backgrounds and opinions. I truly believed there wasn't a single problem that couldn't be sorted out over a pint of fresh beer.
I didn’t run for office for fame, money, or power. I ran partly because I didn’t want to have a boss. But the main reason: I wanted to bring people together to solve problems. And that’s exactly what we’ve done.
I ran for the Senate on that same idea — to get things done.
We’ve invested billions to confront the climate crisis, lowered prescription drug costs, and made investments to rebuild our infrastructure. We’ve brought thousands of good-paying manufacturing jobs back to America, and worked to make housing more affordable. _And we’re not done yet._
**But look, National Republicans are throwing everything they’ve got at us. They’re determined to flip this seat back to red and roll back the progress we’ve worked so hard for. We’re going to need all the help we can get to keep Colorado blue and keep serving folks like you.**
**_[So in honor of International Beer Day, we’re asking you to contribute $5 — _about the price of two pints at Wynkoop back in the day!_ — to help our team defend this must-hold seat and take back the Senate.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136834284/638742639/-1114402239?amounts=5,10,15,25,50,100&amount=5&refcode=email_080726_beerday-RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZDZlODQ5MS1hZjkyLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=-1o28Vfhj8GO5-IN4bFj40oqNKoDJxWSahyt6aJ8gDI=)_**

body:
Clearing the Path for Independents

| | | [ ](www.forwardparty.com)
---
###
### Peter —
Last week we told you that Idaho’s math changed in favor of Senate candidate Todd Achilles. This week, it happened again with South Dakota’s Democratic Senate Nominee Julian Beaudion dropping out of the race, leaving a clear one-on-one race between independent Senate candidate Brian Bengs and Republican candidate Mike Rounds. The move from Beaudion verifies the direction more voters are heading, which is preferring independent leadership over partisan picks. It leaves Bengs as the main competitor against Rounds, mirroring last week's development in Idaho. These are the first dominoes to fall in states where Democratic nominees are unlikely to win and have historically served only to split the non-Republican vote and hand incumbents an easy victory. Legacy party nominees are beginning to recognize the overwhelming support for a new kind of leadership in these states and are stepping aside, ultimately clearing a path for independent candidates who can compete. **At the center of this South Dakota shift is Brian Bengs, Independent Senate Candidate.** He is a _dual-service military veteran, attorney, former criminal justice professor at Northern State University, and National Park Ranger._ He served in the United States Navy and then as a Lieutenant Colonel in the United States Air Force, where he spent years as a JAG officer. He has been an independent for, in his own words, _"97% of my adult life."_**** We previously noted that Bengs submitted the highest-validity petition of any statewide South Dakota candidate in 2026, which was 93.85% validity, beating both major party candidates in the quality of signatures gathered. This decision by a major party nominee to drop out is becoming an emerging pattern in one-party-rule states, with similar developments possible in additional districts and states. With under 100 days to go until midterms, this election cycle is seeing independent thinking taking root. Our strategy at Forward has always been about math. You don't need 51 independent senators to change the United States Senate. You need enough to hold the balance of power: three or four members who answer only to their constituents, who can't be controlled by either party, and who will vote on the merits of what's in front of them. That math is now closer to real than it has ever been. **The Forward Party endorses[Brian Bengs](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=AOXa9YXuTRM2xxte2I3Ke9Mxrj2b-bw7G3sCLeNVDp8&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_111a&n=1) in South Dakota and [Todd Achilles](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=gDz98NJdqG1BxZ1yWkkZaabbmu8XvNqRStzyElUXI6CRKJam8hXhW5AoLQvAn5i-&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_111a&n=2) in Idaho.** We believe these candidates, and all Forward-endorsed candidates, represent the clearest path to showing that independents can win in the most difficult electoral environments in the country and that when they do, American politics changes. |
## **Primary Highlight**
### **Niina Baum**
**Republican Candidate for Wisconsin's 7th Congressional District**
---
****
This Tuesday (August 11) is primary day in Wisconsin, where [Niina Baum](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=cJRL0nJ0Y3OPu36SMj-8u7ArYZBuKn-66WNNBpxWnZM&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_111a&n=3) is competing for the Republican nomination in the 7th Congressional District. Regardless of party label, her campaign represents the kind of candidate Forward is committed to supporting: someone who cares deeply about the voters they are pledging to represent and who is willing to fight for them while putting effective representation ahead of partisan politics.
Niina grew up on a dairy farm in northern Wisconsin and is now running to represent the same rural communities that shaped her. She co-founded Northwoods Young Professionals to help keep young talent in rural Wisconsin, organized community events that generated more than $500,000 in economic impact, helped establish the Hodag Snack Attack program to provide food for local elementary school students, and currently serves on the Rhinelander Rotary Club Board and as Planning Commissioner for the Town of Crescent.
Baum's campaign reflects many of the qualities the Forward Party looks for in endorsed candidates: a record of community service, independence, and a focus on representing constituents over partisan interests.

clean_body: Clearing the Path for Independents | | | www.forwardparty.com Peter — Last week we told you that Idaho’s math changed in favor of Senate candidate Todd Achilles. This week, it happened again with South Dakota’s Democratic Senate Nominee Julian Beaudion dropping out of the race, leaving a clear one-on-one race between independent Senate candidate Brian Bengs and Republican candidate Mike Rounds. The move from Beaudion verifies the direction more voters are heading, which is preferring independent leadership over partisan picks. It leaves Bengs as the main competitor against Rounds, mirroring last week's development in Idaho. These are the first dominoes to fall in states where Democratic nominees are unlikely to win and have historically served only to split the non-Republican vote and hand incumbents an easy victory. Legacy party nominees are beginning to recognize the overwhelming support for a new kind of leadership in these states and are stepping aside, ultimately clearing a path for independent candidates who can compete. At the center of this South Dakota shift is Brian Bengs, Independent Senate Candidate. He is a dual-service military veteran, attorney, former criminal justice professor at Northern State University, and National Park Ranger. He served in the United States Navy and then as a Lieutenant Colonel in the United States Air Force, where he spent years as a JAG officer. He has been an independent for, in his own words, "97% of my adult life."** We previously noted that Bengs submitted the highest-validity petition of any statewide South Dakota candidate in 2026, which was 93.85% validity, beating both major party candidates in the quality of signatures gathered. This decision by a major party nominee to drop out is becoming an emerging pattern in one-party-rule states, with similar developments possible in additional districts and states. With under 100 days to go until midterms, this election cycle is seeing independent thinking taking root. Our strategy at Forward has always been about math. You don't need 51 independent senators to change the United States Senate. You need enough to hold the balance of power: three or four members who answer only to their constituents, who can't be controlled by either party, and who will vote on the merits of what's in front of them. That math is now closer to real than it has ever been. The Forward Party endorses in South Dakota and in Idaho. We believe these candidates, and all Forward-endorsed candidates, represent the clearest path to showing that independents can win in the most difficult electoral environments in the country and that when they do, American politics changes. | Primary Highlight Niina Baum Republican Candidate for Wisconsin's 7th Congressional District This Tuesday (August 11) is primary day in Wisconsin, where is competing for the Republican nomination in the 7th Congressional District. Regardless of party label, her campaign represents the kind of candidate Forward is committed to supporting: someone who cares deeply about the voters they are pledging to represent and who is willing to fight for them while putting effective representation ahead of partisan politics. Niina grew up on a dairy farm in northern Wisconsin and is now running to represent the same rural communities that shaped her. She co-founded Northwoods Young Professionals to help keep young talent in rural Wisconsin, organized community events that generated more than $500,000 in economic impact, helped establish the Hodag Snack Attack program to provide food for local elementary school students, and currently serves on the Rhinelander Rotary Club Board and as Planning Commissioner for the Town of Crescent. Baum's campaign reflects many of the qualities the Forward Party looks for in endorsed candidates: a record of community service, independence, and a focus on representing constituents over partisan interests. If you missed it last week, we had Todd Achilles (Idaho) on a brand new podcast episode with Bob Chew (Colorado)! They talk with our hosts about what drew them to the Forward Party, why they are running, and what a few good Forwardists in the Senate means for the country. We all know that Donald Trump and Congressional Republicans are using their government offices to enrich themselves and their donors.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3654%2E21716%2EcF19xX)
We all know that Donald Trump and Congressional Republicans are using their government offices to enrich themselves and their donors.
Trump raked in $1.4 billion in crypto profits while the people who bought his coins lost money, and there have been way too many members of Congress who have been getting rich off of suspiciously timed stock trades.
**We need to ban members of Congress and the administration from trading individual stocks.**
But as long as Republicans remain in power, their corruption will remain unchecked. They’re even trying to pass a bill they’ve called the “Stop Insider Trading Act” that _still allows members of Congress to own and sell stocks_ , and exempts the president from the ban on buying stocks.
That’s just one more reason we need to flip the House this November — so we can put a stop to the political games and pass real reforms to combat corruption.
I’m working hard to keep Delaware’s House seat blue and support Democrats in swing districts across the country in this November’s midterm elections, but I need your help. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. Brandon Gill and at 29 years old, I decided to run for Congress where I became the youngest House Republican. You could say I prefer the simple things in life. I grew up on a cattle ranch and television isn’t my pastime. Being a husband and a father are the two most important things in my life. Sometimes, when I'm holding my kids I feel like I'm holding the whole world in my arms. They are the wind in my sails when it comes to the mission I’ve committed my life & career to. And at the end of my life, I want to sit before the Father almighty and declare that I did all I could to leave this great country better off than it was when I grew up. The left hates you, they hate your vote, and they hate MAGA for putting America First. Peter, today, I’ll make the same promise to you that I’ve made to myself, to my wife, and to my children. As long as I live, I will continue to FIGHT to preserve the soul of our country. No force on Earth will push me to abandon my mission and calling. Believe me, I’m not someone who finds it easy to ask for support. Texting you like this is the last thing I thought I’d have to do. But the country we love is on the brink of destruction & God has put it on my heart to fight with all that I have. This is more than a polite request. This is now a final plea for your support. Sincerely, Congressman Brandon Gill(R) TX-26 | | | Paid for by Brandon Gill for Texas | | PO BOX 827 Arlington, VA 22216 Click here to_

Folks, it’s James Carville.
I’ve spent nearly half a century helping Democrats win elections, and I’m gonna tell you something plainly:
For too long, we have waited until the house was already on fire before deciding to buy a hose.
We wait until a race becomes a crisis.
We wait until a great candidate is getting buried in attack ads.
We wait until Republicans have already built the infrastructure, raised the money, and defined the battlefield.
Then everybody starts running around asking what happened.
Well, Raja Krishnamoorthi has gone and done something about it.
He founded Equal Opportunity Now [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email] to find and support bold leaders and important causes before it’s too late — leaders who will stand up to Donald Trump and the MAGA movement, fight for working families, and actually deliver results.
And all I can say is:
FINALLY.
Finally, an organization that understands we cannot defeat MAGA with timid candidates, stale talking points, and a last-minute panic.
But Raja cannot build this by himself.
Will you contribute $25, $50, or whatever you can today to help Equal Opportunity Now find, fund, and support the leaders Democrats need to start winning again? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
SUPPORT EQUAL OPPORTUNITY NOW! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
Now, I know Raja.
He is smart. He is tough. And he knows firsthand what opportunity can mean.
His family came to this country with very little. They relied on public housing and food stamps. He worked his way from Peoria all the way to Congress.
And instead of pulling the ladder up behind him, Raja has spent his career fighting to make sure the next family gets the same shot.
That means standing up for workers.
Holding powerful corporations and corrupt politicians accountable.
Defending immigrants, voting rights, and every American targeted by Trump’s politics of division.
And now he is putting that experience toward building the next generation of Democratic leadership.
Here’s the truth: The leaders we need are already out there.
They are running for city council, state legislature, Congress, and offices most national donors are not paying attention to yet.
They have the courage.
They have the ideas.
What they do not always have is the money, infrastructure, and early support necessary to compete.
That is where Equal Opportunity Now comes in.
Please chip in $25, $50, or whatever you can today to help Raja build the organization Democrats should have built years ago. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
HELP DEMOCRATS WIN: DONATE TODAY! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
We’ve got a good battle plan, now, let’s help Raja build this damn thing.
-- James Carville

Peter, I’m here in Golden Gate Park at Outside Lands - listening to music, dancing with tens of thousands of San Franciscans and visitors from all over the world. Are you here?

**I love music and I know how important it is to the culture of our city. That's why I’ve spent my time in public service turning up the volume on live music in San Francisco.**

I made it easier to get permits for live music and DJs. I created new entertainment zones that support street fairs, nightlife and local businesses. I fought to provide relief for independent music venues and expanded opportunities for outdoor festivals and concerts.

My opponent can't say the same. She was the only vote against free live music in Civic Center, Union Square, and the Embarcadero.

10 commandments in schools + the TX coordinated campaign

| | | [ ](https://www.tanyafortexas.com/r?u=uGD1_JWQzocUoO6G1sZMF-tYIAuKQ97Z_lDiPedGAn11JJNENg30eeUPXVkqayxCfDLIkkjdPcC_U3XuHRoCIwMELeQenzQ2oHmoOYJU340&e=e318ce027ee4de3e55dda42c4424aaf7&utm_source=tanyafortexas&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=how_do_i_explain_adultery_to_a&n=1)
---
This is the first full year that Texas will require teachers to **post the** **10 Commandments in our classrooms.** As a teacher, I have so many questions for the MAGA Republicans who decided to pass this law. _Have they ever read the 10 Commandments?_ Because they’re not acting like it. _How do they expect me to explain what adultery means to an elementary school kid?_ Because I’ve got no idea. _What happened to the separation of church and state?_ Because I remember learning that from the Constitution they claim to follow. The Republican party in our county **spent money to donate the commandments to our school.** All while parents are not sure how they are going to afford school lunches or their health insurance after MAGA eliminated the ACA subsidies. Can you pitch in to send a teacher to Congress who believes our schools should focus on learning, not indoctrination.

body:

Peter,
As one of the most engaged supporters of my U.S. Senate campaign in North Carolina, your involvement has had a real impact on our ability to stay competitive in this fight. Thank you.
I hope you know how grateful I am for your time and attention – [**_and today, I’m asking you to take the next step with your first contribution of $5._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk991&amount=5&t=9&akid=2552%2E124072%2E3U8ylU) Here’s why:
Experts say Senate control will be decided in North Carolina, so between now and November, keeping up our momentum day by day is key to our success.
**However, grassroots donations fell off significantly after our July end-of-month deadline, and my finance team has had to make the tough decision to lower our projection for August.**
That’s a big problem when recent polling shows that my lead has tightened to just 4 points and when the Senate GOP’s top super PAC has gone live with false attack ads against me.
If we have to make the massive budget cuts we’re currently deliberating, we’ll put our chances of flipping this seat at risk.
[**_So Peter, I’m asking you to chip in and help us make today our biggest fundraising day of the month yet so we can turn things around. I’d be grateful for your $5 or anything you can spare.
